  same on every way in. A call keeps stack addresses, the registers the
  prototype model preserves and, when the callee calls nothing, the registers
  the callee does not write. The entry's parameters seed the walk, a typed
  pointer passed to a function seeds that function's parameter, and a typed
  pointer a function returns on every path is what its callers receive. The
  walk repeats, at most four times, until nothing more is learned. What it
  reads:

  - A typed pointer stored into a writable global types the global and names
    it as EDK2 does: `gImageHandle`, `gST`, `gBS`, `gRT`, `gDS`, `gSmst`,
    `gMmst`, and `m<Interface>` for a protocol pointer. A global two different
    types are stored into gets neither.
  - `LocateProtocol`, `HandleProtocol`, `OpenProtocol`, `SmmLocateProtocol` /
    `MmLocateProtocol` and `LocatePpi` take a GUID. When the GUID has an
    interface struct, the global or stack slot the interface out-parameter
    addresses holds a pointer to it, and that one call gets a prototype whose
    out-parameter is `INTERFACE **`
    (`crates/unlace-lift/src/p2_lift/callsiteproto.rs (parked)`:
    a prototype parked by call-instruction address, installed as the call's
    prototype override when `FlowInfo` builds the call, unless the function
    already carries an override there).
  - Every other call the walk reads through a table or interface member
    (`gBS->CreateEvent`, `This->ReadDisk`) gets the member's prototype the
    same way. The decompiler would otherwise learn the prototype only when
    type propagation reaches the pointer the call goes through, which is too
    late to place the arguments, so it analyzes the whole function a second
    time; with the prototype there when the call is built it analyzes the
    function once, and an argument that is a function address is a function
    from the start. It is also the only source for a PEIM that reads the table
    pointer inline, which leaves the decompiler no typed pointer to read the
    member from. A jump through a member (a tail call) states nothing, and a
    call the walk cannot follow to its table (its pointer comes from a heap
    record, or the block is only reached through a jump table) is still
    resolved by the decompiler, at the cost of the second analysis.
  - `InstallProtocolInterface`, `InstallMultipleProtocolInterfaces` (its
    GUID/interface pairs up to the NULL), the MM installs and `InstallPpi` /
    `ReInstallPpi` name an interface instance. The instance is typed with the
    interface struct and named `g<Interface>`, and each function it points at
    is named `<Interface><Member>` with the member's prototype, so a driver's
    `DriverBindingSupported(EFI_DRIVER_BINDING_PROTOCOL *This, EFI_HANDLE
    ControllerHandle, ...)` is recovered from its binding instance. A PPI list
    is walked descriptor by descriptor to the entry flagged
    `EFI_PEI_PPI_DESCRIPTOR_TERMINATE_LIST`, each one typed
    `EFI_PEI_PPI_DESCRIPTOR`; `NotifyPpi` does the same with
    `EFI_PEI_NOTIFY_DESCRIPTOR` and gives each callback the notify prototype
    with its PPI typed from the GUID.
  - `SmmRegisterProtocolNotify` / `MmRegisterProtocolNotify` register an
    `EFI_MM_NOTIFY_FN` the MM core calls once an interface is installed under
    the GUID. A constant callback is named `<Guid>Notify` (the GUID's EDK2
    name without its `g` and `Guid`, `Protocol_<Data1>` for an unknown one)
    and given the prototype `EFI_STATUS(EFI_GUID *Protocol, <Interface> *Interface,
    EFI_HANDLE Handle)`, so the interface the callback receives is typed from
    the GUID like a `LocateProtocol` out-parameter and the walk follows it into
    the callback. The boot-services `RegisterProtocolNotify` takes an event,
    not a function, and is left alone.
  - A member whose prototype has an out-parameter `T **` for a known `T`
    (`EFI_SMM_BASE2_PROTOCOL.GetSmstLocation`) types what it is handed, which is
    how an SMM driver's `gSmst` is found.

  The interface structs come from
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/uefi/protocols.txt`, generated
  by `scripts/gen_uefi_protocols.py` from the EDK2 `MdePkg` and `MdeModulePkg`
  headers (edk2-stable202505, BSD-2-Clause-Patent): 371 protocol and PPI GUIDs
  with the layout of their interface, plus `EFI_MM_SYSTEM_TABLE` and
  `EFI_SMM_SYSTEM_TABLE2`. A member the generator cannot lay out exactly (a
  union, a bit-field, a packed or unknown by-value type) ends its struct, so
  every offset in the table is the header's. A struct is built in the type
  factory the first time something names it
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/uefi/types.rs (EfiTypes)`),
  so an image pays for the interfaces it uses; a `This` parameter is a pointer
  to its own interface. An interface installed under a GUID the table has no
  struct for gets one synthesized from the instance: one member per pointer
  slot up to the last slot that points at a function start, `Function_<off>`
  for those and `Field_<off>` for the others, named from the GUID
  (`gEdkiiFooProtocolGuid` gives `EDKII_FOO_PROTOCOL`, an unknown GUID
  `PROTOCOL_<Data1>`).

  The phase decides the entry prototype. A module whose service calls go
  through `EFI_PEI_SERVICES` is a PEIM, entered as `EFI_STATUS
  _ModuleEntryPoint(VOID *FileHandle, EFI_PEI_SERVICES **PeiServices)`; a
  standalone-MM module is entered with `EFI_MM_SYSTEM_TABLE *MmSystemTable`.
  Without other evidence the walk reads the module as a DXE module first and
  as the other two only when that resolves no service call. Two EDK2 library
  shapes are recognized in a PEIM because every service call goes through
  them: a function that reads the IDT register (`sidt`) and loads the pointer
  below the IDT base is `GetPeiServicesTablePointer`, returning
  `EFI_PEI_SERVICES **` (the X64 and IA32 counterpart of the ARM getters
  above), and a short function that only forwards its own parameters to one
  PEI service is named `PeiServices<Service>` and treated as that service at
  its call sites. On 32-bit ARM (PE machine `ARM`,
  `THUMB` or `ARMNT`) a code pointer's low bit selects Thumb and is not part
  of the address, for the entry point as for an interface member.

  Across the modules of one firmware volume, `unlace unpack <firmware>` writes
  `unlace-uefi.index` beside the modules
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/uefi/index.rs (Index)`): each
  module's FFS file type and, with `--protocols`, every interface instance
  each module installs, read off one load of the module (the pass leaves them
  on the architecture as
  `crates/unlace-middle/src/p0_knowledge/uefiprotocols.rs (InstalledInterface)`).
  A module loaded from
  that directory takes its phase from its file type (PEIM, PEI core and
  combined PEIM/driver are PEI; MM standalone and MM core standalone are MM;
  a traditional SMM driver is entered as a DXE driver), with option `uefientry on`
  its entry point is named `PeimEntryPoint` (a PEIM) or `StandaloneMmEntryPoint`
  (MM standalone) rather than `_ModuleEntryPoint`, takes the struct
  another module synthesized for a GUID, and gets a comment at each interface
  lookup naming the module that installs it, the instance address and the
  member functions: `gEfiPeiRscHandlerPpiGuid is installed by
  ReportStatusCodeRouterPei.efi (EFI_PEI_RSC_HANDLER_PPI at 0x829a90:
  Register=0x8297ff, Unregister=0x8298c8)`. The index is plain text, a line that does not parse
  is skipped and a file over 16 MiB is not read. The walk is static: an
  interface installed from a heap copy, or under a GUID computed at run time,
  is not seen.
- **(unlace) Cortex-M System Control Space** (`cortexmscs`, default on,
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/cortexmscs/mod.rs (CortexMScsPass)`):
  every ARMv7-M and ARMv8-M core maps the same registers at fixed addresses of
  the Private Peripheral Bus, so on a Cortex-M image they are declared as typed
  volatile globals: `SCB` at 0xE000ED00, `NVIC` at 0xE000E100, `SysTick` at
  0xE000E010, `SCnSCB`, `MPU`, `FPU`, `CoreDebug` (ARMv8-M: `DCB`, `DIB`, `SAU`),
  and `ITM`, `DWT`, `FPB`, `TPI` at 0xE0000000, 0xE0001000, 0xE0002000 and
  0xE0040000. An image is a Cortex-M one when its language is `ARM:*:32:Cortex`
  or `ARM:*:32:v8-m` (`layout`; what a raw dump probed from its vector table
  loads as), or when it is an ARM ELF whose `.ARM.attributes` state
  `Tag_CPU_arch_profile` `'M'`
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/loader/armfloatabi.rs (m_profile_arch)`;
  an ELF loads as `ARM:*:32:v8` whatever its core). The language, or
  `Tag_CPU_arch` (16, 17 and 21 are ARMv8-M), picks one of two layouts; ARMv6-M
  takes the ARMv7-M one, which it is a subset of. The layouts
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/cortexmscs/tables.rs`) are
  generated by `scripts/gen_cortexmscs.py` from the CMSIS-Core 5.9.0 headers
  `core_cm7.h` and `core_cm33.h`: each `#define NAME ((NAME_Type *) NAME_BASE)`
  block is laid out with natural alignment and checked against the header's
  offset comments, reserved members are dropped, an anonymous union is its
  first member, and the FPB, which CMSIS does not describe, is stated from the
  architecture manuals (`CTRL`, `REMAP`, `COMP[8]`). CMSIS structures overlap
  (`NVIC_Type` reaches `STIR` at 0xE000EF00, past the SCB; `SCB_Type` on a
  Cortex-M7 reaches the cache registers past the FPU), and two globals cannot,
  so the generator merges the registers by address: a block keeps its registers
  up to the next block's base, each register beyond that is a global of its own
  named `<Block>_<Register>` (`SCB_STIR`, `SCB_ICIALLU`), and a register two
  blocks name belongs to one. A global starts at its block's first register,
  not at a reserved word before it, so 0xE000E000 itself, which code compares
  masked addresses against, stays a number. A structure keeps its CMSIS name (`SCB_Type`)
  and member names, with `unsigned int` members except the byte arrays
  (`SCB.SHPR[12]`, `NVIC.IP[240]`). The pass, and the raw-image bootstrap
  (`crates/unlace-console/src/engine.rs (bootstrap_raw_image)`), which
  has no object file to run passes over, only state which layout applies; the
  commit builds the types (`materialize`), marks each block's range volatile and
  then maps the globals name- and type-locked, so with the option off neither a
  type nor a symbol exists. A block whose structure name is already held by a
  type of another shape is skipped. A `data` assertion at a block's address
  replaces the global, and one inside a block wins its own bytes; the CLI's
  `--svd` import puts the device name in front of a structure name the built-in
  layouts use (`STM32F103_SCB_Type`), so an SVD peripheral keeps the SVD's
  registers.
- **(unlace) COM ids and interfaces** (`com`, default on since unlace#581,
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/com/mod.rs (ComPass)`): on a PE
  image, every 16-byte value at 4-byte alignment in a data or code section
  (an i386 MSVC image merges `.rdata`, ids included, into `.text`) that equals
  a known interface or class id becomes a `GUID` (`Data1`, `Data2`, `Data3`,
  `Data4[8]`) named after it, with a numeric suffix on a repeat:
  `IID_IShellLinkW`, `CLSID_ShellLink`, `CLSID_WbemLocator`. For each interface id it
  finds, the pass builds the interface as COM lays it out
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/com/mod.rs (ComTypes)`): a struct
  named after the interface whose only member is `<Interface>Vtbl *lpVtbl`, and
  the table, one function pointer per method in slot order, the methods of the
  base interfaces first (`IUnknown`'s `QueryInterface`, `AddRef`, `Release`,
  then `IDispatch`'s four for a dual interface), each with `This` (a pointer
  to the interface) as its first parameter. A method whose parameters include
  a by-value aggregate (a `VARIANT`, a `POINT`, a `GUID`) keeps an untyped
  code pointer in its slot, so the table's offsets stay right without stating
  a prototype the pass cannot spell. A name the program already holds for a
  complete type of another size is left alone. The commit hands the engine the
  map from each id's address to its interface
  (`crates/unlace-bandb-base/src/p5_types/comtyping.rs (ComInterfaces)`),
  which types the out-parameter of a COM request by the id it passes (chapter
  05). The imported `ole32` requests (`CoCreateInstance`, `CoGetClassObject`,
  `CoGetObject`, `CoGetInterfaceAndReleaseStream`, `CoGetObjectContext`,
  `CoGetCallContext`, `OleCreate`, and the four that fill a `MULTI_QI` array:
  `CoCreateInstanceEx`, `CoCreateInstanceFromApp`,
  `CoGetInstanceFromIStorage`, `CoGetInstanceFromFile`) get their prototypes by import address,
  so the out-parameter is an argument at every call even where the call site
  alone would not place it (the fifth argument of `CoCreateInstance` on x86-64
  is on the stack). The pass builds types, so it runs at the analysis commit
  and only when the option is on
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/passes.rs (run_com)`); with it off no type,
  name or prototype exists. The tables are generated by
  `scripts/gen_com_tables.py` from the Win32 bindings of the `windows` crate
  (microsoft/windows-rs 0.62, MIT OR Apache-2.0), which are generated from the
  Windows metadata: `analyzers/com/interfaces.txt` holds 4401 interfaces, each
  with its base and the methods it adds, a letter per return and parameter
  type (`h` HRESULT, `u`/`i` 4-byte integers, `p` a pointer, `w` a wide
  string, `8` a by-value 64-bit integer, ...), and `analyzers/com/guids.txt`
  5239 ids, the interfaces' ids as `IID_<Interface>` and the coclasses'
  as `CLSID_<Class>`. The media, device and printing namespaces are left
  out. The model is IDA 9.5's `comhelper` plugin, which names a GUID from
  `clsid.cfg` and applies the `<Interface>Vtbl` type its type library holds.
  The option `comcfg`
  (`crates/unlace-middle/src/p0_knowledge/comcfg.rs (ComCfg)`, default
  `off`) names a file in that `clsid.cfg` format, one
  `guid {00000000-0000-0000-C000-000000000046} IUnknown` line per id and `;`
  starting a comment, read at the commit
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/com/mod.rs (parse_clsid_cfg)`, at
  most 64 MiB): each id the built-in table lacks is named after its line,
  spaces and other characters made `_`, and a bare name the interface table
  holds (`IShellLinkW`) is read as `IID_IShellLinkW`, so its interface is
  built like a built-in id's. An id both hold keeps the built-in name; a
  malformed line is skipped. IDA 9.5's own `clsid.cfg` holds 16,117 ids, 13,674
  of them not in the built-in table.
- **(unlace) Declared names** (`declaredlibcproto`,
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/protos/mod.rs (declared_libc_prototype)`,
  consulted from `crates/unlace-console/src/engine.rs (ConsoleProgram::declare_function)`):
  both passes above match a name the **image** carries — its FUNC symbols, its
  imports — which is exactly the evidence a stripped, statically linked target does
  not have. There the name exists only because an operator supplied it
  (`--define-function 0x8048968=ptrace`, `--assert 'function 0x8048968 ptrace'`,
  console `function bounds … as ptrace`), and a name that buys no prototype buys
  almost nothing: the callee's arity has to come from somewhere, and a varargs
  wrapper cannot yield it to any amount of body analysis, so the call sites keep
  rendering `ptrace()` with the pushed argument slots stranded as raw stores on the
  lines above. So a declared name is looked up in both tables at declaration time
  and the matching signature parked on the **declared entry address** — the key
  `ActionDefaultParams` reads a callee prototype back by, and the only key that
  survives two symbols sharing a spelling. The imports-only restriction the measured
  table carries is deliberately lifted here: it exists so a *coincidental* spelling
  cannot retype a function the image defines itself, which is a judgement about
  evidence, and the evidence is different once a human or an agent has identified
  the entry outright. The lookup runs after the declaration is registered and before
  any assertion is applied, so an explicit `--assert prototype` on the same function
  still wins. The base table carries `ptrace` for this reason: glibc *declares* it
  `long ptrace(enum __ptrace_request, …)` and fetches the rest with `va_arg`, so the
  four fixed slots — glibc's own, and the call form `ptrace(2)` documents — can only
  come from a table.
- **DWARF** (`dwarf`, the `DWARFAnalyzer` port,
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/mod.rs (DwarfPass)`), the
  parser wholesale-substituted by `gimli` (the same dependency-substitution loss as
  BFD → `object`). Compressed sections (`SHF_COMPRESSED` zlib/zstd and GNU
  `.zdebug_*`) are inflated by `object` before `gimli` reads them. Three
  recoveries: (1) names — each defined `DW_TAG_subprogram`
  emits a function symbol, each top-level `DW_TAG_variable` with a `DW_OP_addr`
  location a data symbol (the operand read in the file's byte order; a DWARF 5
  `DW_OP_addrx`, or GNU `DW_OP_GNU_addr_index`, resolved through the unit's
  `.debug_addr` table); (2) typed signatures — return + formal-parameter DIEs
  mapped to unlace `Datatype`s (structs as named opaques, with a cycle guard on the
  DIE walk — see `typedepth` below), registered *after* libproto so real source
  signatures win,
  and read back at *two* points: by a caller's `ActionDefaultParams` for the call
  site, and by the drive as the function's own locked prototype (04 §4.2 —
  `int main(int argc, char **argv)`, not `undefined16 main(uint4, void*)`).
  A compilation unit with no type references and no formal or variadic parameter
  records supplies names and ranges only. Its functions do not acquire locked
  prototypes: rustc minimal debug information omits this signature evidence, and
  treating the omission as `void f(void)` would erase arguments and return values.
  The same guard covers both the direct and declaration-derived prototype paths
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/dwarfsignatures.rs`).
  Units with signature evidence retain their typed imports, including genuinely
  parameterless functions. Names from such minimal units retain their namespace
  qualification, so Rust `core::fmt::write` does not become a global `write`
  alias that could inherit the C import's incompatible signature.
  The default-on `godwarfsig` arm
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/godwarfsig.rs`)
  recovers complete scalar/pointer contracts from Go compiler units on
  little-endian amd64 under `abi-internal`. It requires the producer's `regabi`
  marker and `DW_AT_variable_parameter` to distinguish every input from every
  result. Unit-relative and absolute type/origin references share a bounded
  cross-unit graph. Concrete one-hop abstract origins must account for every
  inherited formal exactly once and in order; additional concrete formals may
  only be results. Malformed references, missing roles, closures, trampolines,
  ABI0 wrappers, unsupported composites by value and unsupported multiple results are
  refused as a whole, retaining existing inference.

  Go compilation units never supply prototypes through the generic C or C++
  DWARF importer (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/goformals.rs`).
  Go encodes results as formal-parameter children, so those importers would
  otherwise install extra inputs and a void return for uncompressed units.
  This exclusion follows each unit's `DW_AT_language`, independently of target
  architecture and option settings. Names and other metadata remain available;
  only the Go-specific importer may install a source signature. Unsupported
  Go contracts therefore retain inference in compressed and uncompressed files.

  On little-endian AArch64 Go ELF with uncompressed or zlib-compressed
  DWARF, this importer also accepts a single pointer-to-`int32` input and
  one signed `int32` or `int64` result. The concrete DWARF definition must
  have a unique entry and match the linked text function's name and full
  extent. Require the Go register-ABI producer,
  explicit input and result roles, and an X0 location at entry for the input.
  A result location can name X0 or be explicitly empty in the debug record.
  The `abi-internal` model must independently place the pointer in X0 and
  choose the low four or eight bytes of X0 for the result. This preserves
  the `int32` boundary even when a widened `int64` function has the same
  machine body. Explicit prototypes still take precedence at the entry.
  This recovers the physical signature. Receiver declarations and method
  call syntax continue to require verified Go pointer method metadata,
  which currently applies to amd64.

  The AArch64 importer limits the total retained DWARF section size to
  64 MiB, counting the larger of each stored and decoded size. When
  enabled, it validates compressed streams and scans complete Go units
  for the selected types and direct formals. It counts duplicate
  definitions before considering the type shape and checks the linked
  name and extent before reading parameter locations. Malformed headers,
  invalid compressed streams and oversized section sets leave signature
  inference in place. The generic DWARF importer continues its ordinary
  section loading and traversal for every format.


  Accepted inputs occupy the verified Go integer or float register sequence;
  an explicit empty location is permitted for an optimized-away input. A
  nonempty location must identify its expected entry register. Go DWARF 5 may
  give a RET-only input a zero-length entry range. That case requires exactly
  one raw range, a base equal to function entry, offsets `[0,0)`, and a single
  register expression matching the input's ABI slot. The function must declare
  a one-byte extent and the image must contain `RET` (`0xc3`) there. Additional
  ranges, a wrong register/base, longer bodies and result-range substitutions
  are refused. General DWARF location-list handling is unchanged. The existing
  calling-convention model must assign every recovered slot to that same
  register with its exact width and no hidden parameter. Stack arguments and
  float arguments beyond the model's eight-register bank are therefore refused.
  A result uses RAX or XMM0. Scalar aliases are checked against width and Go
  kind; pointers retain grounded scalar pointees, unsafe.Pointer, or named flat
  records with nonoverlapping scalar/pointer fields. Cycles, unresolved fields,
  bitfields and invalid extents are refused. Materialized pointees and fields
  must still match the validated graph; a generic void-pointer fallback cannot
  silently satisfy a typed contract.

  A unique function with a scalar or void result may also import up to two Go
  string inputs as their ABI words. Each input needs a Go kind-24, 16-byte
  descriptor with a byte pointer at offset zero and a signed machine-width
  length at offset eight. Each entry location must contain two ordered
  eight-byte register pieces in consecutive expected integer slots. Scalars
  and each accepted pair advance the integer slots independently of the float
  bank. Every slot goes through the ordinary scalar storage checks. The output
  names the separate pointer and length parameters `<formal>_data` and
  `<formal>_len`. Calls keep both words of each input and explicit function
  and call-site prototypes retain precedence. Ambiguous names, missing or
  partial locations, conflicting types, and unsupported contracts fall back
  to inference for the entire function. An accepted single string input also
  records the exact function entry, source formal, physical slot indexes, and
  register storage beside the committed DWARF prototype. Replacing the
  declaration clears that record even when all displayed physical types and
  names agree. P9 may use it for a guarded byte read after checking the
  effective definition. The imported definition and all calls keep their
  physical words. Slice layouts, string results, and grouping these inputs
  into a source-level parameter remain outside this arm.

  Paired results are part of this importer (formerly the separate
  `gopairreturns` option) and follow the target-gated `godwarfsig` default.
  Exactly two signed or unsigned 64-bit integer
  results may follow the scalar inputs. Result allocation restarts independently
  at RAX and RBX. Explicit result locations must name those registers in source
  order; unavailable locations still require the compiler and complete type
  contract. Repeated concrete function entries are ambiguous and cannot receive
  a pair contract. The bounded result list uses two fixed slots, including for
  scalar contracts, so this extension adds no per-result list allocation.
  Narrow, floating, mixed, aggregate and three-result contracts
  remain unsupported. Assignment first uses a temporary ordinary 16-byte struct;
  its zero-flag join must contain RBX then RAX, each eight bytes in the exact
  architectural register space. Input assignments retain their existing checks.
  Only after this proof is the struct interned with fields `result0` and
  `result1` at offsets zero and eight and a `GoPairResults` language facet.
  The facet stores signedness, never interned type references. Existing names
  require matching metadata and complete layout; unrelated names or stale
  metadata cannot be overwritten. No metatype or pcode output count changes.

  A separate bounded result proof
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/godwarfsig/goerror.rs`)
  accepts an actual Go `int` followed by `error`. The first type must name
  signed eight-byte `int` with Go kind 2. The second must resolve through an
  `error` typedef carrying interface kind 20 to the sixteen-byte
  `runtime.iface` struct, kind 25, with exactly `tab` at zero and `data` at
  eight. The table is an eight-byte pointer to the named 32-byte runtime
  `runtime.itab` or `internal/abi.ITab` struct; its internals remain opaque.
  The data is an eight-byte `unsafe.Pointer`. Alias walks are bounded and
  refuse cycles, conflicting kinds, incomplete declarations, qualifiers,
  bitfields and inconsistent extents. The composite result requires an
  explicitly empty result location: neither missing location metadata nor a
  lone register proves its two words. The complete ordered function contract,
  unique entry, producer, input checks and ABI model gates still apply.

  Storage assignment must prove the zero-flag 24-byte join RCX/RBX/RAX before
  interning `__unlace_go_int_error_result`. This ordinary struct contains the
  signed integer `result0` and separate opaque pointers `error_tab` and
  `error_data` at offsets zero, eight and sixteen. Its `GoIntErrorResults`
  facet validates the complete storage and protects reserved-name reuse;
  existing conflicting types or stale metadata are refused. Definitions and
  calls consume the same raw carrier through the normal prototype importer.
  Table and data stay separate, preserving the distinction between nil and
  typed nil. This does not infer `error` from register count, reinterpret
  data as a nil discriminator, or introduce high-level Go error syntax.
  Stripped images, arbitrary interfaces and other composite results retain
  inference. With `godwarfsig off`, this carrier and its metadata are absent.

  A status-only channel receive on amd64 Go ELF can supply a single boolean
  contract. Its unique concrete entry must have a register-ABI input in RAX
  declared as the compiler's receive-only `int` channel and a sole one-byte
  boolean result. The channel typedef must resolve to the complete compiler
  backing record through an eight-byte pointer. `DW_AT_go_elem` must resolve
  to the signed eight-byte Go `int`. That width must fit the private stack
  slot addressed by the guarded receive instruction sequence. The loader
  verifies the sequence against the exact executable `runtime.chanrecv2`
  entry from Go's function table and preserves the proven caller and call site
  for §4's locked-call recovery. Unavailable, ambiguous or inconsistent
  evidence leaves the ordinary inference path in place.

  Named amd64 Go ELF images with supported linked layouts can additionally
  carry a pointer receiver on a complete imported scalar prototype. The
  rooted module descriptor and symbol table must agree on the type region,
  text base, and unique named pointer and record. A method-table entry must
  identify the same ordinary executable function through both Ifn and Tfn.
  The receiver, argument, result and record fields must independently agree
  with the compiler DWARF runtime type offsets and layouts, including the
  RAX and RBX input locations and word-sized result. A value-method record,
  wrapper flag, trampoline, duplicate or missing type evidence leaves the
  ordinary declaration. The function symbol retains receiver evidence only
  while the exact imported prototype and name remain in authority.

  Native Go zlib debug sections are retained compressed at load time. Their
  combined stored/declared extents are bounded to 64 MiB and are inflated only
  when `godwarfsig` is enabled. Each stream must end exactly, pass its checksum
  and produce precisely its declared size. Ordinary non-Go DWARF decompression
  behavior is unchanged. Uncompressed Go units reuse the ordinary snapshots;
  neither path interns new types while the option is off. Enabled contracts
  bind by entry address before function analysis and reach both definitions and
  callers. Later explicit user prototype assertions retain precedence. Source
  aliases, aggregate register decomposition and high-level receiver syntax are
  separate from this import contract.
  An externally visible defined DWARF function's exact `DW_AT_linkage_name` also binds its prototype
  to matching ELF PLT entry addresses
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/dwarflinkage.rs`). The linker spelling is taken from the
  definition or its one-hop `DW_AT_specification` declaration. When no explicit
  linker spelling is present, a source name is accepted only if a defined, global
  ELF function symbol has that exact name and the definition's exact entry address.
  This covers ordinary C declarations without guessing a mangling scheme or
  following abstract-origin clones. Address binding avoids
  ambiguity between an exported implementation and its same-named PLT stub.
  C++ declaration-derived aliases remain in the `cppproto` fact stream, and
  explicit prototype assertions retain their later precedence. Declaration-only
  DIEs and other binary formats do not acquire these aliases. `DW_AT_external`
  must be true on the definition or its specification; a local definition cannot
  retype an unrelated import with the same linker name. A name the file defines as
  an `STT_GNU_IFUNC` symbol is never bound: the DWARF definition behind it is the
  resolver (`void *(void)`), not the implementation its PLT entry dispatches to.
  Separately,
  a formal parameter of a Fortran compilation unit whose location is exactly
  `DW_OP_fbreg` followed by `DW_OP_deref`
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/dwarfbyref.rs`)
  receives a pointer to its described value type. GNU Fortran passes every
  non-`VALUE` dummy argument by reference but describes it by its value type
  plus a frame slot that holds the address; taking that value type as the ABI
  argument instead selected floating registers for a `real` dummy and
  disconnected the incoming address, so `output = sample + bias` printed as
  three unrelated pointer locals. Plain frame slots, including Fortran `VALUE`
  arguments, keep their value types. Other source languages are not inferred
  from this pattern (a C++ class passed by invisible reference carries the same
  location form), nor are composite expressions. Optimized arguments also receive pointer
  types when their location is exactly `DW_OP_breg<n> 0` in an incoming integer
  argument register for the image ABI. Location lists must contain one unambiguous
  expression covering the subprogram entry. Register values, stack/frame-pointer
  locations, nonzero offsets and stack-value expressions retain their value types.
  The register rule skips only values the ABI itself may pass by value through a
  hidden address in that register: none on x86-64 System V or 32-bit Arm, sizes
  other than 1, 2, 4 and 8 bytes on Win64, and values wider than two argument
  registers on AArch64 and RISC-V. Every other value type, including derived
  types, arrays, complex and extended floating types, becomes a pointer; leaving
  one of them a value would hand its register to the next reference argument
  and misname every argument after it. Both
  the name-bound and the address-bound prototype import paths apply the rule;
  a `DW_TAG_enumeration_type` becomes a real enum type — name, declared width,
  signedness, and the `DW_TAG_enumerator` value→name map (05 §5.1), which is what
  turns `quotearg_style(4, …)` into
  `quotearg_style(shell_escape_always_quoting_style, …)`; the enum is looked up
  before it is built, because the same declaration recurs in every compilation
  unit that includes its header. The sign is the enum's `DW_AT_encoding`, which
  gcc emits, else the encoding of the integer its `DW_AT_type` names, which is
  all clang emits (clang's signed enums used to read as unsigned). An enum that
  is not built (anonymous or memberless) falls back to a plain integer: `int` at
  32 bits or wider, as it always was, and below 32 bits an integer of the enum's
  own sign, since that sign decides how a calling convention extends the value
  (04 §4.4, `narrowext`); an enum whose DWARF states no sign (strict DWARF 2) is
  unsigned, named or not, which is what the RISC-V spec's zero extension
  assumed. Base types
  map by encoding; `DW_ATE_UTF` (`char8_t`, `char16_t`, `char32_t`, unsigned in
  C++), the Fortran character encodings and `DW_ATE_unsigned_fixed` are unsigned
  integers, where they used to fall through to a signed one. The two character
  encodings map by name as well (`char_datatype`): `unsigned char` (and so
  `uint8_t`) and `signed char` become character types of that sign
  (`TypeFactory::get_type_char_signed`, Ghidra's `uchar`/`schar`), which print
  as characters and still collapse to `builtin_memset`/`builtin_memcpy`, but
  extend, compare and convert by their own sign. Plain `char`, and any other
  name, keeps the core `char` type whatever its encoding, since its sign is
  the target's (AArch64 and Arm state it `DW_ATE_unsigned_char`) and a string
  stays a `char *`. Both used to read
  as `char`, so a clang `int fwd(char *b, const char *f, unsigned char c)
  { return sprintf(b, f, c); }` printed `sprintf(b,f,c)` with `char c`, which
  compiles to a sign extension (202 prints as -54). A `DW_ATE_complex_float`
  base type
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/dwarfcomplex.rs`)
  becomes a structure of two floating fields, `real` and `imag`, each half
  the value's size, aligned to that half (`unlace_complex_float`,
  `unlace_complex_double`), on the compiler specifications whose ABI passes and
  returns the complex value exactly like that pair structure: ELF SysV AMD64
  and PE x64 Windows for complex float and double, PE i386 for complex float
  only (double-complex recovery there additionally requires correct stack
  argument alignment). It used to fall through to the integer mapping, so
  `float complex f(float complex z) { return cexpf(z); }` printed
  `long f(long z)` with the call's argument and result lost. A complete
  layout of that name is reused across units; a same-named type with any
  other layout (a user's) is left untouched and the next free numbered name
  is taken. Other targets, and `long double` complex everywhere, keep their
  previous mapping. An array's length is the product of the lengths of all its
  `DW_TAG_subrange_type` children, so a multidimensional `int a[3][4]` (or
  gfortran's `grid(-2:0,5:11)`) becomes one flat array of every element (12, 21)
  rather than of its first dimension only, which under-sized the storage of
  multidimensional locals, globals and members. Each subrange's length
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/dwarfbounds.rs`) is
  an explicit `DW_AT_count` if present, otherwise `upper - lower + 1` over signed bounds,
  where an omitted lower bound takes the compilation unit's `DW_AT_language`
  default (one for Fortran and Ada, zero for C, C++ and an unknown language).
  A bound given as a reference or an expression is not a constant, and a count
  that does not fit 64 bits is rejected rather than wrapped; such a dimension
  contributes nothing to the product (a flexible `int rows[][4]` is one row), an
  array with no known dimension is one element, and a product that overflows 64
  bits or exceeds `int4` leaves the array untyped. The
  zero origin used to be assumed everywhere, so gfortran's `real :: a(3)` read
  as `float a[4]` and `a(-8:-4)` as `float a[1]`;
  (3) stack locals — direct `DW_OP_fbreg` children become typelock|namelock stack
  symbols at `call_frame_cfa + fbreg`, re-seeded per decompile (§1.1). A frame
  location may include `DW_OP_plus_uconst` displacements, as emitted for interior
  equivalence views. Each unsigned LEB128 operand is decoded and added without
  signed overflow; truncated operands and dereference, piece, register, or value
  expressions remain outside this fixed-local path. The offset is relative to
  the subprogram's `DW_AT_frame_base`
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/dwarfscopes.rs (frame_base_offset)`):
  gcc's `DW_OP_call_frame_cfa` is `call_frame_cfa`; clang's frame-pointer
  bases are where the standard prologue leaves them, RBP on x86-64 16 bytes
  below the CFA, EBP on i386 8 below, x29 on AArch64 16 below, s0 on RISC-V at
  the CFA; any other register base (an `-fomit-frame-pointer` RSP) moves with
  the body, so that function gets no DWARF stack locals. Every clang -O0 local
  used to be placed 16 bytes off and named the wrong slot. (unlace `dwarfscopes`,
  default on, a load-time env bridge `UNLACE_DWARFSCOPES`) Locals nested in
  `DW_TAG_lexical_block` scopes at any depth are collected in document order
  like direct children, and a variable whose location is a location list takes
  the stack slot when every frame-relative entry of the list names the same one;
  a composite whose `DW_OP_piece` parts are consecutive frame slots is the
  first slot (`dwarfscopes.rs (piece_frame_offset)`). Inlined subroutines
  are walked like lexical blocks, their variables named through
  `DW_AT_abstract_origin`, a repeated name in one function suffixed `_2`, `_3`
  (`scope_vars`, `LocalNames`). A variable held in one register (a whole-function
  `DW_OP_reg<n>`/`DW_OP_regx`, or the longest single-register entry of its
  location list, `register_location`) becomes a `pass.rs (RegLocalFact)`; the
  DWARF register number is turned into the SLEIGH name by the psABI tables in
  `register_name` (x86-64, i386, AArch64, ARM, RISC-V, MIPS, PowerPC). The
  commit parks them on the architecture by function entry, and the decompile
  (`crates/unlace-middle/src/substrate/funcdata.rs (seed_dwarf_register_locals)`)
  maps each as a namelocked, typelocked local at the use point its value will
  have after heritage (`crates/unlace-middle/src/substrate/dwarfregbind.rs
  (reaching_write)`): the range's start when it begins a basic block (a
  loop-carried value's phi); otherwise the last raw write covering the storage
  strictly before the start in the block holding it, or, when that block has
  none, the last one in its single predecessor and so on up the chain (at most
  64 blocks, no window in bytes: an `-O2` local is often defined well before
  its range opens); where the chain reaches a block with several predecessors,
  that block's phi; the entry block with no write (a function input) binds
  nothing. Among writes at one address the one of the type's exact width wins.
  When the reaching write is wider than the DWARF type and the type is an
  integer, a `bool` or an enum (a `char` kept in EBP, written by
  `movzbl` as all of EBP), the local is mapped at the write's own storage and
  width with a same-signed integer type (`widened_metatype`), name-locked but
  not type-locked, so the name binds and type recovery picks the width it
  prints; a narrower pointer, float or record is not widened and stays
  unbound. This also places a narrow local on a big-endian register at the
  bytes the write really covers. The matching raw varnodes have their
  properties refreshed, as for a console `type varnode`. A local left unbound is
  returned to the drive, which with `option honestgaps` on names it in a
  `debuginfo:` header warning instead of dropping it silently (chapter 02). A parameter whose location at the entry PC is a
  single register (`entry_storage`) is locked to that register when the
  default model would put some parameter of the function elsewhere and gives it
  no hidden return pointer (the commit asks the model with
  `assign_parameter_storage`): locked twice, as a `map param` lock for the
  function's own decompile and as explicit input storage on the prototype its
  callers read, so a `regparm(3)` callee and its call sites agree. A function the
  model already describes keeps its model-derived storage. A composite held in several registers (a struct split
  across RDI:RSI) is not mapped; it would need a local symbol at a join-space
  address. (ida) The
  data-global fix (DIV-24): a global used to be mapped with a size-1 type, so any
  multi-byte access queried `queryContainer(addr, 4)` past it and rendered
  `dat_<addr>`; the pass now resolves `DW_AT_type` to a byte size
  (`pass.rs (DataObjectFact)`) and the commit maps an `undefined<size>` entry —
  namelocked but *not* typelocked, so inference still recovers the real type —
  matching how IDA Pro and Ghidra name symbol-table globals (`max_width`, not
  `dat_<addr>`). (unlace `dwarfglobaltypes`, default off: a `decompile-project` export does not yet declare such a global with its type in the header) The pass also emits each
  such global with its declared type (`pass.rs (AnalysisOutput::dwarf_typed_globals)`)
  when that type is sized, complete and not void; with the option on the commit
  drops the untyped entry for those addresses and maps the typed one,
  typelocked and namelocked, first among the typed data facts, so
  `cfg._12_4_ + cfg._8_4_` reads `cfg.flags + cfg.port` and
  `*(char **)&modes[i * 8L]` reads `modes[i]`. (unlace `dwarfdecls`, default on) A
  declaration-only `DW_TAG_subprogram` (`DW_AT_declaration`, no `DW_AT_low_pc`) is kept
  when its linkage name, or else its name, is an ELF import with PLT entries, no DWARF
  definition of it exists in the file, it is prototyped, and every unit declaring it
  agrees on return type, parameter types and variadic slot
  (`dwarf/dwarfdecls.rs`); it is emitted at each PLT entry
  (`pass.rs (AnalysisOutput::dwarf_decl_prototypes)`), and with the option on the
  commit adds it to the address-keyed prototypes where no by-name prototype names the
  import and no address-keyed one sits at that entry, so library signatures, type
  libraries and DWARF definitions keep precedence. Calls to the import then take its
  types: an enum parameter prints a constant argument as its member
  (`gnutls_bye(s,GNUTLS_SHUT_WR)`). (unlace `dwarfenumtypedef`, default on; a load-time
  env bridge, `UNLACE_DWARFENUMTYPEDEF`) An anonymous `DW_TAG_enumeration_type` reached
  through a typedef is interned as an enum under the typedef's name, the alias
  `strip_qualifiers` already gives an anonymous aggregate
  (`dwarf/dwarfenumtypedef.rs`); off, it is the plain underlying integer. (unlace) When neither `.comment`
  nor the other signals name the toolchain, ELF and Mach-O detection falls back
  to the debug info (`analyzers/sourcelang/dwarfproducer.rs (dwarf_compiler)`):
  the first 16 compile units' `DW_AT_language` (Rust, Go, Swift) or
  `DW_AT_producer` (`rustc`, `clang`, `GNU `) decide. Declaration-only DIEs are skipped so DWARF never fights libproto
  over imports. `dwarf_lines`
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/lines.rs (DwarfLinesPass)`)
  is the separate `.debug_line` pass: each row becomes a `file:line` instruction
  comment in the commentdb; default-off because it changes the output.
- **DWARF C++ prototypes** (`cppproto`, always on,
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/cppproto.rs`) is the
  C++ arm of that same pass. Keying every recovery off a subprogram DIE's own
  `DW_AT_name` is right for C and wrong for C++, where the compiler splits a
  definition from its declaration: an out-of-line member or namespace definition
  carries only `DW_AT_specification`, and a concrete out-of-line instance of an
  inlined function only `DW_AT_abstract_origin`. Neither has a name of its own, so
  the whole DIE — name, signature and stack locals — used to be dropped, and on a
  `-g` C++ binary that is most of the program. This arm fuses the definition with
  the declaration it points at (a **single hop**: what a definition points at is
  always a declaration, never another indirection — the reduction of Ghidra's
  `DIEAggregate`), takes the name, return type and parameter names from whichever
  DIE carries them, and builds the source name by walking the DIE's
  namespace/class ancestry (`DWARFName`), so the installed symbol carries
  `Account::deposit` rather than the bare `deposit` the declaration DIE holds. Three type-mapper corrections ride
  along: `DW_TAG_class_type` maps like a structure and a C++ reference like a
  pointer (both are what Ghidra's importer does, and without the first every
  `Foo *this` degraded to `void *`); the transparent qualifier hops
  (`typedef`/`const`/`volatile`/`restrict`) are collapsed before the type switch
  runs, because a `const` member function's `this` is `const Account *const` —
  four DIEs deep, and under the pre-`typedepth` budget one hop too many; and a
  parameter whose type the switch still cannot
  map degrades to an `undefined<n>` of that DIE's own width instead of discarding
  the entire signature, so one exotic member type costs one parameter's type
  rather than the function's whole prototype. Finally the recovered prototype is
  parked by **entry address** rather than by name. Address is the key the read
  side already uses, and the only one that survives C++: unlace files the demangled
  template name `maxof<int>` as `maxof`, and a qualified name lives in a nested
  scope that a global by-name query cannot reach — so both the drive's own-prototype
  lookup (04 §4.2) and the callee-prototype snapshot resolve across every scope,
  not just the global one. The producing pass runs at `load file`; its C++ facts
  are stashed apart from the generic ones and merged at the commit. (Struct/class **fields** are the
  sibling `dwarfstructs` increment below; before it, a class stayed a named opaque
  and `this->balance` printed as an offset.)
- **Changed-convention prototypes** (`dwarfnocall`, default-on,
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/pass.rs (apply_dwarf_nocall)`). A DWARF
  prototype is applied locked, so its parameter list decides which registers a
  function reads. Clang's dead-argument elimination rewrites an internal
  function's convention: an unused or constant parameter is removed, the
  remaining ones move into the earlier argument slots, and the subprogram is
  marked `DW_AT_calling_convention DW_CC_nocall`. The DWARF still lists every
  source parameter; a removed one has no `DW_AT_location` (a constant one has
  `DW_AT_const_value` instead). Both DWARF arms record, for a `DW_CC_nocall`
  subprogram, the positions of its location-less parameters, and the commit
  removes those parameters from the by-name and the by-address prototype before
  either is parked. `work(int *p,int unused,int k)` then decompiles as
  `work(int *p,int k)` with the loop bound read as `k`, and its callers pass two
  arguments instead of an undefined third. The return type is kept, because
  DWARF does not say whether the return value was removed too. GCC's IPA clones
  (`.constprop`, `.isra`, `.part`) need no such rule: they are concrete instances
  linked by `DW_AT_abstract_origin`, which neither arm follows, so a clone never
  receives the source prototype. With `dwarfnocall off` the source list is
  applied unchanged.

  At the enabled commit boundary,
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/cppnames.rs`
  also reconciles a qualified
  function fact with the generic DWARF fact at the same entry address. A unique
  qualified name replaces only its exact bare leaf in the incoming function
  stream. This prevents a redundant global `target` from shadowing
  `left::target` during address lookup, including Rust crate/module paths.
  Definitions, direct calls and whole-function values then share the same
  namespace fact; P9's C function-address qualification preserves the target when
  a function returns its address instead of calling it.
  Every component must be a plain ASCII C++ identifier and must not be a C++
  keyword, using the same spelling check as P9 function-address qualification.
  This retains the generic alias for Rust raw-identifier modules such as `union`,
  template/reference type scopes, and anonymous or malformed scope paths rather
  than replacing printable C definitions with invalid qualified spellings.
  Conflicting qualified facts, different names or addresses, and data symbols
  remain intact. Existing symbols in the database,
  including explicit global aliases and unmangled exports, are never removed.
  Address-keyed prototype application follows generic prototype application.
- **Aggregate layout**
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/dwarfstructs.rs`,
  always on with `dwarf`; formerly the `dwarfstructs` option) is
  what turns a recovered aggregate from a *name* into a *type*. The mapper used to
  resolve every `DW_TAG_structure_type`/`union_type`/`class_type` to
  `get_type_struct(name)` — a named, empty, **zero-size** shell — and never read
  `DW_AT_byte_size` or walked a single `DW_TAG_member`. That is enough for
  `struct foo *p` to render, and the shortfall was filed as a fields gap; it is
  worse than that, because a zero width is not a conservative answer. The
  x86-64 parameter-storage model reads the size, so a struct passed **by value**
  had no width to classify and its slot degraded to the raw register it arrives
  in (`int take_struct(unsigned long,int)` for `take_struct(P8,int)`), and an
  8-byte struct **return** — a register return on this ABI — was classified as a
  hidden-return-buffer call: a *phantom* `rethidden` parameter appeared in front of
  the real ones and the body then did arithmetic on it. This arm reads
  `DW_AT_byte_size`, walks the `DW_TAG_member` children, places each at its
  `DW_AT_data_member_location` **verbatim**, accepting both integer attributes
  and DWARF 2's single `DW_OP_plus_uconst` expression. As upstream reads it, an
  absent location places the member at offset zero (DWARF lets a producer omit
  it there), a location that is present but not a constant displacement skips
  the member rather than misplacing it, and a static member (external or
  declaration-only) is not part of the layout. Global `DW_OP_addr` locations
  are read in the DWARF reader's byte order and must be exactly one address of
  the unit's address size; an address followed by more operations is not a
  static location. A DWARF 5 producer writes the same location as
  `DW_OP_addrx <index>` (GNU split DWARF: `DW_OP_GNU_addr_index`); that index
  is resolved through the unit's `.debug_addr` table
  (`dwarf/mod.rs (indexed_addr_location)`), so a clang `-g` binary whose
  statics have no ELF symbol still names them.
  The mapper recurses each member's
  `DW_AT_type` through the same DIE switch; bitfields come off `DW_AT_bit_size`
  with either the DWARF 4/5 `DW_AT_data_bit_offset` or the DWARF 2/3
  `byte_size` + `bit_offset` spelling, each placed in the smallest byte span that
  covers it — the geometry the compiler's own access agrees with, and the one the
  printer's `.`-versus-`->` test reads. Positions follow the target's bit order:
  on a big-endian target both `DW_AT_data_bit_offset` and `DW_AT_bit_offset`
  count from the most significant bit of the first byte (of the aggregate and of
  the storage unit respectively), and a span's least significant bit lies in its
  last byte. `DW_AT_bit_offset` is signed: a packed field that extends past its
  unit has a negative one, which GCC writes as `DW_FORM_sdata` and clang as the
  two's complement in a `DW_FORM_data8`, so a fixed-size form is sign-extended
  from its width. The unit defaults to the member type's size
  when `DW_AT_byte_size` is absent, and a bitfield with a location but no bit
  offset starts at that byte. Bitfields are listed in memory order, the order the
  bitfield lookup's binary search expects. A member with `DW_AT_bit_size` that
  cannot be placed, or that ends past the aggregate, is skipped. A "bitfield"
  occupying whole aligned bytes of a natural width is not one and goes in as a
  plain field of that width, as upstream's wire decode makes it. That is exact
  in either byte order and gives type inference, which runs before the bitfield
  transforms, the field's own integer type to propagate (chapter 05). Offsets
  are installed through a raw
  field-setting entry point rather than the C packing rules, because the layout is
  the compiler's own answer for the target ABI and re-deriving it would silently
  disagree with the bytes the decompiler reads.

  Two hazards come with populating fields, and both are handled in the naming.
  The type factory interns by `(name, hash(name))` and refuses a second, different
  definition of a name it already holds; while every aggregate was a sizeless
  shell that was invisible, because two shells compare equal. It goes live the
  moment fields exist — and it is not exotic: `rustc -g` names every enum payload
  struct **bare** (`Some`, `Ok`, `Err`), and a five-function Rust witness carries
  four distinct `Some` DIEs of sizes 16, 24, 16 and 12. Aggregates are therefore
  interned under their **parent-qualified** name (the namespace/class ancestry walk
  the C++ arm already had) and, when that name is still held by an aggregate of a
  different size, under a size-suffixed variant; a name held by a non-aggregate is
  stepped over the same way. The second hazard is self-reference: a
  `struct node { struct node *next; }` reaches its own DIE while its fields are
  being built, so the shell is interned **before** the members are walked and the
  inner resolution finds it by name, with the walk guard refusing a re-entrant
  population. LOSS: because an interned type is immutable in unlace, completing one
  mints a new handle, so the pointer the inner frame captured still refers to the
  pre-completion shell — the name renders but the chain is one level shorter.
  `DW_TAG_variant_part`/`DW_TAG_variant`/`DW_AT_discr`, the Rust tagged-enum
  encoding, are not read by this arm; the sibling variant-part increment below
  reads them, and where it refuses a Rust enum recovers its width and no fields.
  The layout is installed inside `load file`, with the rest of the DWARF import.
- **Discriminated unions**
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/dwarfvariants.rs`,
  always on with `dwarf`; formerly the `dwarfvariants` option) is
  the arm for the aggregates the member walk above cannot see at all. A Rust
  tagged enum carries **no `DW_TAG_member` of its own**: its layout hangs off a
  `DW_TAG_variant_part`, whose `DW_AT_discr` points at the artificial member that
  IS the discriminant, and whose `DW_TAG_variant` children each carry a
  `DW_AT_discr_value` plus one `DW_TAG_member` naming the variant (`Ok`, `Err`,
  `Some`, `None`) and referring to its payload struct. So `dwarfstructs` alone
  gave a Rust enum its `DW_AT_byte_size` and zero fields — and a field-less
  aggregate is still an aggregate the ABI classifier acts on, so an 8-byte
  `fn(u32) -> Result<u32,u32>` came out with the same phantom `rethidden`
  parameter described above and a 16-byte one wrote its variants as
  `*(uint *)&r->field_0x4`.

  Reading it from DWARF rather than from codegen is the point. The two questions
  a decompiler cannot answer from shape are *is this a discriminated union* and
  *which variant is which*: two return paths storing different constants at
  offset 0 is equally a `#[repr(C)] struct {kind, val}`, a `(u64,u64)` tuple, a
  bitmask pair, or a `&'static str` fat pointer whose "discriminant" would be a
  `.rodata` address. `DW_AT_discr` and `DW_AT_discr_value` are the compiler
  stating both answers, so no name installed here is an inference — though a name
  DWARF states is still only installed where the union model can select it
  unambiguously, which is the second limitation at the end of this bullet.

  The recovered type is a struct of the discriminant plus a **union** of one
  payload struct per variant. A union's members all sit at offset 0, which is
  exactly a variant overlay, so this uses the existing type model rather than
  adding a `type_metatype` (that enum is matched at ~1,700 sites in this
  workspace — `grep -ro 'type_metatype::' --include=*.rs crates | wc -l`
  reports 1678 — mostly non-exhaustively, so a new variant would compile clean and
  behave wrong;
  `sub_metatype` is a contiguous propagation sort key; and `metatype2string`
  writes a fixed vocabulary onto the Ghidra wire). The overlay
  begins at the lowest offset any variant places a field at, and each facet's
  fields are **re-based** to it: DWARF gives a variant's payload struct the width
  of the whole enum with its members at their absolute offsets
  (`Result<u32,u32>::Ok` is 8 bytes with `__0` at 4), which describes an overlay
  at offset 0 and cannot be placed beside a `tag` field at the same offset.
  Every name minted — the facets and the overlay union — is derived from the
  enum's own parent-qualified name and goes through the same collision policy
  `dwarfstructs` established, because rustc names payload structs bare and the
  collision is not hypothetical: the committed `dwarfvariants_x86_64` fixture
  alone carries **3 structure DIEs named `Some` at two different widths** (8 and
  16), and a std-linked `rustc 1.90 -C debuginfo=2` witness with 152 variant parts
  carries 61 named `Some` across 8 byte sizes (0/8/12/16/24/32/48/64), 61 `None`,
  and 31 each `Ok`/`Err` across 7. A suppressed facet, whose name is derived from
  its offset rather than from the variant, can collide inside a single enum
  (`Tree::field_0x8` for both `Leaf` and `Node`); identical layouts then share one
  interned struct and differing ones are given a numeric suffix, because the ABI
  classifier common-refines the union's members.

  Two shapes get specific treatment. A **fieldless** variant (`None`, `Nil`, a
  unit variant) overlays nothing and gets **no union member**: an empty struct of
  the overlay's width is indistinguishable to the union-field scorer from the
  facet that does carry the payload, and it wins the tie by declaration order.
  Ablating the exclusion, a std-linked `rustc -g` witness writes an `Option<i64>`
  payload as `v13.payload.None = ...` and reads drop glue as
  `(*a0).dropfn.drop.None` — 2 functions of 612, measured, which is what fixed it
  this way. The variant is not lost — its name and its discriminant value
  are on the side table, which is where a `match` renderer reads them, and there
  is no payload for a field path to reach. A **niche-encoded** enum, where a
  `DW_TAG_variant` carries no `DW_AT_discr_value` at all (it is the default
  variant: every value the others did not claim) and the discriminant's bytes
  overlap the payload, has no byte range that is only the tag — so the recovered
  type is the **overlay alone**: the union, at the variants' own DWARF offsets,
  under the enum's own name, with no enclosing struct, because a `tag` field would
  have to sit at an offset a variant already owns. The geometry still reaches the
  side table, marked as a niche.

  The geometry — the discriminant's offset and width, each variant's name,
  discriminant value and absolute field offsets, and whether the encoding is a
  niche — is recorded in a side table on the `TypeFactory`
  (`crates/unlace-middle/src/p0_knowledge/dwarfvariants.rs`). It is
  the `unlace_wire_symbols` arrangement: nothing in the analysis reads it, no
  `Datatype` points at it, and it is not encoded onto the wire, so filling it
  cannot perturb emitted C. It exists so a later pass can render `match` /
  `if let` / `Ok(v)` from the compiler's own answer.

  Every guard REFUSES rather than guesses, and every refusal ends at the same
  answer the `dwarfstructs` path above gives — a named aggregate with the enum's
  byte size and no fields — but by two different routes. Refused BEFORE anything
  is interned, so the DIE simply falls through: no `DW_AT_discr`; a variant with
  anything other than exactly one named member; two variants with no
  `DW_AT_discr_value`, or with the same one, or with the same name; a payload
  struct carrying its own `DW_TAG_variant_part` (a nested variant part, which the
  single-level overlay cannot describe — rustc 1.90 emitted none across the 75
  variant parts in the two witnesses measured for this change); no variant with
  any field at all (a C-like enum, which rustc emits as a
  `DW_TAG_enumeration_type` instead); a discriminant whose location cannot be
  decoded, or whose type is not integer-shaped, zero-width, or wider than the
  enum; a zero-width or absent `DW_AT_byte_size`; and a `DW_AT_declaration` DIE.
  Payload members are placed by the member rule above: a member without a
  location starts the payload, and a static member or one whose location cannot
  be decoded is skipped.

  Refused AFTER the shell is interned — it has to exist before the members are
  walked so a recursive payload has something to point at — the answer cannot be
  "leave it to `dwarfstructs`", because a zero-size incomplete type is already
  sitting in the factory under the enum's own name, and downstream that degrades
  to `void`. Those refusals instead SEAL that shell at the enum's
  `DW_AT_byte_size` with no fields, which is byte for byte the `dwarfstructs`
  answer: a member that would extend past the enum; every facet's fields being
  unbuildable, which would leave a zero-member union describing nothing; and the
  overlay union's name being unmintable or any of the three completions being
  refused by the factory. This arm extends the member walk above and runs with
  it.

- **Prototype merge** (always on, no option; unlace;
  `crates/unlace-bandb-base/src/p4_calls/protomerge.rs (merge)`): the
  load-time sources park whole prototypes on a function at the analysis commit
  (the by-name and by-address libc tables, the demangled C++ signature, DWARF),
  and the last used to replace the earlier wholesale. Two prototypes of the same
  shape (arity, variadic slot, the same size in every slot) now merge slot by
  slot: a typed slot (pointer, float, bool, aggregate, enum) beats a plain
  integer, which beats an undefined; two typed slots, two pointers included, are
  a tie that the later source wins, so DWARF's `void *` stays even where a table
  spelled `unsigned char *`. Names fill in from the earlier source; a return type
  survives a later source that leaves it open. Different shapes replace as
  before; directive, console and decompile-time prototypes never merge. IDA's
  per-argument `score_tinfo` merge. On Lua 5.4.8 with DWARF, llvm-objdump, bzip2
  and an i386 C++ fixture it changes no signature.

- **Name ladder** (`nameladder`, default-on; unlace;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/protos/nameladder.rs (fallbacks)`):
  a function name that is not in a prototype table or the no-return list as
  spelled is retried under its undecorated spellings, each rung stripping one
  more decoration: a `j_` jump-thunk prefix, an import prefix (`__imp_`, `_imp_`,
  `imp__`), a stdcall/fastcall `@N` decoration, the leading ABI underscores, and
  a trailing `_<digits>` duplicate-name suffix. The first spelling a table holds
  gives the prototype (keyed to the image's own name) or the no-return verdict.
  A name the table holds as spelled is never retried, so the ladder only adds
  facts. This is IDA's type-library lookup ladder (`guess_tinfo`,
  `cleanup_name`). The passes that climb it run at `load file`, so they read
  the option as `UNLACE_NAMELADDER` (exported by the CLI, set for the next
  `load file` by the console's `option nameladder`).

- **Discriminant-value naming**
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/variantnames.rs`,
  always on with `dwarf`; formerly the `variantnames` option;
  `docs/multilang.md`, the first `VariantLayout` consumer) closes the loop the
  side table above left open at its cheapest point. The variant-part importer
  installs the `tag` member with the plain integer type DWARF declares for it,
  so every test or store of the discriminant renders a bare constant —
  `(*e).tag == 1`, `rethidden->tag = 0` — when the compiler stated what those
  values MEAN. With the gate on, the importer instead gives the tag member a
  synthesized enum, `<enum>::Discriminant`, of the tag's own width
  (`TYPE_ENUM_UINT` plus a namemap of exactly the variant part's
  `(DW_AT_discr_value, variant name)` pairs, masked to the tag's width the way
  `build_enum` masks a C enumerator), and the stock enum-constant rendering
  prints `(*e).tag == Err` / `rethidden->tag = A` with no new emission
  machinery. A bit-TESTED tag takes the stock flag-enum arithmetic form —
  `(l->tag & Nil) == Cons` where `off` prints `!(l->tag & 1)` — which carries
  the vocabulary at some cost in plainness; that form is the existing C-enum
  behavior, not a new renderer, and `off` restores the integers. Stand-downs,
  each deliberate: a NICHE layout has no tag field, so nothing is retyped (an
  `Option<&T>` null test keeps its rendering — selecting the facet a niche
  value implies is the `match` renderer's job on the same side table); a tag
  DWARF already declares as an enum keeps the compiler's own type; the DEFAULT
  variant has no single value and so gets no member; and a foreign type
  already owning the synthesized name is never fought (the re-imported
  compilation unit reuses it on an exact shape match, the `build_enum` rule).
  It acts only where a variant part was imported — no layout, no tag member,
  nothing to retype. `tests/stages/variantnames.toml` and
  the unlace-console `verify_variantnames` gate own the naming assertions
  (store, read, declaration type, and the niche no-op) over the committed
  `dwarfvariants_x86_64` fixture.

  **The limitation is the channel.** This needs full debug info
  (`-C debuginfo=2`, cargo `debug = true`). Where a binary's DWARF carries no type
  DIEs the arm is not degraded, it is inert: it recovers nothing and attempts no
  fallback, because the only available fallback is the shape inference above. A C
  program has no variant part at all, so the arm never fires on one.

  **The second limitation is the union model, and it decides what may be named.**
  Representing a variant overlay as a union means a member selects itself by
  OFFSET; the discriminant is never consulted. For a tagged enum that is not a
  corner case but the definition of the encoding: every payload variant begins
  immediately after the tag, so `Ok` and `Err` are at the same offset, always, and
  the facet the union-field scorer picks is not evidence of anything. Measured, on
  a `Result<u64,u64>` witness the label was not merely uncertain but consistently
  false — `Ok` was printed on both arms of the producing `if`/`else` and on the
  consumer's `Err(e) => e + 100`, and `Err` appeared nowhere in the binary.

  So a variant name is installed **only where it is forced**, and the rule is
  applied per byte range rather than per variant:

  - a facet keeps its `DW_TAG_variant` name only when no other variant claims a
    byte it claims. `Option<T>` has exactly one payload-carrying variant, so
    `Some` survives; `Result<T,E>` has two over one range, so both are spelled
    `field_0x<offset>` — the offset rendering a reader gets when the answer is
    unknown. Both the union member
    and the facet's own interned type name are suppressed, because a cast in the
    emitted C prints the type name and suppressing only one of the two would still
    leak the variant. Two suppressed facets that describe the same bytes share one
    interned struct; two that differ get distinct ones, because the ABI classifier
    common-refines the union's members and merging two shapes would change how the
    enum is passed.
  - a field inside a facet keeps its DWARF name only when every other variant
    either claims none of its bytes or names exactly that range the same way.
    rustc names tuple payloads `__0`/`__1`, so `Result`'s two `__0`s agree and the
    name claims nothing about which variant is live; `enum Multi { P{a,b}, Q(u64) }`
    keeps `P.a` (nothing else claims [4,8)) and spells the word at 8 by offset,
    because `P.b` and `Q.__0` disagree there.

  The rule is deliberately conservative at facet granularity: an access WIDTH can
  sometimes single out a variant that the byte range alone cannot (an 8-byte store
  at offset 8 of `Multi` can only be `Q`), but a union member name is fixed when
  the type is built, not per access, so those labels go too. What is given up is
  the label, never the layout — offsets, widths, member types and the enum's own
  size are exactly what DWARF states either way, and every variant's source name
  and `DW_AT_discr_value` remain on the side table. Picking the facet from the tag
  needs a dominating-guard analysis; that is what the side table is recorded for,
  and it is not attempted here.
- **Function-pointer types** (`calltargettype`, on by default, off for Rust
  output) keep what a `DW_TAG_subroutine_type` says. The mapper used
  to give up on the tag, so a pointer to one became a pointer to `void`: a
  parameter, a record field or a local declared `int (*f)(int, long)` came out
  `void *`, and every call through it was a call of a `void *` that no C compiler
  accepts. With the option on, a prototyped subroutine type maps to a code type
  whose prototype is its `DW_AT_type` (none is `void`) and its
  `DW_TAG_formal_parameter` types, a trailing `DW_TAG_unspecified_parameters`
  making it variadic, through `TypeFactory::get_type_code_proto`
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/mod.rs
  (build_subroutine)`), and a pointer to it is a function pointer:
  `unsigned long (*hasher)(void *,unsigned long);`. A type without
  `DW_AT_prototyped` (`int (*)()` in C, and every C++ one, which never carries
  it) states no parameters, a `...` with nothing before it has no C spelling,
  and a parameter type the switch cannot build leaves nothing to state, so each
  keeps the `void` pointee. The mapping happens inside `load file`, before any
  option is applied, so the gate is the `UNLACE_CALLTARGETTYPE` environment
  variable (chapter 00) the CLI exports ahead of the load from the run's options,
  the mode's preset included, and leaves off when the output language is Rust;
  the browser front-end does not export it.
  Chapter 05 covers what the option does to the calls.
- **Full-depth DWARF types** (`typedepth`, always on,
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/typedepth.rs`) is the
  type mapper's recursion guard, and it exists because the DIE walk can be handed a
  chain that closes on itself — a `DW_TAG_pointer_type` whose `DW_AT_type` is its
  own offset, a `typedef`/`const` pair pointing at each other — which nothing in
  the format forbids and a truncated or forged `.debug_info` supplies. Upstream
  (`DWARFDataTypeImporter.trackRecursion`) guards it with a **per-DIE-offset
  re-entry counter**: a DIE may be re-entered twice and the third entry is refused,
  which fires only on a cycle because an acyclic chain visits each offset once.
  unlace's port had reduced that to a flat three-hop budget counted over *every*
  link, transparent qualifiers included — which conflates "the same DIE again" with
  "a deep but finite chain". Four DIEs is ordinary C: `const char *const *`,
  `const size_t *`, `char *const []`, `char ***`. All of them ran out of budget and
  fell back to `void`, so a `-g` binary's stack locals, its globals (a truncated
  element type sizes the global at one byte, and the extent is what the container
  query needs — §1.4) and its deeper pointer parameters rendered `void *` while the
  debug info named a concrete type. This restores upstream's counter, with a second
  absolute nesting bound as a native-stack backstop that a Java port does not need;
  termination no longer rests on a cap that also has to be small. Two consequences
  ride along: the qualifier collapse the C++ arm introduced now runs for the C
  callers too — that is what carries an anonymous aggregate's typedef name onto it
  (a local `mbstate_t`, not the shared `anon_struct` every unnamed struct fuses
  into) — and when the borrowed name is one the type factory already holds under
  another kind (unlace registers a core type called `code`, which zlib's
  `inftrees.h` really does typedef an anonymous struct to), the aggregate falls
  back to the anonymous name rather than failing to build and letting the pointer
  arm degrade it to `void *`. The mapping happens at `load file`.
- **Demangling** (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/demangle/mod.rs
  (demangle_name)`, the `GnuDemanglerAnalyzer` analog) is not a registered pass but
  a loader hook: applied to every funcsym name after `@VERSION` stripping, before
  install. Upstream shells out to libiberty; unlace substitutes the `cpp_demangle`
  (Itanium), `rustc_demangle`, and `msvc_demangler` (`?…` names) crates. A `?…`
  name `msvc_demangler` rejects goes to `undname`, a port of LLVM's
  MicrosoftDemangle, which reads the newer encodings MSVC emits (a deduced `auto`
  return, `operator<=>`, `noexcept` function types, address and member-pointer
  template arguments, vtordisp thunks); its spelling of a compiler-generated
  member is brought to `msvc_demangler`'s (`dtor` is `destructor`) so a member
  reads the same whichever crate demangled it.

  **Lambda closures** (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/demangle/lambda.rs`,
  `is_lambda_symbol`) are flagged, not renamed. A closure type's `operator()` is
  recognised from three signals, any one enough: the Itanium closure-type name
  `Ul <sig> E [digits] _` (the `Ul` at a nested-name, substitution or length
  boundary), clang's `$_<n>` source name (in the mangled form, or at the start of
  a demangled component), and libiberty's `{lambda(...)#N}` text. The flag is
  metadata only; it changes no emitted name.

  **(unlace, docs/multilang.md) Swift names demangle through a pure-Rust
  demangler written for unlace** (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/demangle/swift.rs
  (demangle_swift_name)`, with the parser in `swift/parse.rs`, the
  `_Tt` runtime-name parser in `swift/oldparse.rs`, the full-form
  printer in `swift/print.rs` and the name-only printer in
  `swift/name.rs`). Every Swift demangler crate (`swift-demangler`,
  `symbolic-demangle`, `macho-demangle`, `razgad`, `swift-demangle`) builds
  Apple's C++ demangler, a build-time C++ toolchain `unlace-wasm` cannot carry,
  so unlace owns the port: the stable `$s`/`$S` grammar of
  `swift/docs/ABI/Mangling.rst` as the postfix stack machine Apple's reference
  implementation uses (each operator pops its operands from a node stack and
  pushes one node; substitutions `A…` and the stdlib shortcuts `S…` re-reference
  earlier nodes; word substitutions `0…` and punycode `00…` identifiers decode),
  plus the Swift 3 `_Tt` type mangling the Objective-C runtime still uses for
  Swift class and protocol names (`_TtC6Sample3Foo`, nested `_TtCC…`, private
  `P33_<hash>`, generic `_TtGC…_`, protocol `_TtP…_`). The parser covers
  entities (functions with labels, variables and every accessor, subscripts,
  constructors and destructors, closures, default arguments, initializers),
  contexts (modules, nominal types, extensions, private and local names), the
  type grammar (bound generics with sugar, tuples, function types with their
  effects, metatypes, existentials, generic parameters and dependent members,
  generic signatures with requirements, builtins, SIL impl function types),
  the runtime artifacts (type metadata and its accessors and caches, nominal
  and protocol descriptors, conformance descriptors, witness tables and
  witnesses, value witnesses, field offsets, enum cases, opaque type
  descriptors, reflection descriptors), and the function attributes
  (dispatch thunks, method descriptors, merged functions, `@objc` thunks,
  partial-apply forwarders, outlined copies, async function pointers and
  resume functions, generic and function-signature specializations,
  reabstraction thunks, key path thunks, once-functions). Out of coverage
  (the symbol stays mangled): the autodiff family (`TJ…`), bridged outlines
  (`Te`), macro entities (`fm`/`fM…`), Embedded Swift symbols (`$e`),
  coroutine continuation prototypes (`TC`) and anonymous contexts (`XZ`).
  The full-form printer (`demangle_raw`) renders the tree the way
  `swift-demangle` from Swift 6.3 does, and is verified byte for byte against
  it on the reference's own `manglings.txt`, on the Swift stdlib, Foundation
  and app symbol tables, and on randomly mutated symbols (where both demangle,
  they agree; where `swift-demangle` refuses, so does unlace). Swift 6.4 renamed
  the two experimental coroutine accessors to `yielding_borrow` and
  `yielding_mutate`; this printer keeps the 6.3 spellings `read2` and
  `modify2`. The one deliberate difference: a constructor carrying a file
  discriminator without a name prints `Foo.(in _HASH).init()` where
  `swift-demangle` prints its parameter type as the name. The name-only printer (`demangle_name`, what the loader installs)
  is a projection of the same tree: space-free Swift reference syntax for
  members (`Sample.Foo.init(x:y:)`, `Foo.bar(_:)`, `Foo.baz()`, `Foo.x.getter`,
  `Foo.subscript(_:).getter`, `Foo.__allocating_init(x:)` on a class), dotted
  tags for runtime artifacts (`Foo.type_metadata`, `.nominal_type_descriptor`,
  `.dispatch_thunk`, `.method_descriptor`, `.merged`, `.objc`, `.closure#1`,
  `.outlined_copy`, `.generic_specialization<Swift.Int>`,
  `.function_signature_specialization`, `.partial_apply`), and `<Type:Protocol>`
  for conformances (`<Sample.Foo:Swift.Hashable>.hash(into:)` is the protocol
  witness, `<…>.protocol_witness_table` and `<…>.protocol_conformance_descriptor`
  the tables). Private discriminators, local-name counters, generic
  signatures, extension modules and parameter types are dropped from the name;
  where a name is meaningless without types (conformances, specializations,
  reabstraction thunks, key path helpers) a compact spelling appears
  (`[Swift.String:Any]`, `(Swift.Int)->Swift.Bool`, `A?`). The contract is
  parse-or-passthrough: an unknown operator, a malformed count, a stack that
  does not reduce, or a node kind without a rendering fails the whole name and
  the symbol keeps its mangled spelling — a wrong path is never printed. The
  Objective-C metadata pass (`analyzers/objc/mod.rs`) renders a class whose
  `class_ro_t.name` is a `_Tt` name through the same demangler, so a Swift
  class's method labels read `-[Sample.Foo viewDidLoad]` while the
  `_OBJC_CLASS_$_…` data symbol keeps the linker's spelling. The arm is
  shape-gated on `sourcelang::is_swift_mangled` — prefixes no other scheme
