  owns — and always on. On a large arm64 iOS app (314,038 functions, 7,382 of them under Swift symbols) it
  takes every Swift symbol from mangled to demangled where the earlier
  name-only subset reached 26%, at no measurable cost (demangling the whole
  symbol table takes under 10 ms). The unit-test corpus is real symbols
  pinned with the `swift-demangle` output; the stage test
  `tests/stages/swiftdemangle.toml` loads `macho_swift_names_arm64`, a
  clang-built arm64 Mach-O whose root class carries the runtime name
  `_TtC4main7Greeter` through `objc_runtime_name` and whose exported function
  carries the symbol `_$s4main10countWords2ofS2i_tF` through an `asm` label,
  and proves both spellings off and on.

  **(unlace, DIV-83) Which crate is asked first is decided by a marker, not by
  which one answers.** Rust's *legacy* scheme reuses the Itanium `_ZN…E`
  envelope, escaping the characters an Itanium identifier cannot hold (`$LT$`
  for `<`, `$C$` for `,`, `$u20$` for a space, `..` for `::`). A C++ demangler
  therefore does not decline such a symbol — it sees a well-formed nested-name
  whose components happen to contain dollar signs, and returns the escapes
  verbatim. Asking Itanium first did not fall through to Rust; it produced a
  wrong answer confidently, and every Rust binary rendered its own call graph as
  escape soup (`core::ptr::drop_in_place$LT$…$GT$` where `nm -C` gives
  `core::ptr::drop_in_place<…>`). `sourcelang::is_rust_mangled` identifies both
  Rust schemes by the v0 grammar or the legacy `17h<16 lowercase hex>E` hash tail,
  so a symbol carrying either goes to `rustc_demangle` first.

  Legacy Rust uses lowercase hexadecimal for its compiler hash. An uppercase
  or mixed-case hash-shaped component can be a user name, including when an
  actual lowercase hash follows it. The reduced-name pass keeps that component,
  and the Rust fallback keeps it when the demangler would elide it under
  alternate formatting. An accepted LLVM suffix still follows the demangler's
  existing suffix rules. `tests/stages/ghangr-rust-uppercase-legacy-hash.toml`
  pins these spellings and ordinary Itanium, MSVC, legacy and v0 names.

  A legacy Rust name with an LLVM import suffix still goes to the Rust
  demangler first. `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/sourcelang/legacy_llvm.rs` removes the suffix
  only for recognition: the preceding name must have a lowercase 16-digit
  Rust hash, the nonempty suffix must use the LLVM characters accepted by
  `rustc_demangle`, and that parser must accept the complete name. The original
  spelling reaches the demangler, which decodes its escapes and omits the LLVM
  suffix. This preserves the closure scope in the pinned
  `lang_start_internal` name instead of installing its dollar escapes as an
  Itanium identifier. Names without the hash, malformed names, uppercase-hash
  lookalikes and unsupported suffixes keep their existing paths; ordinary
  unsuffixed recognition and the versioned-symbol guard are unchanged.

  The v0 arm requires the **leading underscore**, and that requirement is
  load-bearing rather than cosmetic. A prefix test written as
  `strip_prefix('_').unwrap_or(name)` keeps the *original* name when there is no
  underscore to strip, which quietly reduces "begins with `_R`" to "begins with
  `R`" -- and since one matching symbol is enough to classify the whole image,
  any C program importing OpenSSL's `RAND_bytes` or `RSA_new` was reported as
  `Compiler::Rustc`. That misclassification is invisible to both parity corpora,
  whose fixtures are `<bytechunk>` images with no symbol table at all, and it
  reaches the reader through the `--language auto` policy of DIV-80: an ordinary
  C binary rendered as `unsafe fn`.

  A Rust demangling is a *type expression*, not a path: it carries generic
  arguments (`drop_in_place<Vec<u8>>`) and trait qualifiers
  (`<aes::Aes256 as crypto_common::KeyInit>::new`). `normalize_rust_name`
  resolves both, and they cannot be resolved the same way — a generic list
  carries no path and is dropped, but a qualifier carries **two** paths and
  dropping it would leave a leading `::`, an empty scope component the symbol
  table rejects outright. `<X as Y>` keeps the type `X` (so the method stays
  attached to the type that defines it), `<impl X as Y>` keeps the trait `Y`,
  and `<impl Trait for Type>` keeps `Type`. An inherent method's qualified self
  type at the start of the name (`<serde_json::de::Deserializer<R>>::parse_integer`)
  keeps its path too, and loses only its own generics
  (`serde_json::de::Deserializer::parse_integer`); it was dropped like a generic list,
  which left the bare `parse_integer` for 2,154 of fclones' 8,341 functions. A
  self type with no path (`<[T]>::sort_unstable`, a reference, a tuple) still
  resolves to nothing. Angle brackets nest, so this is a
  depth-tracking scan iterated to a fixed point rather than a pattern match.

  A this-adjusting thunk (`_ZTh`, `_ZTv`, `_ZTc`) is named for the function it
  jumps to (`demangle/mod.rs (thunk_target)`): cpp_demangle renders it as
  `{virtual override thunk(<offsets>, <target>)}`, and reducing that whole string
  left `{virtual override thunk}`, the name 46 functions of the iOS 16
  `libc++.1.dylib` shared (every `basic_*stream` destructor thunk). The target is
  the text after the last top-level comma, reduced like any other name.

  The hard contract is **name-only** reduction: unlace's scope splitter nests on every `::`,
  so signature tails and template argument groups must be stripped or they become
  junk scopes. **Operator names are exempt from that stripping**: `operator[]`,
  `operator()`, `operator<<`, `operator->` and their siblings are spelled with the
  very characters the reduction removes, so a bracket run directly after an
  operator head is copied verbatim and only the parameter list that follows it is
  dropped. Without the exemption every bracket-spelled overload of a class
  collapsed onto one indistinguishable `Class::operator` — 65 distinct functions
  in `libstdc++` shared the name `std::operator`, which is now split into its real
  `std::operator<<` (33) and `std::operator>>` (32). A `<` followed by an
  identifier character is left to the generic path, where it opens a template
  argument list rather than spelling the operator. **Anonymous namespaces are the
  second exemption**, and the one whose absence was fatal rather than merely lossy:
  Itanium renders `_GLOBAL__N_…` as the parenthesized `(anonymous namespace)` and
  MSVC as the backtick-quoted `` `anonymous namespace' ``, so the reduction used to
  delete the Itanium spelling whole and leave an **empty** component —
  `leveldb::(anonymous namespace)::HandleDumpCommand` reduced to
  `leveldb::::HandleDumpCommand`. The scope splitter rejects an empty component
  (§0.4), and because the symbol table is installed inside `load file` that
  rejection aborts the entire architecture build, so a binary carrying one such
  symbol produced no output from any command. An anonymous namespace is the
  ordinary way C++ gives a definition internal linkage, which put a large share of
  real unstripped C++ binaries — a MinGW malware DLL with 1184 such libstdc++
  symbols, and `libleveldb` — outside what unlace could load at all. Both spellings
  now become the identifier `anonymous_namespace`, matching what
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/rtti/itaniumrtti.rs
  (sanitize_class_name)` already gives the same construct, so one toolchain's
  anonymous namespace is spelled like another's and the component survives as a
  real scope. Two translation units that each define `helper` in an anonymous
  namespace still collide on one name — the Itanium mangling is identical for both,
  so no demangler can separate them — and their distinct addresses are what every
  resolver keys on. `demangle_raw` keeps the faithful c++filt text it is asked for,
  unrewritten.
- **Demangled C++ signatures** (`cppsig`, `off|proven|inferred`, default `proven`;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/demangle/cppsig.rs`, the
  `DemangledFunction.applyTo` / "Apply Function Signatures" analog) is the
  *signature* half of demangling, and the first consumer of the full c++filt form
  the module has always been able to produce. Where the DWARF arm above needs
  debug info, this one needs only the mangled symbol — which is what a **stripped**
  C++ shared library still exports through `.dynsym` — so the two are
  complementary, and where both reach a function the DWARF prototype (ground truth)
  is applied last and wins over the demangled one (a declaration).
  The declaration is parsed out of the demangled *string*, as upstream's
  `GnuDemanglerParser` does: the last depth-0 parenthesis group is the parameter
  list, the last depth-0 token before it is the qualified name, and a trailing
  `const`/`volatile`/`&`/`&&` is the cv/ref qualifier. Each declared parameter maps
  to a pointer of any depth, a primitive (at its LP64/ILP32 width and with the
  sign C++ gives it, so `char16_t` is `unsigned short`), or — as a POINTEE only —
  a named opaque structure carrying the bare innermost class name (upstream's
  placeholder structure). An aggregate passed **by value**, an array, a function pointer, a
  pointer-to-member or an overloaded operator refuses the whole signature: the
  mangling carries no layout, and a wrong width shifts every following parameter.
  The **return type is deliberately not applied**. Itanium encodes one only for a
  template function, so upstream returns null and keeps whatever the analysis
  recovered; unlace expresses that as a prototype with no `outtype`, which the drive
  reads as "lock the INPUT half only" and leaves return recovery running (04 §4.2).
  What makes this a three-valued option rather than a flag is the **implicit object
  parameter**: Itanium mangles a static member function exactly like a non-static
  one and like a namespaced free function, and inventing a `this` that is not there
  shifts every parameter rather than merely losing precision. `proven` therefore
  applies only the shapes the mangling *entails* — a constructor, a destructor, a
  cv-/ref-qualified member (all three take `this`), an unqualified global name, and
  the MSVC forms, which state the access specifier, `static`, and the calling
  convention outright. `inferred` additionally decides the ambiguous nested names
  from class evidence mined out of the binary's own symbols: a scope that owns a
  constructor, a destructor, a cv-qualified member or a `_ZTV`/`_ZTI`/`_ZTS` symbol
  is a class, so its members take `this`; a scope with no such witness is a
  namespace, so its functions do not. This reading refuses a 32-bit MSVC
  `__thiscall` member — that ABI passes `this` in ECX rather than as ordinary
  argument 0 — and reads an MSVC name only off a defined symbol; the MSVC arm
  below replaces it for MSVC names. Like the DWARF arm the
  pass runs at `load file`, so both certainty tiers are computed there and stashed
  apart, and the mode selects which of them the analysis commit applies.
  Three more shapes are read (unlace, after IDA's `guess_tinfo`): a scope that is
  always a namespace (`std`, `std::__1`, `std::__cxx11`, `__gnu_cxx`,
  `__cxxabiv1`, `boost` and a few more; IDA's `CPP_NAMESPACES`) proves a function
  nested directly in it takes no `this`, so `proven` applies it; an
  `operator new` / `operator delete` (global or class-scope, both static) parses
  with `void *` as the return of the allocation forms; and a gcc
  `[clone .localalias]` or `[clone .lto_priv.N]` suffix is dropped because those
  copies keep the signature, while `.constprop`, `.isra`, `.part` and `.cold`
  clones, whose signature differs, stay refused. While `cppsig` is not `off`,
  `libproto` also parks `void *(size_t[, ...])` / `void(void *[, size_t])` on the
  imported Itanium allocation functions (`_Znwm`, `_Znam`, `_ZdlPv`, `_ZdlPvm`,
  their `nothrow_t` and `align_val_t` forms and the 32-bit `j` spellings), so a
  `T *p = operator new(n)` no longer needs a cast. On an i386 System V ELF a
  defined function whose last instruction is `ret $4` pops a hidden struct-return
  pointer the mangled parameter list never spells, so a `void *rethidden`
  parameter is put in front (IDA's `func_has_stkframe_hole` test, read off the
  function's own epilogue): `_Z2mkii` reads `mk(void *rethidden,int a1,int a2)`
  instead of the shifted `mk(int a0,int a1)`.
- **Template class spelling** (`cppclassargs`, `on|off`, default `off`;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/demangle/cppsig.rs` `this_class`). The
  `this` of a demangled member function is typed by the class it belongs to. The
  parse keeps two names: `class`, the bare template-stripped class (`vector`), and
  `scope`, the whole enclosing scope (`std::vector<int, std::allocator<int> >`).
  Off, the `this` record is the bare class, as before. On, and only when the
  scope's last component carries template arguments, the record is named by the
  whole scope, so each instance is its own class (`std::vector<int, std::allocator<int> >`). A non-template class, every
  parameter type and the function name are unchanged. With `cppshortnames` on the
  printer shortens the record name to `std::vector<int> *this`. The standard
  container names (issue #1343, the archived `cpp_stl` recogniser) are the
  spelling `cppshortnames` already gives; this option supplies the template
  arguments it needs.
- **MSVC declarations** (`msvcsig`, always on, applied only while `cppsig` is
  not `off`;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/demangle/msvcsig.rs`, the
  signature half of Ghidra's `MicrosoftDemanglerAnalyzer`) reads an MSVC-mangled
  name as the full declaration it is, and reads it off the **PE imports** and the
  **PE exports** as well as off defined symbols. A linked PE keeps no symbol
  table, so on a DLL the export directory is the only place a
  `__declspec(dllexport)` member's declaration survives: an MSVC-mangled export
  whose address lies in a code section is read as a defined function at that
  address (`?SendFrame@CUsbCanDriver@@QAEHPAUcan_frame@@I@Z` gives
  `CUsbCanDriver::SendFrame` its ECX `this`, its `can_frame *` and its `int`
  return), and a data or vftable export is not. The Itanium reading above sees only `file.symbols()` and
  `file.dynamic_symbols()`, and a PE import lives in the import table, so a call
  through the IAT to `?IsValid@Arr@@QAEHXZ` was named `Arr::IsValid` and had no
  prototype: the `this` that MSVC passes in ECX was dropped, a hidden return
  pointer was left as the call's only argument, and the arguments a callee did
  not claim were handed to the next call (a copy constructor took the four pushes
  meant for the call after it). Unlike an Itanium name an MSVC name states the
  access specifier, `static`, the calling convention, the return type and every
  parameter type, so the arm decides five things from it. The **convention**: on
  32-bit x86 (a PE or COFF image) the stated `__cdecl`, `__stdcall`, `__thiscall`
  or `__fastcall` names the prototype model the pieces are laid out for, so a
  member takes `this` in ECX and a `__cdecl` callee leaves its arguments for the
  caller to pop; any other platform keeps its one default convention, and a
  convention with no model of its own in the spec (only an alias of the default)
  drops the declaration at the commit. **`this`**: a member that is not `static`
  takes one as argument 0. The **return type** is applied, which Itanium cannot
  offer; a constructor or destructor states none and keeps return recovery. The
  **hidden return pointer**: a class, struct or union returned by value comes back
  through a pointer the caller passes after `this`, and the callee returns that
  pointer in EAX — but not always, since MSVC returns a trivially copyable
  aggregate of 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes from a free or `static` function in EDX:EAX and
  the name gives neither the size nor the triviality. The pointer is placed only
  where it is certain: for every non-static member (which always returns a class
  indirectly), and for any function whose class the image proves non-trivial by
  defining or importing its destructor (`??1`), a vftable (`??_7`), a deleting
  destructor (`??_G`/`??_E`) or a constructor that takes arguments (`??0`, a copy,
  move or user constructor) — a trivial special member is never emitted, so its
  symbol cannot exist. A default constructor is not a witness, because one that
  only runs member initializers is emitted for a class MSVC still returns in
  registers; and a free function returning a class with no witness is refused.
  The **parameters**: a primitive (at the MSVC width: `long` is 4 bytes, `wchar_t`
  2, `long double` 8), a pointer, a reference or a function pointer is placed. A
  class, struct, union or enum passed **by value** has a width the name does not
  give — MSVC copies it into the outgoing argument area at its own size — so on an
  **import** declared `__cdecl` the parameters before it are placed and the rest of
  the list is left open, the way a variadic declaration leaves it (the caller pops,
  so the open tail claims nothing about the stack), and everywhere else the
  declaration is refused: a callee-pops convention would claim a stack adjustment
  that depends on the missing size, and a defined function would lose the
  parameters its own body recovers. Each declaration is checked whole before any
  type is built, so a refused one leaves nothing in the type factory. Overloaded
  operators, which the Itanium reading refuses for its bracket-depth parse, are
  read here (`operator<<`, `operator()`, `operator new`, conversions), since the
  parameter list is found by matching parentheses from the end and an MSVC name
  states its `this` outright; special names (`` `vftable' ``, adjustor thunks),
  data symbols, function templates and the `__vectorcall`/`__clrcall` conventions
  are refused. At the commit an MSVC prototype is parked by entry address on every
  address the import resolver names (the IAT slot and each `FF 25` thunk), its
  model is recorded against that address
  (`crates/unlace-middle/src/infra/architecture.rs
  (Architecture::set_function_prototype_model_at)`), and it is also locked onto the
  function symbol as the prototype-bearing `TypeCode` a `--assert prototype`
  directive would lock (04 §4.1). The lock is what reaches a 32-bit IAT call:
  `ActionDefaultParams` sees the target of a `call [abs32]` as a temporary its
  flow has not linked to the slot yet, and `ActionDeindirect` later merges the
  prototype `query_function` reads off the symbol, so a prototype parked only as
  pieces is not seen there (`ActionDefaultParams` gives such a call the
  parameters of its parked pieces through the slot query of 04 §4.1 instead). The commit also records each locked address, and the
  flow makes a call through one of those slots direct before the spec is built
  (02 §2.1), so the locked prototype is copied in at flow instead of costing the
  function a restart. Measured on the local RE-challenge corpus, 175 distinct
  32-bit and 229 distinct 64-bit MSVC PE images that import MSVC-mangled names
  (the `msvcp` iostream and string API in most): calls printed with no arguments
  fall from 13,819 to 11,302 and from 18,858 to 17,355, 5.4% and 8.3% of the
  functions change, and total decompile CPU time moves by +0.3% and -0.5%.
  A parameter after a by-value class is not placed by the declaration, and where
  MSVC constructs that class in its outgoing slot through a pointer — a copy
  constructor, or a call returning into the slot — the call-site recovery refuses
  every slot above the one whose address was taken. So for such an import (one
  by-value class, no `...`) the arm also parks the whole declaration, the class a
  placeholder, and records every entry that builds an object at an address it is
  handed: a 32-bit `__thiscall` constructor (`??0`) and an applied declaration
  returning a class by value; `msvcbyval.rs` (04 §4.4) sizes the class at each call
  from the caller's cleanup. LOSS: where it declines, those arguments render as stores before the
  call (`MakeStack(a1)`, after `Arr::Arr((Arr *)&v1,a2)`, keeps only its hidden
  return pointer).
- **Source-language detection**
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/sourcelang/mod.rs
  (detect_compiler)`, the `SourceLanguageAnalyzer` detection half) is asked
  for its verdict several times per load: by the loader's language-id choice,
  by pass selection, for the engine fact below, by the `addrtakenentry` gate
  and by the CLI's runtime hints. So it reads the image in place. The PE arm
  tests `.comment` and `.rdata` as one NUL-delimited record stream (a record
  left open at the end of `.comment` continues into `.rdata`) without copying
  either, and decodes only the records around a substring hit of the record
  it looks for. On a 20 MB `.rdata` that is a few milliseconds per ask, where
  copying the section and splitting every record cost a quarter of a second.
  Detection shapes the pass list: `rustc version` records in
  `.comment` or Rust-mangled symbols → the Rust no-return list;
  `.go.buildinfo`/`.note.go.buildid` (any format's spelling) → the Go list plus
  the pclntab pass; a Swift 5 reflection-metadata section (any format's
  spelling of the namespace: `__swift5_…` on Mach-O, `swift5_…` on ELF,
  `.sw5…` in a PE), a Swift-mangled symbol (`$s`/`$S`/`_T0`, held to the
  scheme's next token so an assembler local like `$LN3` is not one), or a
  Swift runtime entry point in either symbol table (`swift_retain`,
  `swift_release`, …, so a stripped binary importing `libswiftCore` still
  reads as Swift) → `Compiler::Swift`, checked after Rust and before the
  toolchain conveniences, and on Mach-O before the Apple-platform fallback
  that would otherwise claim every Swift image for clang. Nothing gates on
  `Swift` yet — a Swift binary's pass set is pinned byte-identical to a
  clang one — the verdict exists so the engine fact below is right and the
  language packs (docs/multilang.md) have a plane to gate on. PE detection
  reads the MSVC Rich header / MinGW `GCC:` records, Mach-O the
  `LC_BUILD_VERSION` family. The `Gcc`/`Clang` values are a unlace convenience
  nothing gates on.

  A Go **PE** names nothing: Go's Windows linker emits only `.text`, `.rdata`,
  `.data` (plus the `.pdata`/`.idata`/`.reloc` bookkeeping), merging the
  build-info blob into the head of `.data` and the pclntab into `.rdata`, so
  the section-name test above can never fire on one. The PE arm therefore
  reads content, and asks two questions
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/sourcelang/mod.rs
  (detect_compiler_pe)`). First, is there a build-info blob where Go's own
  `go version` looks for it
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/loader/gobuildinfo.rs
  (pe_buildinfo_blob)`): the first writable initialized-data section, at a
  16-byte-aligned offset, holding a header that validates whole
  (`blob_is_buildinfo`) — the 14-byte `\xff Go buildinf:` magic, a pointer
  size of 4 or 8, no unknown flag bits, and a version string (`go1.x` or
  `devel …`, printable) that decodes, inline after zero padding since go1.18 or
  through the header's pointer before. The magic string alone, or a header
  shape with no version behind it, is not evidence. The scan visits only the
  aligned slots, so it costs one byte compare per 16 bytes of `.data` (1.5 ms
  on a 13.7 MB `.data`); on an internally linked Go image the blob is the
  section's first object. Second, is there a pclntab in **read-only** data
  whose table resolves and which the image's own `moduledata` names
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/pclntab/mod.rs
  (readonly_table_present, moduledata_anchored)`): a pointer-aligned record in
  writable data whose first word is the header's address and whose next
  pointer is the name table's (go1.16+, `pcHeader` then `funcnametab`) or,
  after the blob's length and capacity, the functab's (go1.2–go1.15,
  `pclntable` then `ftab`). The linker always writes that record for the
  module's own table. A Go image a C program merely carries as data has none
  pointing at where the copy sits, whichever section holds it: a payload in
  `.data` has a valid blob but its table is in writable data, and one carried
  twice (a const copy in `.rdata`, a writable one in `.data`) has a blob and
  a read-only table whose only `moduledata` names the address the table had in
  its own image. A table whose magic was overwritten is counted when the
  `moduledata` record describes it whole (`gomoduledata.rs (locate)`,
  below) and its functab lies in read-only data. Both questions must hold. The arm runs first, as on every format, and
  returns before the `.rdata` toolchain-record scan the later arms do.
  Nothing else changes for a non-Go PE: its verdict is the same as before. The
  same blob lookup (`buildinfo_blob`) gives the version-keyed `goreg` shells
  their toolchain on a PE.

  Every consumer acts on the **effective** verdict
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/sourcelang/mod.rs
  (effective_compiler, effective_compiler_bytes)`): the `UNLACE_SOURCELANG`
  environment override when set, else detection. The override is the
  `sourcelang` option (`auto|c|rust|go|swift`, default `auto`), and it travels
  as an environment variable because pass
  selection happens inside `load file`, upstream of every per-function
  `option` command, so the CLI binds it to the environment before loading
  (`crates/unlace-cli/src/loadtime.rs (binding)`). The engine's copy
  of the verdict is `Architecture::source_lang_detected`, written once at
  `load file` (`crates/unlace-console/src/engine.rs
  (bootstrap_from_object_with_isa)`) as a `SourceLang`
  (`crates/unlace-middle/src/p0_knowledge/sourcelang.rs`), with
  the console `option sourcelang` arm layering a per-run force on top
  (`Architecture::source_lang` reports the effective value, and the catalog's
  `current` reports the option — `auto` until a run forces a language). The
  per-function rules that used to read the `source_is_rust`/`source_is_go`
  bools (`rustabi auto`, the frame-reload rule's Go stand-down) read that one fact now.
  Forcing a language never invents facts (forcing `go` on a non-Go image
  enables the pclntab pass, which finds no table); it changes which
  language-gated rules may act. It is also the escape hatch when detection
  misses: a Go PE whose build-info blob was wiped still has its pclntab in
  `.rdata`, and `--option sourcelang go` registers the Go passes, which find
  it.
  "Rust-mangled" is decided by the mangling grammar, not by a prefix
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/sourcelang/mod.rs
  (is_rust_mangled)`). The v0 scheme spells a symbol `_R` followed by a path, and a
  path opens with one of the tags `C M X Y N I B` — but `_R` is not private to
  Rust. Mach-O prepends a platform underscore to every symbol it carries, so an
  ordinary C function named `Run`, `Read` or `RC4_set_key` is spelled `_Run`,
  `_Read`, `_RC4_set_key` in the image and opens the same two bytes. The name is
  therefore parsed, by the same `rustc_demangle` the demangle pass hands it to, and
  a name that does not parse is not evidence: `_RC4_set_key` gets as far as
  declaring a four-byte crate named `set_` and is then left holding `key`, which is
  no instantiating-crate path. On top of that the detector knows which formats
  carry the platform underscore
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/sourcelang/mod.rs
  (is_rust_mangled_in)`): on Mach-O rustc's own v0 symbols read `__R…`, so a
  single-underscore `_R…` there is a C name however well it parses. The demangle
  pass keeps the format-agnostic test, since what it holds is a bare name with no
  image behind it. The strictness is load-bearing rather than tidy: `Rustc`
  selects the Rust output language for the whole binary, turns `rustabi auto` on
  and widens the no-return list, so a single misread symbol re-languages a C
  program.
- **Call fixups** (`callfixup`,
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/callfixup/mod.rs`, the
  `CallFixupAnalyzer` analog): a function whose name matches a cspec call-fixup
  `<target>` (the `-pg` `mcount`/`__fentry__` stubs) is tagged with the fixup's
  inject id so the engine replaces the CALL with the fixup body; guarded by
  upstream's only-if-no-fixup-set check so a hand-applied fixup is never clobbered.
  The same name match runs when a caller names a function with
  `--define-function` / `function bounds … as NAME`, so declaring a stripped
  helper's CRT name installs its fixup too. A relocatable object's undefined
  symbols carry no type — a kernel module's `__fentry__` and
  `__x86_return_thunk` are `NOTYPE UND` — and the loader binds each one a call
  reaches as an extern function, so an untyped undefined symbol is matched like
  a FUNC one; without that the module's every function opened with
  `__fentry__();` and ended its tail jump in `__x86_return_thunk(); // tail-call`.
  On a PE32 i386 image (target-gated, always on, inert elsewhere) the pass also
  recognizes the statically linked MSVC float-to-integer helpers by their bytes
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/callfixup/msvcftolsig.rs`),
  because a stripped image gives the name-keyed `unlace_msvcftol` fixup nothing to
  match and every `fld …; call sub_XXXX` then loses its x87 operand. The
  signatures are the complete instruction streams of the VS2005 CRT objects:
  `ftol.obj` (`__ftol`), the x87 tail of `ftol2.obj` (`__ftol2`, matched alone
  for images that link only it), and, when that tail sits 0x36 bytes after the
  object's head with its two relocated `___sse2_available` operands wildcarded,
  the head's `__ftol2_sse`, `__ftol2_pentium4` and `__ftol2_sse_excpt` entries.
  Each entry is committed as a function symbol under its CRT name (plus a
  placeholder rename for one another fact already installed) and as a call-fixup
  fact; a match only names and tags, and a near miss of any one byte is no match.
  On a little-endian ARM PE it also recognizes the Windows on ARM `/GS` helpers
  `__security_push_cookie` and `__security_pop_cookie` by their bytes
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/callfixup/armgscookiesig.rs`), with the
  `movw`/`movt` immediates of `__security_cookie`'s address masked out, as IDA 9.5's
  `arm.so` does. The push helper allocates the word below its caller's stack pointer that
  holds the scrambled cookie and returns with `sp` four bytes lower; the pop helper checks
  and releases it. `ARM_win.cspec`'s `security_push_cookie` and `security_pop_cookie`
  fixups model exactly that stack effect (`sp = sp - 4`, `sp = sp + 4`); as plain calls
  every stack reference of the caller after the push was four bytes off, and its first
  stack argument read as its second. With the fixups the cookie word and its check leave
  the C, as `msvcstackguard` removes the x86 cookie.
  The same pass names the MSVC 64-bit arithmetic helpers the `unlace_arithhelpers`
  fixups target (`__allmul`, `__alldiv`, `__allrem`, `__alldvrm`, `__aulldiv`,
  `__aullrem`, `__aulldvrm`, `__allshl`, `__allshr`, `__aullshr`) by their complete
  instruction streams up to the last `ret`
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/callfixup/msvcarithsig.rs`); the
  objects carry no relocation, so nothing is wildcarded. Without it a stripped
  i386 PE prints each `long long` multiply, divide or shift as a call with four
  32-bit words.
  On a 32-bit ARM image the pass likewise recognizes libgcc's Thumb-1 switch
  helpers (`__gnu_thumb1_case_uqi`, `_sqi`, `_uhi`, `_shi`, `_si`) by their
  instructions
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/callfixup/thumb1casesig.rs`).
  gcc compiles a Thumb-1 switch (ARMv6-M, or `-Os`) as `bl helper` followed by
  the case table, and the helper returns into the case the index in `r0`
  selects; the cspec's `switch*_r0` fixups model that, but only by name, so in a
  stripped image the call read as an ordinary call returning into the table and
  every case was lost. Each helper is a fixed routine of nine to eleven Thumb
  instructions (`libgcc/config/arm/lib1funcs.S`), matched whole at a halfword
  boundary (big-endian images are read both ways, since BE8 code is stored
  little-endian), and each hit becomes a function symbol under the libgcc name,
  a rename of its `sub_` name and a call-fixup fact, which the commit installs
  on every global function of that name. The word helper's fixup
  (`switch32_si_r0`) adds the table entry to the word-aligned table address and
  stays in Thumb state, as the helper does (`adds r0,r1; mov lr,r0; mov pc,lr`);
  the vendored body scaled the entry by four and added it to the return
  address, which sent the cases to the wrong addresses. armcc's
  `__ARM_common_switch8` is recognized the same way in its three forms (two
  Thumb-1 bodies, saving `r4,r5` or `r0-r3`, and the Thumb-2 one with `ite`):
  each reads the table size from the byte before the table, clamps the index in
  `r3` to it and branches to the table plus twice the entry, which the
  `switch8_r3` fixup models.
  The same module names the ARM-mode helpers that Apple's libgcc and armcc call with `blx`
  from Thumb code (`___switch8`, `___switchu8`, `___switch16`, `___switch32` and three forms
  of `__rt_switch8`, the forms IDA 9.5's `arm.so` lists), matched as whole instruction words
  at a word boundary. Each reads the table size at `lr-1` (a byte, halfword or word), clamps
  the index to it (the last entry is the default) and branches to `lr` plus twice a byte or
  halfword entry, or plus a word entry. The ARM cspecs model the `r0`-indexed ones with the
  `switch*_r0_sized` fixups and add `__rt_switch8` to `switch8_r3`'s targets; without them each
  call read as an ordinary call returning into its table, so only the first case was decompiled.
- **Linux kernel `__bug_table`** (`kernelbug`, always on, inert without the
  section; `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/kernelbug/mod.rs
  (KernelBugPass)`): the kernel's `WARN_ON`/`BUG_ON` macros plant a trap (`ud2`,
  AArch64 `brk #0x800`) and describe it in a `struct bug_entry` — the trap's
  address, under `CONFIG_DEBUG_BUGVERBOSE` the source file and line, and a flags
  word whose bit 0 (`BUGFLAG_WARNING`) says the handler resumes after the trap.
  The pass reads every entry into a `KernelBugSite` the flow consumes (chapter
  02, `kernelbug`). The entry layout is not declared in the image, so it is
  recovered from the section itself. A module (`ET_REL`) keeps
  `.rela__bug_table`, read on the rebased view: the relocations whose target is
  an executable section are the `bug_addr` fields, their spacing is the entry
  size, and the other relocations inside an entry are its pointer fields (a
  32-bit self-relative displacement under `CONFIG_GENERIC_BUG_RELATIVE_POINTERS`,
  an absolute 64-bit pointer otherwise). A linked image (`vmlinux`) is probed,
  even when it keeps its relocations (an x86-64 `vmlinux` links with
  `--emit-relocs`, whose offsets are addresses, not section offsets): the sizes
  8, 12 and 16 are tried in turn and the first
  under which every `bug_addr` lands in executable bytes wins — under a wrong
  size the field read is a string displacement or a line/flags word, which lands
  outside the code — and a field is a pointer when every entry's value lands in a
  non-executable section. A `bug_addr` need not be a trap: a 7.x kernel's `WARN()`
  with arguments is a `call __WARN_trap` the table also names, which the flow
  leaves alone. Behind the pointers sit `line` (two bytes, only with a `file`)
  and `flags`. With two pointer fields the second is `file` (the first is 7.x's
  `format`); with one, it is `file` when the string it points at is a source path
  (`lib/a.c`) and `format` otherwise, which is the one case the layout alone
  does not decide. A layout is kept only when `flags` ends the entry, before at
  most its alignment padding, so a stride with room no field explains (a
  12-byte entry whose second word is no string pointer) is declined rather than
  read with a displacement standing in for the flags. Before Linux 5.19
  (`69505e3d9a39`) a self-relative `file` counted from the start of the entry
  rather than from the field, so read the newer way it lands four bytes into the
  path; the older reading is taken when it puts more `file` fields on the first
  byte of a string, over 64 entries spread evenly through the table (a linked
  image keeps its entries in link order, and the first string of a merged
  string blob can follow binary data with no NUL before it, so the leading
  entries alone can mislead the vote). A table no size explains yields
  nothing. Section and code lookups are binary searches, so the work is linear
  in the table whatever the section count. The 14,223 entries of
  a 7.3 x86-64 `vmlinux` read in under 0.2 s. Committed sorted by trap address
  onto `Architecture::kernel_bug_sites`.
- **Embedded images and archives** (`blobs on|off`, default on;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/blobs/mod.rs (BlobPass)`): a
  program that ships a logo, an icon set or a packed resource stores the whole
  file in a data section, where it showed only as the string fragments of its
  header (`PNG`, `IHDR`, `IDATx`) and as a bare address in the code that hands
  it out. The pass searches every mapped, file-backed section for nine magic
  numbers (`blobs/mod.rs (scan)`) and keeps a candidate only when its container
  structure walks to its end, which is also what gives the exact length. A PNG
  is its chunks from `IHDR` to `IEND` with every chunk CRC-32 checked and an
  `IDAT` present; a JPEG its marker segments to `EOI` after a frame header and
  a scan, skipping the entropy-coded bytes; a GIF its blocks to the trailer
  after at least one image; a BMP a header whose file size equals the pixel
  array its DIB header describes; an ICO a directory whose images follow it
  back to back, each a PNG or a DIB of the entry's dimensions
  (`blobs/images.rs`). A zip is found from its end-of-central-directory
  record, whose directory must sit right before it and name a local header for
  every entry, so a stub in front of the archive is not part of it and a zip64
  archive is not reported; a gzip member is inflated into a discarded buffer to
  check the trailer's CRC-32 and length, the one kind whose length cannot be
  known otherwise; an xz stream needs a footer and an index whose CRC-32s match
  and whose index sums to the bytes between header and index; a zstd frame is
  its frame and block headers to the last block, with a compressed block whose
  literals and sequences headers fit it, or raw and RLE blocks that sum to the
  declared content size (`blobs/archives.rs`). No pixels are decoded. A
  truncated file is not a blob, and a file stored inside an earlier-starting
  one (a PNG in a zip, a PNG in an ICO) is not reported separately. The image
  is hostile input: every read is bounds-checked and the bytes one scan may
  walk are capped at sixteen times the section, after which it returns what it
  has. The commit (`crates/unlace-console/src/blobdata.rs
  (commit)`) runs after every other data source, so a DWARF global or a
  symbol-table object keeps the address; where nothing covers it the blob
  becomes `<kind>_<addr>` (`png_3c0`), an `unsigned char[length]` with name and
  type locked, and the string facts that fall inside any blob are not planted.
  Each blob's first address is also recorded for constant-pointer recovery
  (chapter 05, `blobs`). `unlace blobs` runs the same scan as an inventory, with
  the functions that reference each file.
- **ARM EHABI unwind index** (ARM32 ELF only;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/entry/armexidx.rs (scan)`):
  an ARM32 ELF carries no `.eh_frame`. Its unwinder searches `.ARM.exidx`, a
  table of 8-byte entries sorted by address: word 0 is a prel31 offset to a
  function's first instruction, word 1 is `1` (`EXIDX_CANTUNWIND`), an inline
  compact description (bit 31 set), or a prel31 offset to an `.ARM.extab`
  entry. In the generic model that entry starts with a prel31 offset to its
  personality routine (bit 31 clear), then one word-aligned run of unwind
  opcodes whose first byte counts the additional words, then the LSDA that
  `itaniumeh` decodes (chapter 02). Every entry that can unwind is a function
  start, bounded by the next entry's start, and joins the entry-discovery
  oracles (the `.eh_frame` FDE oracle's counterpart). A `CANTUNWIND` entry only
  bounds its predecessor: the linker writes one at the end of each code
  section. Bit 0 of a start is the Thumb bit, but a table whose relocations were
  made against section symbols leaves it clear on Thumb code, so the
  instruction set is decided per start: Thumb when the bit is set or the
  address is not a multiple of four; otherwise A32 when nothing in the image is
  known to be Thumb, Thumb when something is and no sized function symbol has
  an even address, and **left out** when the image holds both, because a start
  decoded in the wrong set is a function of garbage. A Thumb start paints
  `TMode=1` over its own `[start, next start)` range.
- **x87 intrinsics** (`x87intrinsics`, always on, i386 only;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/protos/x87intrinsics.rs
  (X87IntrinsicPass)`): binds the MSVC one-operand x87 math intrinsics to the
  `__unlace_x87unary` model and the two-operand ones (`__CIpow`, `__CIatan2`,
  `__CIfmod`) to `__unlace_x87binary`, and locks their signature (chapter 04). A function
  the image names `__CIsin` (linked) or `_CIsin` (imported) and so on is bound
  by name, through the loaded image's function symbols so an object's
  undefined externs and a PE's import thunks count; a bare `CIsin` is not the
  CRT's spelling and is left alone. In a
  stripped PE32 i386 image the VS2005 CRT objects `sqrt.obj`, `sin.obj`,
  `cos.obj`, `tan.obj`, `log.obj`, `log10.obj`, `asin.obj`, `acos.obj`,
  `atan.obj`, `pow.obj` and `87fmod.obj` are recognized whole, without storing
  their code: each signature
  is a 16-byte anchor inside the object, the object's length, the ranges its
  relocations patch, and an FNV-1a 64-bit hash of the object with those ranges
  zeroed. At most 64 hits of one anchor are examined per section (an anchor
  opens each object once, and the eight objects sharing one occur at most once
  each), so a section tiled with an anchor costs a scan, not a hash per hit. An
  anchor hit whose window hashes to a signature names the
  intrinsic entry (bound) and the object's C entry (`sin`, which keeps its
  stack argument). The objects of `sin` and `cos` differ in four unpatched
  bytes, `log` and `log10` in three, so the whole object is what tells them
  apart. `87ctriga.obj` (`atan2`) is two ten-byte `mov edx, <table>; jmp` stubs, too little
  to hash: the dispatcher object `87cdisp.obj` is recognized the same way, and
  a stub that jumps to its `__cintrindisp2` and is not `fmod`'s (the only other
  object that does) is `__CIatan2`, with the stub before it, loading the same
  table and jumping to `__ctrandisp2`, its C entry `atan2`. The stubs are
  collected in one pass per section, and anything but exactly one such stub is
  not the CRT's shape and names nothing, so an image of many stubs costs one
  linear scan. On a VS2005 game
  executable this names eight one-operand and three two-operand intrinsics;
  all 409 one-operand calls in the 207 functions that make one get their
  operand, where 351 printed without it, and the 43 two-operand calls in their
  42 wrappers get both.

The format- and language-gated recoveries (each registered only for its format, so
every other binary's pass list is byte-identical to before the pass existed):

- **Go runtime types** (`gotypes`, Go-detected binaries only, always on;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/gotypes/mod.rs (GoTypesPass)`):
  phase 1 of the `docs/multilang.md` W3 Go provider. A stripped Go binary
  carries no DWARF, but the linker bakes the runtime's type graph in, and the
  pass walks it: moduledata is found WITHOUT symbols (its first field points at
  the pclntab header, which `locate_header` already finds on a stripped image;
  the anchor is the data-section word holding that address whose next three
  words parse as the `funcnametab` slice — go1.26+ emits `firstmoduledata`
  into its own `.go.module` section, which the scan covers, and a PE folds it
  into `.data` with the rest of the data segment), and the type
  metadata is then found by CROSS-VALIDATION inside the moduledata window in
  whichever of its two historical forms is present — never by hardcoded field
  offsets. Through go1.26: the `types`/`etypes` pair plus the `typelinks`
  slice, sampled entries required to decode as plausible `_type` records.
  From go1.27 the slice is gone: moduledata carries `types, typedesclen,
  etypes` and the records sit consecutively in `[types + ptrSize, types +
  typedesclen)`, enumerated by advancing each record's own descriptor size
  (`internal/abi.Type::DescriptorSize` — the per-kind wrapper, the optional
  uncommon block and its methods, and the kind's trailing arrays), the walk
  accepted only when records decode back to back and refused whole on the
  first divergence. That is what lets one implementation hold across
  go1.18..go1.27's layout drift (verified under go1.22, go1.25, go1.26 and go1.27;
  the e2e gate is `verify_gotypes`). Typelinks hold the pointer forms
  interface conversion reaches (`*main.Point`), so the walk follows a
  pointer record's elem to the named struct pointee. It interns
  package-qualified named struct shells (fields at their recorded offsets,
  zero-size embedded markers dropped, overlapping or over-extent layouts
  refused whole). The build-info version
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/loader/gobuildinfo.rs (go_version)`,
  read from the inline go1.18+ blob or the pointer form go1.13..go1.17
  binaries carry) selects the metadata encodings that changed before go1.19:
  a Go 1.9..1.18 version selects the older `offset << 1 | embedded`
  struct-field encoding (the importer shifts the word before checking the
  field extent; Go 1.19 and later use byte offsets directly), and a Go 1.16
  or older version selects the big-endian `u16` name length that preceded
  the go1.17 varint, which is what lets a go1.16 image's descriptors decode
  at all. An absent or unrecognized version retains the direct-offset and
  varint interpretations; the importer never guesses from a plausible
  shifted layout.
  The same bounds and overlap checks apply after decoding. Stripped amd64
  and arm64 tests include an embedded pointer field at a nonzero offset.
  Named struct fields held by value are completed before their enclosing
  structs. The bounded iterative walk in
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/gotypes/structorder.rs (complete_order)`
  follows their descriptors even
  when the child has no independent typelink. Pointer fields do not impose a
  layout dependency. Named shells use the factory's completion link, so pointers
  created before field import resolve to the completed record's size and fields.
  This includes self-references and mutually recursive named structs; an invalid
  layout leaves the linked shell incomplete. Cyclic value layouts and malformed
  descriptors stay opaque. A field whose factory type is still incomplete but whose metadata
  declares a nonzero size refuses the enclosing layout instead of disappearing
  as a zero-size marker. True zero-size fields retain the existing treatment.
  The pass also interns the well-known header shells `go.string`/`go.slice`/
  `go.iface`/`go.eface` with their `LangFacet` records
  (`crates/unlace-middle/src/p0_knowledge/langfacet.rs`). The
  shell interning is OUTPUT-NEUTRAL by construction — nothing binds a shell
  to a variable by itself — the knowledge is for the type surfaces and the
  consumers (the descriptor globals below, then interface dispatch and
  signature recovery). Deliberately out of
  scope: itab/method resolution, generic instantiations, map/chan internals,
  named non-struct aliases and big-endian images. Little-endian 32-bit images
  use pointer-width reads through
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/gotypes/layout.rs (GoImage)`.
  Their base type record is 32 bytes, moduledata and slice words are four bytes,
  and each struct field occupies three words. Header shells and pointer types
  use four-byte words as well. A build-info version identifying Go 1.18 through
  1.26 selects the 32-bit typelinks path. Go 1.26 keeps the typelinks and
  itablinks slices when `firstmoduledata` moves into `.go.module`.
  Go 1.27 selects the consecutive descriptor path and uses the pointer width
  for alignment, wrapper fields,
  slices and function type pointers. Method entries stay fixed-width, and the
  Go 1.27 map wrapper uses ten words plus one aligned flags slot. A partial
  final descriptor refuses the region. Unknown versions are refused on
  32-bit targets.
  Stripped i386 and ARM tests cover integer, string, embedded-pointer and nested
  value fields, with the existing amd64 and arm64 tests as controls.
  Nothing binds the shells to a variable yet, so they do not change the
  decompiled code. Interning happens at
  `load file`, the walk is bounded (20,000 typelinks), and the
  pass registers before `gopclntab`, preserving its appended-last contract.
  Go permits named pointer types that refer to themselves, such as
  `type Pointer *Pointer`, and mutually recursive pointer definitions. The runtime
  field importer in
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/gotypes/fieldtypes.rs`
  walks pointer descriptors iteratively, retaining each distinct pointer layer.
  A repeated descriptor address, an unreadable target or the 64-pointer expansion
  limit ends the chain with an opaque `void` pointee. This retains the field's
  machine-word size and the following fields' offsets without recursing forever.
  Named struct pointees still resolve through the existing struct shells; ordinary
  scalar, string, slice and interface field mappings are unchanged. This is part of
  `gotypes`, correcting a loader crash rather than adding a separate option.

- **Go pclntab** (`gopclntab`, Go-detected binaries only, default-on;
  **Descriptor globals** (`gotypeglobals`, on by default;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/gotypes/typeglobals.rs`):
  the first consumer of the harvest, riding the same walk. A Go binary's
  runtime metadata types two families of data objects outright — its own
  `_type` descriptors and the interface-dispatch tables (itabs) that bind
  them. A descriptor is a global of layout `internal/abi.Type` that
  Go's linker names `type:main.Point` / `type:*main.Point` / `type:[]uint8`;
  stripping deletes those symtab names while the records stay reachable
  through the moduledata. The typelinks (and the go1.27+ descriptor region)
  list the types interface conversion reaches; the types those are built
  from have descriptors of their own that allocation and reflection sites
  name just as often, so the located records are the roots of a walk over
  the type graph
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/gotypes/typeglobals.rs (reachable)`): `ptrToThis`, the
  element and key of an array, chan, map, pointer or slice, a func's
  parameters and results, an interface's method types and a struct's field
  types, bounded at 200,000 descriptors. Every reachable record (deduplicated
  by VMA, emitted in address order) becomes one typed-data fact: the record's
  VMA, the linker-spelling `type:<name>` symbol, and the `go.typedesc` shell.
  The name is the linker's
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/gotypes/typeglobals.rs (linker_name)`): a named
  type's package qualifier is the full import path from its
  `uncommontype.pkgPath` (`type:internal/poll.FD`, where the name record
  holds `poll.FD`), and a pointer, slice, array or map spelling is rebuilt
  from its elements' so the qualifier reaches it (`type:*internal/poll.FD`,
  `type:[]io/fs.DirEntry`); a func or chan type and an anonymous struct keep the
  record's spelling. A named map type's `pkgPath` is read past its map record,
  whose size follows the Go version: the swiss-table record from go1.24
  (`GoImage::swiss_maps`, set from the build-info version), the old buckets
  record before (`GoImage::map_record`). A pointer record genuinely starts with
  `*`; an extra-star name was already stripped by the record reader. The
  `gonewtype` client maps the symbol back to the interned record by
  dropping the directory part of a named type's own qualifier, before any
  type arguments (`geom.Box[example.com/q/store.T]` keeps its argument's
  path); a pointer, slice, array, map or func spelling is kept whole and
  refuses. The shell is the
  48/32-byte `abi.Type` base record at the harvest's own decode offsets
  (`Size_` through `PtrToThis`), spanning only the base record so the mapped
  extent never overlaps the next descriptor; runtime code walking a
  descriptor renders named field reads (`t->Kind_`). The global-name
  vocabulary is wider than the interning one (unnamed composites like
  `[]uint8` are kept — their spelled form is what an analyst searches for)
  but refuses anything with a non-graphic byte or interior whitespace
  (anonymous `struct { ... }` literals, `func(int) bool`), which would break
  the C document a symbol is printed into. The facts are produced at load,
  held in their own `AnalysisOutput` stream
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/pass.rs (go_type_globals)`), and the
  COMMIT is gated: the engine folds them into the typed-data stream
  (`typelock|namelock`, the `libctypes` arm) only when `gotypeglobals` is on,
  so `off` renders exactly what the provider alone renders, and a non-Go
  image produces no facts either way. This is what makes the harvested names
  APPEAR in emitted C: `runtime.newobject`, `convT*` and interface-conversion
  call sites name the type they manipulate instead of passing a bare
  `&DAT_<addr>` (e2e: `verify_gotypes`, the
  `stripped_go_descriptor_globals_render_in_c` two-pass gate).

  **Interface tables** (the itab leg of `gotypeglobals`, same gate;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/gotypes/itabs.rs`): each
  static `itab` the runtime lists binds one interface type to one concrete
  type and Go's linker names it `go:itab.<concrete>,<interface>`. The records
  sit in the `itablinks` pointer slice of moduledata (go1.18..go1.26) or, from
  go1.27, in the contiguous `[types + itaboffset, + itabsize)` region walked by
  each record's `internal/abi.ITab::Size()` — the parallel of the typelinks →
  descriptor-region change `locate_type_meta_descriptors` already handles —
  both located by cross-validation in the moduledata window (sampled records
  must decode, `Inter` interface-kind). The two type names come from the two
  descriptor ADDRESSES the record points at (`Inter` at offset 0, `Type` at
  offset 8), never a spelled name — the sound key, since a Go reflection name
  is not unique. Each becomes a NAME-only data symbol at the itab's VMA (not a typed
  object: an itab address is used polymorphically — passed to `getitab`,
  compared, stored into an interface word — so locking its global to a struct
  type demotes those uses and hides the symbol a reference renders, exactly
  how Go's own symtab names an itab), so an interface conversion renders
  `go:itab.main.Point,fmt.Stringer` instead of a bare `&DAT_<addr>`. An itab
  the image already names is left to that name, so the pass only ADDS the ones
  stripping removed. Both names are the linker's spellings (`linker_name`,
  full import paths: `go:itab.*internal/poll.FD,io.Writer`), so a stripped
  image's itab symbols match an unstripped build's byte for byte (e2e:
  `verify_gotypes::stripped_go_itab_renders_named`, green on the itablinks
  and the contiguous-region layouts).

  **Interface method slots** (`goitabcalls`, on by default;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/gotypes/itabtypes.rs (intern)`):
  every itab of one interface lays its `Fun` array out in the order of the
  interface descriptor's `Methods` slice (`Imethod {Name, Typ}` after the
  `Type` base and the `PkgPath` word, sorted by name), so one record per
  interface types all of them. On a 64-bit image the harvest reads the method
  names of every interface descriptor the graph walk reaches and every itab's
  `Inter`, and interns `go.itab.<interface>` (the linker spelling,
  `go.itab.io.Writer`): `inter`, `_type`, `hash`, then one `code *` slot per
  method at `24 + 8*i` named after it, with a `LangFacet::GoItab` facet naming
  the interface. A spelling whose descriptors disagree on the method list, an
  anonymous interface literal, an empty interface and a method name that is not
  an ASCII identifier (or is a header field's name) get no record. Interning
  binds nothing. With the option on, two consumers bind it. The Go DWARF
  signature (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/dwarf/godwarfsig/goiface.rs (input_types)`)
  takes a formal whose type is a nominal interface typedef chain over the
  `runtime.iface` storage, passed in the next two integer registers, as two
  inputs, `<name>_tab` typed as a pointer to the interface's record and
  `<name>_data` an opaque pointer; without the record the function keeps the
  inference it had. The printer
  (`crates/unlace-emit/src/p9_emit/goitabcall.rs (interface_method)`)
  prints a CALLIND whose target is a LOAD of a method slot of such a record
  (`PTRSUB` or `INT_ADD` of the record pointer and a constant at or past
  offset 24) as `Interface.Method(args)`, the receiver first:
  `main.Shape.Area(s_data)`. When the image's default prototype model is
  the Go register ABI (`abi-internal`), each slot whose method signature
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/gotypes/itabtypes.rs (method_pieces)`,
  read from the `Imethod.Typ` func descriptor) is all one-register scalars,
  integers and bool at their own width and the pointer-shaped kinds (pointer,
  unsafe pointer, chan, map, func) as an opaque pointer, with at most eight
  parameters, at most one result and no variadic tail, is a pointer to a
  function of that prototype under that model, the receiver (the data word,
  an opaque pointer) first; `ActionDeindirect` forces it on a call through a
  table typed by the record, so the call passes exactly those arguments. Any
  other slot is an untyped `code *` and the call keeps the arguments the
  call site recovers.
  The table pointer need not be typed: the printer also follows it back
  through copies and joins whose inputs all agree to a LOAD of the first word
  of an interface-typed field of a named struct, read through a chain of
  constant offsets from a pointer to the struct (`h->S.tab`, nested structs
  included). The harvest records those fields
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/gotypes/ifacefields.rs (register)`):
  for each named struct descriptor, the byte offset and interface of every
  field whose type descriptor is an interface, as a
  `LangFacet::GoInterfaceFields` facet on the struct's reflection and linker
  spellings, so it holds whether the harvest or DWARF built the layout. A name
  the harvest marked ambiguous, whose descriptors disagree, or that already
  carries a facet gets none.
  When the chain of offsets ends at the function's own receiver, which needs
  no type at all, the receiver supplies the struct: in a pointer method
  `pkg.(*T).M` (the name a stripped binary keeps in its pclntab) the x86-64
  input in `RAX`, directly or through copies, is the receiver, so a LOAD at
  a constant offset from it reads `pkg.T`'s field there, and `pkg.T`'s
  facet names the interface
  (`crates/unlace-emit/src/p9_emit/goitabcall.rs (receiver_field_interface)`;
  top-level fields only, a generic receiver is refused). The receiver counts
  as the input when every definition back to it is a copy, cast, call guard
  or join (a loop's join included) and `RAX`'s input is the only root. A
  value method `pkg.T.M` receives its struct field by field in registers, so
  when `pkg.T`'s facet lists an interface at offset 0 its first input is
  that field's table (`io.nopCloser.Read`).
  A type assertion's result is the third source
  (`crates/unlace-emit/src/p9_emit/goitabcall.rs (asserted_interface)`):
  the output of a call to `runtime.typeAssert` whose first argument is a
  constant `abi.TypeAssert` record names the interface in the record's
  `Inter` word (read from the image at the record plus 8), and
  `runtime.assertE2I` or `runtime.getitab` name it in a constant first
  argument; either address must start a `type:<interface>` symbol
  (`gotypeglobals`). The compiler joins that result with the hit path of the
  assertion's inline cache probe, an itab loaded from the cache the record's
  `Cache` word points at; a join input computed from a read of that word
  within eight defining ops counts as the same interface, a constant zero (the
  nil table of the failed assertion) agrees with any interface, and any other
  input must resolve to it.
  A stripped binary has no DWARF to type an interface parameter, but its
  callers state it: converting a concrete value to an interface at a call
  loads the static itab into the register that carries the table word. The
  Listing consumer
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/gotypes/itabargs.rs (votes)`,
  x86-64, run only under the option) takes every `LEA` of a static itab (the
  located itabs and their interfaces, as the harvest finds them), follows its
  fall-through to the first direct call within 16 instructions, refusing a
  branch and an indirect call, and keeps the set of registers holding the
  itab: the `LEA`'s destination plus every whole integer argument register a
  `MOV dst,src` copies it to (the compiler often loads it into `RCX` and moves
  it to `RAX` just before the call), each dropped at an instruction that names
  it or one of its parts as its first operand (except `CMP`, `TEST`, `PUSH`,
  `NOP`, `BT`) or writes registers it does not name. At the call it votes
  `(callee, register) -> interface` for every register still in the set. A Go value of interface type has one
  static type, so a pair with two interfaces is dropped; a pair every vote
  agrees on, whose interface has a record, becomes an unlocked input hint:
  the callee's register is `arg<N>_tab`, a pointer to the record.

- **Go pclntab** (`gopclntab`, Go-detected binaries only, always on;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/pclntab/mod.rs`): the runtime
  needs the PC→name table for stack traces, so it survives stripping; the pass
  handles all four header magics (go1.2/1.16/1.18/1.20 layouts) and emits one
  function symbol per entry, so a stripped Go binary renders `main.main` and
  `runtime.*` instead of `sub_<addr>`. It is format-neutral: the table is located
  by its ELF `.gopclntab` / Mach-O `__gopclntab` section, or the
  `.lrodata_gopclntab` / `__lrodata_gopcln` section a link that splits out large
  read-only data gives it, or a scan of the data sections Go places it in. An
  internally linked ELF PIE from go1.25 or older keeps the table in
  `.data.rel.ro.gopclntab` (the relro spelling of `.gopclntab`, which no scanned
  section covers), so that name is on the section list too. The
  scan is the only route on a PE, whose linker writes no pclntab section and
  keeps the table inside `.rdata` among every other rodata symbol, so `.rdata`
  is on the list; and because a PE scan walks megabytes of other data before
  reaching the table, an 8-byte magic-shaped match is only a candidate — the
  header must also describe a table that resolves (a function count in range, a
  functab and a name table that both lie inside the image,
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/pclntab/mod.rs
  (table_plausible)`), or the scan moves on. A plausible table can still be
  someone else's: a Go program that `//go:embed`s another Go executable keeps
  it in the same rodata, ahead of its own table, so the scan prefers the first
  table the image's `moduledata` names (`moduledata_anchored`, as in the PE
  detection above) and keeps the first plausible one only for an image where
  no table is named. An entry is admitted only
  when it lands in an executable extent — a corrupt table cannot mint a function
  over data. Because the `functab` also carries each function's **end**, the pass
  feeds those extents to the interior-entry rejection, so a jump-table case block
  or landing pad inside a Go function is no longer claimed as a `sub_<addr>` of its
  own (on arm64 that artifact used to clip every function that contained one).
  The last function ends at the table's closing `etext` entry, so host code an
  external link places after Go's is not swallowed. Go 1.26 stopped storing the
  text base in the header, so an `entryoff` is then resolved against the module's
  `moduledata.text` (the record read through the `unlace_gomoduledata` layout
  table, accepted only when its `ftab` holds `nfunc + 1` entries) — an external
  link puts `crt` code and
  `.init`/`.plt` ahead of `runtime.text` — falling back to the lowest code section
  when no record is found.

  A packer or obfuscator can overwrite the header's magic in the file (putting
  it back, or skipping the runtime's start-up check, when the program runs) and
  leave the table itself intact. When no magic
  matches a table the image names, the pass finds `runtime.firstmoduledata` by
  its shape and reads the table from that record alone, never consulting the
  header
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/pclntab/gomoduledata.rs
  (locate)`). Every pointer-aligned position of every section that is not code
  is tried; section names and kinds are not consulted, because a packer renames
  them. A go1.16+ record is `pcHeader`, then the `funcnametab`, `cutab`,
  `filetab`, `pctab`, `pclntable` and `ftab` slices, `findfunctab`, and
  `minpc`, `maxpc`, `text`, `etext`. It is accepted when `ftab` starts where
  `pclntable` does, the header, the name table and the functab sit in that
  order, every slice's length is within its capacity, `len(ftab) - 1` is a
  function count in range, the four PC bounds nest, and the functab bears the
  bounds out: its first entry is `minpc` and its closing entry is `maxpc`, the
  identity the runtime itself checks at start-up. That last test also selects
  the entry shape: 32-bit offsets from `text` (go1.18+) are tried first, then
  absolute pointers (go1.16/go1.17). A go1.5–go1.15 record opens with
  `pclntable` and `ftab` instead, with `ftab` starting 8 bytes plus one pointer
  into the table, and is checked the same way. The name table, the functab, the
  `_func` base, the function count and the text base all come from the record,
  so the names, entries and extents are the unmodified image's, and a header
  wiped whole reads the same as one with only its magic gone. The record's
  first word is still the header's address, which is what the Go type harvest
  anchors on, so it works unchanged. The PE detection above counts such a table
  when its functab lies in read-only data. The search runs only after every
  magic-based route has failed, so an image with an intact header never pays
  for it.
- **Go source positions and inline tree** (`gopcln`, Go-detected binaries
  only, default `off`; `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/pclntab/gopcln.rs`):
  the same pclntab carries, per function, the tables the runtime builds a stack
  trace from: `pcfile` and `pcln` (the source file and line of every PC), the
  `PCDATA_InlTreeIndex` table (which inlined call a PC belongs to, -1 for
  none) and the `FUNCDATA_InlTree` records (`runtime.inlinedCall`). Each
  pcvalue table is decoded as `runtime.step` does: the value starts at -1,
  each row adds a zigzag value delta and advances the PC by a delta in
  instruction quanta, and a zero value delta after the first row ends the
  table; rows past the function's end (the next functab entry) are dropped. A
  file value indexes the function's compilation unit in `cutab`, whose entry
  is the name's offset in `filetab`. The tables are located through
  `moduledata` (its `cutab`, `filetab` and, from go1.18, `gofunc`, three
  words after `types`), falling back to the header's `cuOffset` and
  `filetabOffset` when no record is found. Three layouts are read: go1.16-1.17
  (pointer-wide entry, funcdata as absolute pointers aligned to the pointer
  size), go1.18-1.19 (32-bit entry offset, funcdata as offsets from `gofunc`,
  20-byte inline records) and go1.20 on (`_func.startLine`, 16-byte inline
  records `funcID, nameOff, parentPc, startLine`); the header magic picks
  between the last two, or the build-info release when the magic was
  overwritten. The go1.2 layout has no `cutab` and is not read. With `on`,
  each function gets a header comment `source: <file>:<line>` (the line is
  `startLine` on go1.20+, else the `pcln` value at the entry), and the first
  instruction of each inline-tree index the function's PCs reach gets
  `inlined <outer> > ... > <callee> at <file>:<line>`: the chain is followed
  through the index at each record's `entry + parentPc` (the instruction whose
  position is the call site, which on every layout also gives the parent), up
  to 64 hops, and the call site is the source position at that instruction.
  On go1.18 and later the header comment also lists the function's
  `FUNCDATA_StackObjects` table (funcdata index 2): a `uintptr` count, then
  16-byte records `off, size, ptrdata, gcdataoff`, read as
  `stack objects: frame <off> size <n> ptrdata <n>; ...`, at most eight objects
  and then `+N more`. The frame offsets are not yet applied to the stack
  variables and `gcdataoff` is not resolved, so the clause is a comment only.
  With `lines`, a second pass (`gopcln_lines`) also comments `<file>:<line>`
  at each PC where the position changes, the Go counterpart of `dwarf_lines`.
  Both passes run at the commit point, only when the option is on
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/passes.rs (run_gopcln)`): a load-time pass sees
  the option's constructor default, so registered at load they never wrote a
  comment. A default run decodes nothing;
  a function is read only when its entry lies in executable bytes, and at most
  2,000,000 comments are written per image. The comments go through the same
  comment database as `dwarf_lines`, so they appear in the C text and in the
  `code` and `line_mappings` of the JSON document. Without `gofunc` on
  go1.18+ (no `moduledata` and no `go:func.*` symbol) only the source
  positions are written.
- **MSVC RTTI** (`rtti`, PE-only, on by default and inert elsewhere;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/rtti/mod.rs`): find the shared
  `type_info` vftable, byte-search back from each `.?A…@@` TypeDescriptor to its
  CompleteObjectLocator, validate the COL→RTTI3→RTTI2→RTTI1→RTTI0 reachability
  chain (x86 raw-VA vs x64 image-base-relative refs behind a refkind dispatch), and
  label `<Class>::vftable` / `RTTI_*` with the class names demangled by the
  existing MSVC arm. From each recovered `<Class>::vftable` base the pass then walks
  the slot array (`vftable.rs`), bounded at the first NULL or non-`.text` slot, and,
  in a relocatable PE whose base-relocation table reads whole, at the first word that
  table does not list (`TextRanges::with_relocations`): the loader fixes up every
  slot, so an unlisted word is data however it reads, such as the UTF-16 text after
  the last vftable of a large `.text` (Holley EFI's MFC `Holley.exe` read
  `0x0065006e` as `CGDIPCrank::vfunc_97` and split real functions at five such
  words). It then emits one **function** symbol per surviving slot at the address it points at. That
  symbol is named `<Class>::vfunc_<i>` — the class name comes from the RTTI0
  `TypeDescriptor` and the slot index is the only disambiguator MSVC metadata offers,
  since it records no per-method names. The stem is `vfunc_`, not `vftable_`, because
  the name lands on *code*: a class compiled under multiple inheritance genuinely owns
  more than one vftable, so an indexed `<Class>::vftable_<i>` reads as that class's
  i-th table and made `unlace functions` report hundreds of bytes of executable
  `std::basic_stringbuf` code as vtable objects. Only the table itself wears a
  `vftable` name, and it is unindexed. The slots named are those of the vftable
  as the typed vftables below cut it (`msvcvtabletypes.rs (trim_overruns)`):
  the walk alone ran on into a table laid directly after the vftable, and named
  SensorService.dll's RPC server routines `Sensors::BrSensor::vfunc_4` to
  `vfunc_14`. The `<Class>::vftable` label is installed as typed data, an array
  of one code pointer per slot (`mod.rs (type_vftable_labels)`): as an untyped
  label it took the `code` type, and a constructor's store of its address
  printed as a store of the label's value (`this->__vftable = (C_vtbl *)vftable`).
  A function several classes' vftables hold is named once, for the holder that is a
  base of every other holder (`mod.rs (SlotNames::emit)`, the bases read from each
  class's `BaseClassArray`): a derived class that does not override a method keeps
  its base's entry, so the method is the base's. Named per holder, the shortest
  name won, and USBCAN-Driver.dll's `std::exception::what` read
  `std::bad_alloc::vfunc_1`, Holley's `PEGRP32F.dll` `CDialog::DoModal`
  `MaxDlg::vfunc_83` (38 such functions there against IDA 9.5). With no such
  holder (unrelated classes sharing `_purecall` or an identical-code fold) every
  holder names it, as before.

  The pass runs at every PE load whatever its gate says (its facts are committed
  only when it is on), so its cost is paid by every command on a C++ DLL. Both of
  its byte-searches — from the TypeDescriptors back to the words that reference
  them, and from the validated CompleteObjectLocators forward to the meta slots
  before their vftables — are therefore one scan of the image for every class at
  once, grouping the hits by target and visiting them in image order, which emits
  exactly what a search per class would. A search per class is
  `O(classes × image)`: `torch_cpu.dll` (31,623 type descriptors in 309 MB) did
  not finish loading in 30 minutes that way.

  With `vtabletypes` on (the default), a second pass
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/rtti/msvcvtabletypes.rs (facts)`)
  runs the same recovery on its own, whatever `rtti` says, and reports the classes
  in the shape the typed Itanium vtables use (chapter 05). Each
  CompleteObjectLocator gives its class, the `offset` of the subobject its vftable
  serves, and the class's whole hierarchy: every BaseClassDescriptor's class, its
  displacement `mdisp`, and whether it is, or lies in, a virtual base (`pdisp` is
  not -1, and `pdisp`/`vdisp` name its vbtable entry). A vftable at offset 0 is
  the class's own; one at a nonzero offset serves the non-virtual bases at that
  displacement, the most derived of them first. One no non-virtual base accounts
  for serves a virtual base, placed by the vbtable order
  (`msvcvtabletypes.rs (vbase_offsets)`): the virtual bases follow the
  non-virtual part in the order of their vbtable entries, so taken in
  `(pdisp, vdisp)` order (one base reached through two vbtable pointers counted
  once) each that keeps a vftable takes the lowest such vftable left, and the
  bases inside it at a nonzero displacement the vftables at that displacement
  from it. A virtual base keeps a vftable when one of its own or a non-virtual
  subobject vftable shows it does; when that leaves a vftable over, every virtual
  base is taken to keep one. A leftover vftable, a virtual base finding none, or
  a slot count differing from the virtual base's own vftable drops the reading,
  and such vftables serve none. A
  class is typed with the slots of its own vftable, and for each slot the function
  there and every function the vftables serving it in derived classes hold at the
  same slot; a class the image never instantiates (an abstract base) has no vftable
  of its own and takes the slots every serving vftable shares. A slot is named
  after the method a symbol names (`?area@Square@@...` is `area`; `??1` is
  `dtor`; `??_G` and `??_E`, the scalar and vector deleting destructors, are
  `deleting_dtor`), else `vfn_<i>`. A class whose structure name two classes
  share is not typed. Each non-virtual base at a nonzero displacement is reported
  for embedding. The pass also reports, for every function a vftable holds, the
  class its `this` points to: MSVC calls a virtual method with `this` pointing at
  the subobject the vftable serves (an override reached through a secondary base's
  vftable takes the base's subobject), so it is the first class that vftable
  serves; a function several vftables hold takes the nearest class that is, in
  every one of them, that class or one of its bases at offset 0, and a function
  that also sits in a vftable no base accounts for, or whose holders share no
  such class (identical-code folding, `_purecall`), is left untyped. Finally it
  reports each vftable whose first class was typed, with the `rtti` label of
  that address, and every vftable's slot words. A vftable walk stops only at a
  slot that is not code, so a vftable laid directly before another table of code
  pointers ran into it (SensorService.dll's `Sensors::BrSensor` took an RPC
  server's dispatch table for 11 more slots, and typed those routines' first
  parameter `BrSensor *`). Before any of the above, each class's own vftable is
  cut to the shortest vftable a derived class keeps for its subobject, which is
  never shorter than the base's, and every vftable is cut at the first slot,
  past its first, that a pointer-width word of the image points to
  (`msvcvtabletypes.rs (trim_overruns)`). At the analysis commit a third
  pass (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/rtti/msvcctors.rs (run)`,
  x86 and x86-64 only) names the constructors and destructors that store a
  class's vftable through `this` and reports their `this` class too (chapter
  05).
- **(unlace) Itanium RTTI** (`itaniumrtti`, ELF and Mach-O, on by default and inert elsewhere;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/rtti/itaniumrtti.rs`): the
  GCC/Clang counterpart of the pass above, and a capability with **no Ghidra
  equivalent at all** — upstream's `RttiAnalyzer` is a Microsoft-PE analyzer and its
  GCC class recovery is script-tier, so on a stripped `g++` binary Ghidra leaves the
  vtable as an unnamed `DAT_<addr>`.

  Where the MSVC sibling has to *guess* which bytes are metadata (it byte-searches
  for `.?A` strings and treats `ref − 12` as a candidate structure), the Itanium
  graph offers an **exact anchor**. The three `__cxxabiv1` typeinfo vtables live in
  libstdc++, so on any dynamically linked C++ image every `_ZTI…` typeinfo object's
  leading `vptr` word is an undefined-symbol dynamic relocation naming
  `__class_type_info`, `__si_class_type_info` or `__vmi_class_type_info` with addend
  `2 × ptr` — and `.rela.dyn` is a loader input that `strip --strip-all` cannot
  remove. The relocation's offset *is* the typeinfo address and its symbol *is* the
  flavour, which fixes the object's layout past the `[vptr][name ptr]` prefix. A
  defined `_ZTI…` symbol is a second discovery source for the unstripped or
  statically linked case, its flavour sniffed from the object's shape. A non-PIE
  executable has no such relocation: its code refers to the three typeinfo
  vtables by absolute address, so the linker copies each into the image
  (`R_X86_64_COPY`) and every typeinfo's vptr word is a plain pointer two words
  into a copy. The copies keep their `.dynsym` names through `strip`, so a scan
  for words pointing two words into one finds the typeinfo objects of a stripped
  non-PIE image (`itaniumrtti.rs (copied_abi_vtables)`).
