  Each typeinfo's `_ZTS…` type-name string — the bare mangled-name component, which
  no demangler accepts alone — is recovered by wrapping it back into the `_ZTS`
  symbol form and demangling that, the exact analog of the MSVC `??_R0…@8` wrap and
  likewise adding no new demangler. Two details of that string are load-bearing and
  each one silently costs whole classes when missed. A **leading `*`** marks a type
  whose identity is local to one translation unit (ABI §2.9.1: compare `type_info`s
  by pointer, not by string); it is not part of the mangled name, and leaving it on
  makes every anonymous-namespace class — which is how most C++ spells a concrete
  implementation of an exported interface — undemangleable. And the demangled result
  is turned into an identifier by **folding** template arguments in
  (`Vec<int>` → `Vec_int`) rather than by the module-wide `strip_bracket_groups`
  reduction the rest of the demangler applies: two instantiations are two classes
  with two vtables, and collapsing both to `Vec` makes the second lose the idempotent
  symbol-commit race and keep `sub_<addr>` for every method. The `::` split is
  depth-aware so a separator inside an argument list is not read as a scope boundary.

  The `__si_`/`__vmi_` base lists then give the inheritance graph *with its byte
  displacements*, the datum the MSVC path discards along with its `pmd` fields.

  Vtables are reached **from** the typeinfo rather than guessed: every sub-vtable's
  second header word points at its most-derived class's typeinfo, so one scan for
  pointer slots holding a discovered typeinfo address yields them all, and two exact
  ABI constraints reject the coincidental hits (chiefly the base-class pointers
  inside other typeinfo objects, which also hold a typeinfo address) — `offset-to-top`
  is always `≤ 0`, and a real sub-vtable has at least one slot pointing into an
  executable section. A slot whose file word is zero but which carries a dynamic
  relocation is an *imported* virtual method (`__cxa_pure_virtual`, a base method
  defined in another image), so the walk steps over it instead of terminating and an
  abstract interface keeps its true extent.

  The pass emits `<C>_typeinfo`, `<C>_typeinfo_name`, `<C>_vtable` and `<C>_vptr`
  data labels — the last being the value an object's vptr actually holds, two words
  past the header, which is the constant a constructor stores — plus one
  `<C>::vfunc_<i>` function symbol per virtual slot, and marks the slot arrays
  read-only. The slot stem is `vfunc_`, as in the MSVC pass above: a routine is named
  after what it is, not after the data object that points at it. A secondary
  sub-vtable takes the name of the base subobject its displacement identifies
  (`Widget_vtable_for_Drawable`), and its slot names are prefixed accordingly
  (`Widget::vfunc_for_Drawable_<i>`), because a multiple-inheritance class has several
  sub-vtables whose indices all restart at 0. An inherited slot claimed by several classes'
  tables is attributed to the class that **defines** it, using the recovered base
  graph, so `Shape::perimeter` — repeated verbatim in `Circle`'s and `Square`'s
  tables — is named once, for `Shape`. Data labels join the class to the kind with
  `_` rather than `::` because the C printer emits a global by its leaf name, which
  would otherwise render every class's vptr as a bare, ambiguous `vptr`; function
  symbols keep the `::` form, whose qualification *is* rendered at a call site
  (§9, `cppcallnames`).

  Where the Listing is built, the same option also names constructors and
  destructors (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/rtti/itaniumctors.rs`,
  a Listing consumer, because the decoder and the Listing's operand text are not
  available when the vtable recovery runs at load). A constructor or destructor of
  `C` is the function that stores `C`'s vptr into the object it was called on. A
  function becomes a candidate when a decoded operand names a vptr value or its
  4 KiB page; each candidate is lifted to p-code and walked along its fall-through
  path with a small symbolic state in which the first parameter (from the default
  prototype model) is `this`, the stack pointer is the frame base, spills to the
  frame are followed, and a call keeps only the registers the model leaves
  unaffected. Only a STORE of a vptr constant through `this + off` is evidence, so
  a factory that inlines `new C` (it stores through `operator new`'s result) or a
  caller that builds a `C` in its frame is not mistaken for a constructor. The
  owner is the most-derived class whose primary vptr is stored at offset 0, and
  every stored vptr must belong to it or to a base. A function in `C`'s own
  primary vtable is shaped like one of its virtual destructors, `C::~C` (the name
  a symbol table gives the complete-object and the deleting destructor alike), when
  its stores make `C` the owner twice over: all of them, and also the ones made
  before the walk's first call or conditional branch. A destructor sets its vptr
  before anything else; a virtual method that inlined one behind a test (a
  COM-style `Release` checking its count before `delete this`) stores only after
  it, and one that rebuilds `*this` by placement new and goes on to build a
  polymorphic member or a derived class in place also stores that other vptr.
  The ABI puts the deleting destructor in the slot after the complete one, and the
  deleting one either stores too (at `-O2` it may inline the other), calls the
  complete one (a direct call, or an indirect call through a constant, which
  AArch64 clang emits at `-O0`), or, for an abstract class built by clang, only
  traps (a raised exception jumped through). So a class's destructors are named
  from two neighbouring shaped slots, or from a single one whose next slot calls it
  or only traps; that next slot is also named when it calls it. Any other shaped
  slot is a virtual method carrying a constructor's or destructor's code with
  nothing before it — a lone one whose neighbour is an ordinary method
  (`reinit() { new (this) C(); }`, `destroy() { delete this; }` with a non-virtual
  destructor), one beside a complete destructor its own neighbour calls, a third,
  or two that are not neighbours — and none of that class's slots is named. A
  deleting destructor that only tail-calls `operator delete` (clang drops a
  complete destructor's dead stores from it) cannot be told from an ordinary method,
  so such a class keeps its slot names, unless its base says where they are. GCC
  writes the destructor slots of an abstract class as two null words: its vtable is
  only installed while a derived object is built or destroyed, when neither is called
  through it. A primary vtable that walks to no slot because its first two words are
  0, neither covered by a dynamic relocation, followed by a method (code, or an
  imported slot such as `__cxa_pure_virtual`), is such a class's
  (`itaniumrtti.rs (null_dtor_pair)`); the class keeps that vptr and has a
  virtual destructor at slot 0. Under single inheritance a class's primary vtable
  extends its base's, so a class whose own slots show no destructor, on a single
  inheritance chain (every two ancestors one the other's), takes its `D1` and `D0`
  from the slots of the nearest ancestor whose destructors are known (from the null
  pair or the shapes above): both slots its own, not the ancestor's entries, holding
  two different functions no other class's slots hold
  (`itaniumctors.rs (inherited_destructor_slots)`). That names the destructors a
  GCC `-O2` build drops every vptr store from (a final class whose destructor only
  frees members) and those that store only the vptr of the base destructor they
  inlined: apfs-fuse's `PLString`, `PLInteger`, `PLData`, `PLDict` and `PLArray`
  under the abstract `PLObject`, and `BTreeNodeVar`/`BTreeNodeFix` under `BTreeNode`.
  A destructor takes only `this`, while a
  virtual method returning its own class by value builds the result in a return
  slot passed as its first parameter, reads its own `this` from the second, and
  hands the slot's address back, so its first store is the class's vptr through
  "`this`" (`virtual Color darker() const`, `virtual Vec scaled(int) const`). A
  slot whose walk loads or stores through the second parameter (its register, or
  its stack slot on i386), or returns with `this` in a pointer return register
  that is not `this`'s own (x86-64's `RAX`), is not shaped like a destructor. A
  function in no vtable is a constructor `C::C`, but only when `C` or a base has such a virtual destructor, because a
  non-virtual destructor stores the vptr exactly as a constructor does, and only
  when every vptr store goes through `this` read back from a frame slot the
  function itself spilled it to. That is the shape of unoptimized code, which
  inlines nothing; in optimized code a helper that a constructor or destructor was
  inlined into stores the vptr through its first parameter exactly as a
  constructor does (a by-value factory's return slot, a placement-new helper, the
  constructor of a class whose first member is a `C`, a `delete p` wrapper), so an
  optimized constructor is left unnamed rather than risk naming one of those,
  unless the order of its stores says it builds `C` from a base: the last vptr it
  stores at offset 0 is `C`'s primary, no ancestor's follows the first of `C`'s, and
  before it either an ancestor's primary vptr was stored there (an inlined base
  constructor) or a call was passed `this` (an out-of-line one), with no other call
  before; it returns nothing (a by-value factory returns its slot) and touches no
  second parameter (`itaniumctors.rs (built_after_base)`). Every helper above
  stores a class's own vptr alone or, inlining a destructor, the class's and then
  its bases', and a class with no base gives no order to read. GCC `-O2` keeps
  apfs-fuse's `DeviceDMG::DeviceDMG` (a call to `Device::Device` passed `this`,
  then its own vptr) and `BTreeNodeVar::BTreeNodeVar(BTree &, ...)` (the inlined
  `BTreeNode` vptr first) out of line in that shape; `PLArray::PLArray`, whose
  inlined base stores nothing, stays unnamed. The class of a member that
  is itself built from a base (`Holder`'s first member a `Derived`) shows the same
  order, and its constructor is then named `Derived::Derived`. For a constructor the
  walk also follows an unconditional forward jump of at most 512 bytes rather than
  ending there: GCC lays an optimized constructor's member initializers out across
  branches and joins them with a `jmp` ahead of its own vptr store (apfs-fuse's
  `BTreeNodeVar(BTree &, ...)` stores the inlined `BTreeNode` vptr, branches over a
  `shared_ptr` copy, and stores its own after the join). A
  `this` the function stores to a second frame slot is an inlined callee's
  parameter home (an always_inline constructor inlined into the function) until a
  call follows, which makes it the compiler's own spill across that call; a store
  through it is not a store through `this`. A `this` passed in memory is never
  spilled by the function itself, so on such an ABI no constructor is named. An
  unoptimized constructor calls nothing before its vptr store but its bases'
  constructors, each passed `this`; an optimized function returning a class by
  value can spill its return slot across calls it does not pass it to and store
  through the reloaded slot exactly as unoptimized code does (TagLib's
  `Ogg::Page::paginate`, returning a `List<Page*>`), so a store preceded by calls
  none of which was passed `this` names nothing. And
  when `C` has a base, every store must follow a call: a constructor runs its base
  constructors before it sets its own vptr, while a destructor sets it first — the
  shape of a pure virtual destructor, which no vtable slot holds. A
  fact for a function the symbol table already names (anything but a placeholder,
  an entry-table slot or a slot index) is dropped, so a recovered name never joins
  a real one as a second name the call-site lookup could prefer. A
  destructor's slot already carries its slot-index name from the load-time commit;
  the commit of a Function fact replaces a slot-index name (the kind the function
  inventory already ranks as structural) in the same scope with a real,
  non-placeholder name.

  Still named wrongly, all from optimized code: a virtual method that rebuilds
  `*this` (placement new, or an explicit destructor call) when its next slot only
  traps or calls it directly, or when two such methods are neighbours; and, on
  i386, where `this` arrives on the stack, a virtual method returning its own
  class by value without reading `*this` (`virtual Vec zero() const`) beside
  another such method.

  The pass is blind to a `-fno-rtti` build by construction: no typeinfo is emitted,
  so no anchor exists and the output is empty. Independent code-pointer-run scanning
  — which would find such vtables heuristically — is deliberately **not** part of
  this pass.


  **On Mach-O** the same walk runs over a copy of the sections in which every
  `LC_DYLD_CHAINED_FIXUPS` slot holds what dyld writes there
  (`itaniumrtti.rs (MachoSlots)`, over
  `loader/format/macho/chained.rs (resolve_chained_fixups)`): a rebase's
  target, or 0 for a bind, which is the shape an ELF import slot has in the
  file. The bind slots are the "relocated" set the slot walk steps over. The
  exact anchor is a bind to `__ZTVN10__cxxabiv1…_type_infoE` (the Mach-O
  spelling, one more `_`) with addend `2 × ptr`; `__ZTI…` symbols are the
  second source. The copy is made only after an anchor is found, so a Mach-O
  without C++ RTTI pays for the bind list alone. Apple's arm64 ABI sets bit 63
  of a typeinfo's name pointer when the type may be duplicated across images
  and must be compared by string, so the name pointer is read with that bit
  cleared. On a `-fixup_chains` dylib whose `Circle` and `Square` typeinfos
  are local, `make()` changes from `v1 = 0x40a8;` to `v1 = Square_vptr;`. A
  classic `LC_DYLD_INFO` image already has the ELF shape (rebased pointers in
  the file, zeros in bind slots); only its bind names are needed, and they
  come from replaying the bind opcodes
  (`loader/format/macho/dyldinfo.rs (resolve_dyld_info_binds)`), which keeps
  no addend, so the anchor is accepted on the name alone. Pinned by
  `tests/stages/itaniumrtti-macho.toml` and its `-classic` twin.
- **Objective-C** (`objc`, Mach-O-only, on by default and inert elsewhere;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/mod.rs`): walk
  `__objc_classlist` → `class_t` → `class_ro_t` → method lists (both absolute and
  small/relative forms), reading pointer slots through the chained-fixup overlay
  (§1.2) on arm64, and rename each IMP `-[Class sel]`/`+[Class sel]` behind the
  placeholder label gate. The walks share one work budget of eight times the
  image's mapped bytes (16 MiB at least), charged per record and per string
  byte; a string read stops scanning where the budget left runs out, so a
  crafted section of one unterminated run costs no more than the budget
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/sections.rs (read_cstr)`). A selector
  spelled as a Swift-mangled name (`$s` or `_$s` prefix) is shown in the demangler's
  name-only form (`main.hello()`), the form Swift class names take; a name outside
  the demangler's coverage stays raw
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/methods.rs (display_selector)`).

  Code never touches a selector string or a `class_t` directly, so naming those
  alone leaves every send unreadable: `objc_msgSend(obj, sel)` loads `sel` from a
  `__objc_selrefs` slot, a class-method receiver comes from a `__objc_classrefs`
  slot, `[super init]` fills `objc_super.class` from a `__objc_superrefs` slot,
  and a modern link (`-objc_stubs_fast`, the default since Xcode 14) routes most
  sends through a `__objc_stubs` entry — `adrp/ldr x1` of the selref, then a
  jump to `objc_msgSend` through `__got` — so the send is a call to an anonymous
  32-byte function. On an 84 MB arm64 iOS app, 274 of the 1,622 calls in a
  500-function sample were such `sub_<addr>(obj)` calls and every direct send
  read `objc_msgSendSuper2(&super, dat_1045b76f0)`.
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objcrefs.rs (emit)`
  names all four (unlace; the names follow IDA's `selRef_`/`classRef_` convention,
  Ghidra labels the same slots by their pointer type only):

  - each `__objc_selrefs` slot is the pointer-sized data object `selRef_<sel>`,
    colons sanitized to underscores as in the `sel_<sel>` symbol the method walk
    already puts on the selector string (a sent-only selector such as `alloc`
    gets its `sel_` symbol here, since no local method names it);
  - each `__objc_classrefs` / `__objc_superrefs` slot is `classRef_<Class>` /
    `superRef_<Class>`: a rebase slot's class is read off the `class_t` it points
    at, a chained **bind** slot's from the import it names with `_OBJC_CLASS_$_`
    stripped (§1.2), so `classRef_UIView` is named although no address exists for
    it. A classic `LC_DYLD_INFO` image stores a bind slot as zero; its name comes
    from the replayed bind program (§1.2,
    `crates/unlace-analysis/src/loader/format/macho/dyldinfo.rs`);
  - each `__objc_stubs` entry is the function `objc_msgSend$<sel>`, the name the
    linker gives the symbol it synthesized the stub for. The entry is found by
    its own first two instructions (arm64 `adrp x1; ldr x1, [x1, #off]`, x86-64
    `mov rsi, [rip+off]`) at every 4-byte offset, so the 32-byte fast and the
    12-byte small layouts need no stride. When this image's own methods agree on
    one type encoding for the selector, the stub gets that method's prototype
    with `_cmd` removed and every remaining parameter pinned to the register the
    full `(self, _cmd, …)` call places it in (`x0`, then `x2`…, floats in
    `d0`…), which is what keeps a caller from printing the dead `x1` it never
    wrote as an argument: `objc_msgSend$greet:(obj, 5)`. A selector no local
    method defines, or whose arguments would need the stack, keeps the untyped
    call-site inference.
  - the C entry points a send or a log goes through, `objc_msgSend`,
    `objc_msgSendSuper`, `objc_msgSendSuper2` and `NSLog`, each get the
    shape their header declares: the fixed parameters (the receiver or the
    `objc_super *`, then the `SEL`; the format) followed by `...`, on the
    image's resolved import addresses
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objcruntime.rs (variadic)`,
    unlace, no option: it rides `objc`). Unprototyped, a call was recovered from its
    register trials in the model's entry order, which on AArch64 lists `d0..d7`
    before `x0`, so `[super initWithFrame:r]` printed
    `objc_msgSendSuper2(r.x,r.y,r.width,r.height,&sup,sel_initWithFrame_)`; and
    Apple's AArch64 convention puts every variadic value on the stack, past the
    seven `x` registers left unused, where the unprototyped trials stop, so
    `NSLog(fmt, err, payload)` printed with its format alone. With `...` the open
    tail is taken from the same trials after the fixed parameters:
    `objc_msgSendSuper2(&sup,sel_initWithFrame_,r.x,r.y,r.width,r.height)`,
    `NSLog(CFSTR("Error %@ parsing token payload %@"),v4,v2)`. A send's return
    stays recovered from the call site, since the method decides it, so a
    function that ends in a tail-call send is recovered `void`. Each fixed
    parameter is an unnamed `void *`: the declaration renames none of the
    caller's variables and never types a receiver as an instance (a class
    method's receiver is not an `objc_object *`), but a variable passed only as
    a receiver reads `void *`, and an integer-typed value passed straight in,
    such as the result of a runtime call with no prototype (`objc_retain`,
    `swift_getInitializedObjCClass`) or of a nested send, is cast to it. An
    int-sized method argument in the tail is the whole register the call passes,
    `(uint8)(uint4)arg1`, as a declared variadic tail is everywhere
    (`ActionDeadCode` consumes a locked prototype's inputs in full). In `-O0`
    code a dead local spilled just past the outgoing argument area cannot be
    told from one more stack argument, so an `NSLog` there can read a trailing
    argument its format does not have. An import-less definition of the same
    name (libobjc itself) keeps what its body says.

    One stub serves every receiver of its selector, so its prototype is a claim
    about all of them, and a wrong return register is the costly error: a
    protocol of the image declaring `- (double)length` typed
    `objc_msgSend$length` as returning in `d0` for every sender, so after
    `[name length]` on a string `x0` read as dead and the next call lost all its
    arguments (`objc_msgSend$length(arg3); if (sub_103434eb4())`). The stub
    therefore takes the image's agreed spelling
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objcrefs.rs (stub_encoding)`)
    only when, if the SDK headers of `objcsdk` spell the selector, they place
    its return and every argument in the same register class: integer, pointer,
    object and selector all `x`, floating-point `d`, a by-value struct its own
    layout (`Q` and `q` agree, `d` and `Q` do not). A selector only a protocol
    of the image declares, with no class or category of the image implementing
    it, is promised to conformers the image need not hold, so when its return
    is floating-point or a struct it also needs the headers to spell it alike:
    that is the return that hides `x0` from a framework class answering the
    same selector there. A protocol-only `x` or `void` return keeps typing the
    stub. Headers that cannot spell a selector neither confirm nor refute it.
    One the image declares nowhere still takes the headers' spelling. Anything
    else keeps the untyped call-site inference, which recovers the return from
    its use: `v4 = objc_msgSend$length(arg1); if (sub_103434eb4(v4,arg6,1,…))`.
    Without headers an implemented declaration is the only evidence and still
    types the stub, so a framework class answering the same selector
    differently stays mistyped until `objcsdk` names the SDK. An untyped stub
    takes only the arguments the call site shows, so a receiver the caller
    never moved (its own incoming `x0`) is not listed:
    `v1 = objc_msgSend$length();`. A strict fix, no option;
    `tests/stages/objcstubagree.toml` pins it.

  The rebase slots of the three ref sections are also reported constant
  (`AnalysisOutput::const_ranges`). dyld fills them once before any code runs
  and nothing rewrites them — Ghidra's `ObjectiveC2_ClassAnalyzer` marks the same
  blocks read-only for that reason — but they live in writable `__DATA`, outside
  the `SG_READ_ONLY` warrant of `dynrelocs` (§1.3), so the claim is the
  metadata's, and it rides with `objc` (unlace; formerly the separate
  `objcrefconst` option — `objc` is on any Mach-O image under 500 KiB). The commit paints the ranges `Varnode::readonly`
  and adds them to `dynreloc_const` **before** the slots' own symbols are mapped
  (a `SymbolEntry` copies the range property as it is created), so
  `ActionVarnodeProps` folds a load through a selref to the selector string and
  through a classref to the class: `objc_msgSend(obj, sel_init)`,
  `objc_msgSendSuper2(&super, sel_init)` with `super.class = _OBJC_CLASS_$_Derived`,
  `objc_msgSend$tag(_OBJC_CLASS_$_Derived)`. A bind slot has no static value and
  is never folded, so `objc_msgSend(classRef_Remote, sel_tag)` keeps the name.
  The fold is what the chained-fixup unpacking in §1.3 exists for
  here: a chained slot holds its packed chain word until `dynrelocs` unpacks it
  (the ivar offset variables are plain words, not fixups, and fold regardless).
  Like every analysis gate, `objc` is read at the
  `read symbols` commit; flipping it afterwards does not re-paint.
- **Swift metadata** (`swiftmetadata`, Mach-O and ELF, Swift images only, on by
  default and inert elsewhere; `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/swift/mod.rs`, the
  The class walk reaches only what `__objc_classlist` reaches. Three more
  metadata tables fill in the rest (unlace; Ghidra's `ObjectiveC2_ClassAnalyzer`
  reads the same three):
  - **Categories**
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objccats.rs (categories)`):
    `__objc_catlist` and `__objc_nlcatlist` point at `category_t` records whose
    class is usually in another image, so their IMPs were the bulk of the
    `sub_<addr>` left on an ObjC app (77 of 1,892 on a 1.9 MB iOS app). The
    class is read off the `class_t` a rebase slot points at or off the bind name
    (`_OBJC_CLASS_$_UIView` → `UIView`), and the two method lists go through the
    same rename as a class's own: `-[UIView(YYAdd) setLeft:]`,
    `+[NSMutableDictionary(Branch) dictionaryWithJSON:]`. A category whose class
    slot resolves to nothing is labelled `-[(Category) sel]` rather than guessed.
    Protocol and property lists are not read; nothing in the C would show them.
  - **Protocols**
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objcprotos.rs (protocols)`):
    each `__objc_protolist` entry is a `protocol_t` named `_OBJC_PROTOCOL_$_<P>`,
    and its four method lists (required/optional × instance/class) are
    declarations with no IMP — which `method_list_t` readers now keep (`imp ==
    0`) because the declaration carries the one thing a sent-only selector lacks:
    its **type encoding**. `UITableViewDelegate` redeclared in the image spells
    the signature of every `tableView:didSelectRowAtIndexPath:` send, so those
    encodings feed the `objc_msgSend$<sel>` stub prototypes above (kcm: 13 more
    stubs typed, the fixture's `objc_msgSend$wave(self)` from `v16@0:8`). A
    `__objc_protorefs` slot is `protoRef_<P>` and folds like the other refs. A
    class's own conformance list is not read: it names nothing the C would show.
  - **Instance layouts**
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objcivars.rs (Structs::build)`,
    option **`objcivars`**, unlace, default-on, inert unless `objc` is on):
    `class_ro_t.ivars` names every ivar with its type encoding, its size and a
    pointer to its *offset variable* in `__objc_ivar` — the word a compiled method
    loads and adds to `self` (`ldrsw x8, [x8, #off]; ldr d0, [x19, x8]`), because
    under the non-fragile ABI the runtime may slide an offset when a superclass
    from another image grows. The offset variable was already labelled, but as a
    1-byte symbol a 4-byte load never matched, so 505 ivar accesses on kcm read
    `*(long *)((long)self + dat_1001aea74)`; it is now the 4-byte data object
    `<Class>::<ivar>`. Statically the word holds the compile-time layout, so the
    pass builds `struct <Class>` with each ivar at that offset (type from the
    encoding — `@"NSString"` is an opaque `NSString *`, `#` an `objc_class *`,
    a non-decoding encoding an `undefined<size>` — a local superclass embedded as
    `super` at 0 so `self->super.count` keeps its name, an imported one left as
    an anonymous prefix; `instanceSize` is the struct size), superclass first so
    a child can embed its parent. Under `objcivars` the commit types `self` as
    `<Class> *` in the class's and its categories' instance methods (the encoding
    still decodes `@`; the typed `self` rides a separate fact so the gate decides
    at the commit) and reports the offset variables constant through the same
    `dynrelocs` fold path as the refs, so `*(double *)((long)self + Foo::ratio)`
    renders `self->ratio` and `objc_storeStrong((long)self + Foo::_name, x)`
    renders `objc_storeStrong(&self->_name, x)` (kcm: 5,207 field accesses, 0
    anonymous offset loads; Toyota's Swift classes expose their stored
    properties the same way, `self->swiftRUMMonitor`). A class that got no
    layout — one of another image behind a category, or one with no field of
    its own — still types `self` as a pointer to its declared record, so the
    receiver is a `<Class> *` even when it is opaque. A Swift class registers
    with the runtime as `_TtC6Toyota3Foo`; every type the ObjC pass interns or
    declares for it — the instance struct, the embedded superclass, a
    `@"_TtC…"` pointer, the typed `self` — goes through the one
    runtime-to-shown name mapping
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/swiftclassnames.rs (display_class_name)`,
    `Toyota.Foo` under `swiftdemangle`, the runtime spelling off), the same
    mapping the method labels use, while the lookups between the ObjC tables
    keep the runtime spelling. On a Swift image (one with `__swift5_fieldmd`
    that the Swift pass runs on) under `swifttypes` (read at load as
    `UNLACE_SWIFTTYPES`, since this pass runs before any `option` line), a
    Swift class's layout is left to the field descriptors:
    the ivar list encodes Swift-typed stored properties as nothing, so the ObjC
    pass only declares the record and `swifttypes` completes it with the Swift
    names and types — one struct per class (Toyota: `Toyota.AddMileageViewController`
    once, `Toyota.AddMileageViewModel *viewModel` and `bool nativePush` where
    the ivar list gave `unsigned long` and `char`; before, 3,114 `_TtC…`
    structs sat beside 4,886 demangled ones). The Swift pass builds layouts
    when the image is loaded, whatever `swiftmetadata` (which gates only the
    commit of its facts) says; when it does not run at all (`sourcelang`
    forced to another language) the ivar list builds the struct, under the
    demangled name. The stage test
    `tests/stages/swiftclassnames.toml` proves both spellings on
    `macho_swift_classnames_arm64`, and both owners of the layout on
    `macho_swift_classnames_fieldmd_arm64`. Off (the option is read
    at load as `UNLACE_OBJCIVARS` for the structs and at the commit for `self`
    and the fold, so it is set before the `load file` it applies to), no class
    struct is interned, `self` stays `id`, the offset variable keeps its name
    and the load stays a load — the shape to read when a superclass from
    another image may have grown since the link. A class whose name already
    denotes a complete struct (DWARF) is that struct. Class (`+`) methods keep
    `objc_object *self`. The number of classes given a layout is bounded
    (32,768): every type the factory interns costs a linear name scan.
    Properties are not read: a property is a method pair plus an ivar, all
    already named.

  - **Direct methods**
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objcdirect.rs (emit)`):
    a method declared `__attribute__((objc_direct))` (or in an
    `objc_direct_members` class) is called as a C function. It is in no
    `method_list_t`, takes no `_cmd`, and has no type encoding; only its
    symbol, `-[UILabel _setAllowsDefaultTighteningForTruncation:]`, says it is
    a method (iOS 16.4's UIKitCore has 1,541, named by the dyld shared
    cache's local symbols). The walk above never reaches it, so its
    receiver stayed whatever inference made of the first argument while the
    offset variables it loads were still folded: an ivar read printed
    `((objc_object **)a0)[0x56]`, with neither the field nor the
    `_OBJC_IVAR_$_` name. Every method symbol of the image whose address no
    method list gave now hints `x0` as `self` on AArch64 — an unlocked input hint (`unlace_inputhints`, the seam Swift's
    `self` uses, applied here under the default convention), because a
    prototype would have to state the other parameters and nothing declares
    them. Under `objcivars` an instance method's hint carries the `<Class> *`
    of the class the symbol names (category spelling dropped), the same struct
    a listed method's `self` takes, so the read is `self->_configuration`; a
    class method's hint, and every hint with `objcivars` off, only names
    `self`. A body that never reads the register declares no parameter, as
    with any hint, and a function Swift already hinted keeps that hint.
    x86-64 gets no hint: a direct method returning a struct in memory
    (`- (CGRect)frame`) takes the result buffer in `RDI` and `self` in
    `RSI`, and nothing in the symbol says which shape a method has, so a
    `self` hint on `RDI` would type the result buffer as the receiver.
  - **Declarations typed by class**
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objcprops.rs (declarations)`):
    a method's own encoding spells every object as a bare `@`, so the structs
    above typed only `self`. The class is in the metadata: an ivar's encoding
    (`@"Base"`) and a property's attribute string (`T@"Base",&,N,Vinner`, read
    from the `property_list_t` of every class, metaclass, category and
    protocol into a getter `<T>@:` and, unless `R`, a setter `v@:<T>`, with
    `G`/`S` custom selectors honoured; a protocol's class properties too when
    its record is long enough to carry them). The selector table keeps, of two
    declarations that agree once frame offsets and class names are erased
    (`@16@0:8` and `@"Base"@:`), the one naming the class, so a synthesized
    getter is emitted as `Base * -[Holder inner](Holder *self, …)`, its setter
    takes `Base *arg1`, and the `objc_msgSend$inner` stub returns `Base *`. An
    IMP is typed with its *own* class's property spelling, and otherwise its
    own method encoding, so two classes whose `view` return different classes
    each keep theirs and a class that merely shares a selector takes no other
    class's spelling. A stub belongs to no class, so it takes the class only
    when every declaration that names one names the same class; once two
    declarations name different classes (`@"UIView"@:` and `@"NSView"@:`) the
    stub keeps the agreed encoding with the class left out (`@@:`), and so does
    the SDK header reader (`objcsdk`). Every
    declaration — class, category and protocol — is recorded before any IMP is
    emitted. The
    decoder resolves `@"Base"` to the struct the layout built — a pointer built
    before the class's layout lands is to a *declared* record and reads the
    completion afterwards — so a field read through any of them renders:
    `v1 = self->inner->count;`. With `objcivars` off the declared pointer types
    stay (they are the metadata's own statement) while `self` and the offset
    fold do not, so only a deref through such a declared pointer still shows a
    field.
  - **SDK signatures** (`objcsdk`, unlace, default off,
    `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objcsdk.rs (signatures)`):
    the stub prototypes above exist only for selectors the image declares, and
    a framework setter never is, so on kcm 2,897 of 25,084 stub calls rendered
    with no argument at all. The declarations exist in the SDK the app was built
    against, and Apple's headers may not be shipped with unlace, so the option
    names a directory to read **at load** (`UNLACE_OBJCSDK`; nothing derived from
    it is written anywhere): an SDK root contributes the `Headers/` of every
    framework the image links (`LC_LOAD_DYLIB`, 73 on Toyota; ~0.1 s), any
    other directory every `.h` up to eight directories below it. The reader takes the declaration
    subset of the grammar — comments and preprocessor lines stripped,
    `@interface` / `@protocol` / category bodies with their ivar block skipped,
    `- (ret)sel:(T)a …;` methods, `@property (attrs) T name;` as a getter and
    (unless `readonly`) a `setName:` setter with `getter=`/`setter=` honoured,
    and `typedef`s anywhere so `NSInteger`, `CGFloat`, an `NS_ENUM` name or an
    `NSString *`-backed typed enum resolve — and spells each declaration as the
    type encoding the runtime metadata would carry (`v@:d` for
    `setAlpha:(CGFloat)`), so it rides the one selector → prototype path; the
    image's own declarations win unless the headers place a selector's return
    or arguments in different registers (the stub rule above). A class-pointer argument keeps its
    class (`@"UIView"`), a block is `@?`, an `id<P>` is `@`; a type the reader
    cannot encode (an unknown struct, a function pointer) makes the selector
    unusable rather than guessed, and a selector declared two ways across
    classes is dropped (class names erased before comparing; two declarations
    naming different classes keep the selector with neither). By-value structs
    follow AAPCS64 in the stub prototype: a homogeneous aggregate of up to four
    doubles (`CGRect`, `UIEdgeInsets`) is spread over `d` registers as
    `arg_x, arg_y, arg_width, arg_height`, `NSRange` over two `x` registers, a
    larger one (`CGAffineTransform`) is the pointer the caller passes; a struct
    return that spreads over registers is the flat struct
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/encoding.rs (struct_type)`,
    `CGRect {x, y, width, height}`) the model places in `d0..d3`, so
    `v = objc_msgSend$bounds(view); objc_msgSend$setFrame:(view, v.x, v.y, v.width, v.height)`.
    Only nested by-value structs are flattened into their leaf members; a
    pointer member is one pointer-sized field whatever it points to
    (`{S=^{T=ii}q}` has two members, a pointer and a `q`). The leaves keep their
    C offsets: each member is aligned to its size (at most a pointer's), a
    nested struct to its widest member and padded to a multiple of it, and the
    struct's size is padded the same way, so `{S={T=iC}C}` puts the last `C` at
    8 and `{Tri=iii}` is 12 bytes, not 16. A layout with a bitfield member
    (`b3`), whose packing the encoding does not give, is not laid out at all.
    A pointer to a named struct whose layout the encoding spells (`^{S=Q^@}`,
    from the image's metadata or from the headers) is a pointer to that struct
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/encoding.rs (struct_type_at)`),
    with the member names the encoding carries (`{S="count"Q"items"^@}`) and
    `[N T]` members as arrays; an anonymous or empty layout (`^{?=Q}`,
    `^{__CFString=}`) stays `void *`. The header reader spells a pointer to a
    `typedef struct { … } Name;` that way, member names included
    (`(NSFastEnumerationState *)` is
    `^{NSFastEnumerationState="state"Q"itemsPtr"^@"mutationsPtr"^Q"extra"[5Q]}`),
    a pointer to a struct it cannot lay out (a bitfield, a nested definition,
    no body) as `^v` and never as a class pointer, a pointer to a scalar with its
    pointee (`NSInteger *` is `^q`), an array parameter (`id [_Nonnull]`) as a
    pointer to its element, and the lightweight generic parameters of an
    `@interface Name<K, V>` as `id` (so `NSDictionary`'s `(K [])` spelling of
    `countByEnumeratingWithState:objects:count:` agrees with `NSEnumerator.h`'s
    `(id [])`). The typelocked struct pointer then types the stack object whose
    address the caller passes (P6 `gatherOpen`), so a for-in loop's eight words
    of enumeration state are one `NSFastEnumerationState` local and the loop
    reads `state.itemsPtr[i]` and `*state.mutationsPtr`.
    System V x86-64 has no such registers past two eightbytes (it passes a
    larger struct on the stack), so a selector with such an argument or return
    gets no prototype there
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objcrefs.rs (struct_passing)`).
    The 1.9 MB app: 2,897 → 1,221 argument-less stub calls; an 84 MB app sample: 32 → 4, 60 of
    265 stub calls change shape (`setTransitioningDelegate:(v3, delegate)`,
    `presentViewController:animated:completion:(vc, (UIViewController *)v10, 1, NULL)`).

  - **Message sends typed and resolved by their receiver**
    (`crates/unlace-bandb-base/src/p5_types/objcrettype.rs (instancetype)`,
    options **`objcrettype`** and **`objcresolve`**, unlace, default-on, inert
    unless `objc` is on): the names above are per entry point, so a send still
    read `objc_msgSend(v1, sel_setInner_, v2)` with `v1` an `objc_object *`
    from `objc_alloc_init(_OBJC_CLASS_$_Base)`. Hex-Rays walks the receiver
    instead, and so does this: the analysis hands the engine its class table
    (every class's own methods by selector — categories included — its
    superclass, the `class_t` address a class reference folds to, every selector
    string and selector-reference slot). At P5, `TypeOpCall::getOutputLocal`
    answers for a send before the stub's locked `id` does: `alloc`,
    `allocWithZone:`, `new` and the runtime's `objc_alloc`/`objc_alloc_init`/
    `objc_opt_new` on a class reference return `Base *`; `init…`, `self`,
    `retain`, `autorelease`, `copy`, `mutableCopy` return their receiver's class
    pointer, a receiver that is itself a send being asked first so an alloc/init
    chain types through (`objcrettype`). A method's own locked `id` return still
    wins where the two meet (`return (objc_object *)v1;`). At P9 the printed
    callee of a send whose receiver's class is known — a folded class reference,
    a pointer to a class struct, or a value the P5 walk resolves — is the IMP
    found along the superclass chain: `-[Base setInner:](v1, sel_setInner_, …)`,
    `-[Base count](self->inner, sel_count)`, `-[Holder inner](self)` for the
    `objc_msgSend$inner` stub (`objcresolve`). The resolution is not a
    rendering: once the first decompile has resolved the sends of a function,
    each site's IMP is recorded on the architecture
    (`decompile_step.rs (objc_retargets)`) and the function is decompiled
    again with every such CALL sent to the IMP — `FlowInfo::setup_call_specs`
    asks `query_call_retarget` before the callee is looked up, so the call
    carries the method's own prototype (`-[Base setInner:](self, SEL, id)`) and
    `unlace xrefs` its edge. An `objc_msgSend$<sel>` stub site has no selector
    argument, so it keeps the stub's argument shape (`query_call_site_pieces`)
    with `self` typed as the receiver's class and the method's declared return.
    The retarget is the unlace analog of Hex-Rays' `cot_obj` callee plus the code
    xref it adds; `unlace xrefs --from f` decompiles `f` and `--to m` the callers
    of the selector's stub and then of `objc_msgSend` (at most 512), reading the
    retargets back. A method's `self`/`_cmd` parameter names are never adopted
    for the caller's variables. A selector no class of the chain declares keeps
    the runtime entry point. The stage test `tests/stages/objcresolve.toml`
    runs both fixtures with the options off and on; `unlace-cli`'s
    `xrefs_objc_resolved` test asks both directions.

    Classes the image only imports come from the SDK headers `objcsdk` names
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objcsdk.rs (read)`,
    `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/mod.rs (add_sdk_classes)`).
    Each `@interface` gives its class a superclass and the methods and
    properties it declares (a category's are merged into its class;
    `@property (class)` is a class method), each with its declared result when
    that is `instancetype` or a class pointer. The table takes the classes the
    image imports (an undefined `_OBJC_CLASS_$_<name>`) or subclasses, closed
    over their superclasses, and declares an opaque record for each of them
    and for every class one of their methods returns, so a result typed by one
    is `NSURL *` without an interned layout. A method of such a class has no
    IMP: it names the callee (`+[NSNumber numberWithLongLong:]`) and is never
    retargeted. The engine adds the class receivers the loader binds: a
    `machodataslots` data import slot named `_OBJC_CLASS_$_<name>`
    (`crates/unlace-console/src/engine.rs (commit_analysis_output)`)
    is a class receiver while it holds the value the loader put there (the
    same test as `importdata`'s `&<import>`). A receiver is followed by its
    value (`crates/unlace-bandb-base/src/p5_types/objcrettype.rs (class_value)`):
    through copies and casts, a value a call leaves alone (`INDIRECT`), a join
    whose inputs all name the same class (an input that leads back to the join
    adds nothing), and the runtime functions that return their argument
    (`objc_opt_self`, `objc_retain`, `objc_autorelease` and the
    autoreleased-return claims), so Swift's
    `[objc_opt_self(&OBJC_CLASS_$_NSBundle) mainBundle]` resolves. Besides the
    linked frameworks, an SDK root's `usr/include/objc` is read for the root
    class `NSObject`. Under `objcrettype` a class send then types its result
    from the declaration along the chain (`instancetype` is the receiver class,
    a class pointer that class), or, undeclared, from a factory selector whose
    leading noun, before `With`, is the class name's tail case-insensitively
    (`numberWithInt:` on `NSNumber`, `stringWithFormat:` on
    `NSMutableString`); an instance send takes its declared result the same
    way. `objc_msgSendSuper2(&super, sel)` is looked up from the superclass of
    the sending method's class (its label `-[Foo bar]` names it), `[super
    init…]` returns that class, and a super send is never retargeted either,
    since its first argument is the `objc_super`. On a 390-function sample of
    a 72 MB iOS app this resolves 88 more sends (64 to 152) and types 13 more
    locals as class pointers (108 to 121); `tests/stages/objcsdksend.toml`
    runs a fixture that sends to an imported class with `objcresolve` and
    `objcrettype` off and on.

  - **By-value aggregates and global blocks**
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/encoding.rs (struct_leaves)`,
    `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objcblocks.rs (emit)`,
    unlace, no option — a strict fix): a struct by value in an encoding
    (`{CGRect={CGPoint=dd}{CGSize=dd}}`) used to decode to a void placeholder,
    so a `CGRect frame` ivar read `*(double *)&self->frame[0x10]`, an `int
    counts[4]` ivar (`[4i]`) was indexed by hand, and an IMP taking a `CGRect`
    lost its prototype altogether. The decoder now builds the struct the
    encoding spells through the same `struct_type` the stub returns use, with
    the member names an ivar encoding quotes (`"origin"{CGPoint="x"d"y"d}`,
    nested structs flattened to `x, y, width, height`) and the CoreGraphics
    table for a method encoding that quotes none, and `[n T]` as an array. The
    IMP then reads
    `-[Shape setFrame:](Shape *self, SEL _cmd, CGRect arg1)` with `arg1` placed
    by the model (`d0..d3`).
    The record is laid out as the C compiler lays it out
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/encoding.rs (record_layout)`):
    each member at its natural alignment, a nested struct placed as a unit
    before its fields are listed in the parent (`{Outer=C{Inner=Cq}C}` is 32
    bytes with fields at 0, 8, 16 and 24), the whole padded to its widest
    member. A union (`(Word=qf)`) is built the same way with every member at
    offset zero and is one field where it sits in a struct. A zero-length array
    member (`[0C]`) takes no room. The encoding gives a bit-field its width and
    not its declared type (`b3`), so a run of adjacent bit-fields is one
    unsigned field over the bytes the run packs into, starting at the next free
    byte, and the record is aligned as for `unsigned int`, or `unsigned long
    long` once the run passes 32 bits: `{Flags=b3b5S}` is 4 bytes, not the 12
    of one word per bit-field. A struct or union with no name (`{?=qiIq}`, the
    spelling of `CMTime` and of every typedef'd anonymous struct) is named from
    its member codes, `struct_qiIq`, or from a hash of them when they are long
    or hold punctuation, with quoted member names left out, so an ivar's and a
    method's spelling of one layout are one type. A flattened field name that
    is already taken is prefixed with the name of the member it came from
    (`duration_value`). `{Name}` spells no layout: it is the incomplete record
    of that name, so `^{Name}` is a `Name *`, and a method that passes or
    returns one by value gets no prototype, as does one whose record holds
    itself, has no member, has a member that does not decode (`{?=[4]}`, a
    SIMD matrix), or passes the bounds (32 levels of records and arrays, 4096
    fields, 1 MiB). A refused layout is remembered by name and not retried. An
    array argument (`[10Q]`) is the pointer C passes. With the record built,
    the convention's own rules place it, nothing in the decoder: on Apple
    arm64 a homogeneous floating-point aggregate of up to four members travels
    in `d0..d3`, any other record of up to 16 bytes in `x` registers, a larger
    one as a pointer to the caller's copy, and a return past 16 bytes through
    `x8` (`void -[Shape transform](CGAffineTransform *rethidden, Shape *self,
    SEL _cmd)`); on System V x86-64 a record past two eightbytes is on the
    stack and its return through `rdi`. Before this a union or an unnamed
    struct by value decoded to void and the method lost its prototype and its
    typed `self` (`long -[Shape word:](void *a0, unsigned long a1, long a2)`
    reading `((long *)a0)[0x12]`; now `long -[Shape word:](Shape *self, SEL
    _cmd, Word arg1)` returning `self->total + arg1.field_0`); of the distinct
    method encodings in an iOS 16.4 dyld cache that pass or return a record by
    value, 29% spell one of the two.
    A global block literal — `isa =
    _NSConcreteGlobalBlock, flags, reserved, invoke, descriptor` in `__const`,
    found by the isa slot's bind name — is typed `Block_layout`
    (`block_literal_<addr>`), its invoke is named `block_invoke_<addr>` and,
    when `BLOCK_HAS_SIGNATURE` is set, typed from the descriptor's signature
    with the block itself first (`long block_invoke_10000071c(Block_layout *block, long arg1)`).
    A stack block is built by its creator at run time; `stack_blocks` finds
    the build in each arm64 function the way Hex-Rays reads the creator's
    microcode: the isa's GOT slot load (`adrp; ldr`, or the linker's `ldr
    <literal>`) stored to `sp`, then the `adr` / `adrp; add` addresses stored
    16 and 24 bytes after it (`str`/`stp`), state cleared at every `ret`. The
    invoke is named `<creator>_block_invoke` (`_2`, `_3` for the next blocks
    of one creator; the creator is the nearest IMP label or symbol at or before
    the store), typed from the descriptor's signature, and its first argument
    is `Block_layout_<invoke> *` — `Block_layout` then one field per captured
    value up to the descriptor's `size` — so `return block->capture_0 * arg1;`.
    Each capture's type comes from the descriptor's copy helper when the block
    has one (`BLOCK_HAS_COPY_DISPOSE`: the helper's `_Block_object_assign`
    flags say 3 object, 7 block, 8 byref, 16 weak, and a capture it
    `objc_retain`s itself is an object) and otherwise from the store that
    filled it (`str w` an `int`, `str d` a `double`, `str s` a `float`, `str q`
    16 bytes, a frame or code address a `void *`, else a `long`). A `__block`
    variable's cell — built on the same frame as `isa = 0`, `forwarding =
    &cell`, `flags`/`size` (one eight-byte constant the compiler pools, or two
    words) and the value — becomes `Block_byref_<size>_<width>` (`isa`,
    `forwarding` of its own type, `flags`, `size`, the copy/dispose helpers
    when `flags` says so, `value` as wide as the initializing store), and the
    capture that holds its address a pointer to it, so the invoke reads
    `block->capture_1->forwarding->value`. The creator's frame is typed too
    (`LocalFact`s the decompile seeds like DWARF locals): the literal is
    `block` (`block_2`, …) and each cell `cell_<k>`, so the build reads
    `block.block.invoke = …; block.capture_1 = &cell_1; cell_1.forwarding = block.capture_1;`
    — Hex-Rays' `Block_layout_<ea>` frame members. A capture's signedness is
    not modelled. The stage tests
    `tests/stages/objcstructs.toml` and `tests/stages/objcblocks.toml`
    run `macho_objc_structs_arm64` and `macho_objc_blocks_arm64`.

    On an x86-64 Mach-O the same recovery reads x86-64 creators
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objcblocks/x86.rs (sites)`,
    on with `objc` on that target and never run on another): the isa is
    `mov r, [rip + slot]` of the `_NSConcreteStackBlock` GOT slot, the invoke
    and descriptor are `lea r, [rip + addr]`, the flags a 32-bit immediate
    moved through a register (or two `mov dword` stores), and the stores go
    through `rbp`, `rsp` or a register holding a frame address. Instructions
    there have no fixed width, so the scan does not walk the whole text: it
    first finds every four bytes that, read as a `rip`-relative displacement,
    land on the isa slot, and decodes only the functions those lie in, from
    their start (the image's function starts and every label that can name a
    creator). The decoder (`x86.rs (decode)`) gives every 64-bit-mode
    instruction its length (legacy, REX and VEX prefixes, the one-byte, `0F`,
    `0F 38` and `0F 3A` maps); bytes that are no instruction (EVEX, an opcode
    invalid in 64-bit mode, a jump table in the text) are stepped over one at a
    time with the state cleared. The scan models the handful a literal is
    built from: `mov` between registers, to and from the frame and of an
    immediate, `lea`, `xor r, r`, the SSE/AVX stores (`movsd` a `double`,
    `movss` a `float`, `movaps`/`movups`/`movdqa` 16 bytes),
    `push`/`pop`/`add`/`sub rsp`/`leave` for the frame depth. Every other
    instruction clears the registers it may write (never fewer than it does
    write), a call clears the caller-saved ones, and `ret` or an unconditional
    jump clears everything but the frame registers and gives the code after it
    the `rsp` and `rbp` the function body had before its epilogue. Frame
    offsets are kept relative to `rsp` at entry, so a literal at `[rbp - 0x68]`
    under `push rbp; mov rbp, rsp` is the local at `stack - 0x70`. The copy
    helper is read the same way (`x86.rs (copy_helper_kinds)`): the capture is
    the last `mov r, [r + off]` into `rdi` at an `objc_retain` /
    `objc_retainBlock` or into `rsi` at a `_Block_object_assign` (its flags in
    `edx`), whether the call is direct, a tail jump, or through the GOT (`call
    [rip + slot]`). Naming, the descriptor, the captured layout and the typed
    locals are the shared code above; only a label at or after the function's
    start names its creator. An image with no `LC_FUNCTION_STARTS` has only its
    labels and exports for starts, so there the code after a `ret`, a jump
    through a slot or a jump out of `__text` may be another function's: a block
    built past one has no known creator, is named
    `block_<invoke>_block_invoke`, and types no frame; its invoke is typed all
    the same. `tests/stages/objcblocksx86.toml` runs
    `macho_objc_blocks_x86_64` and `macho_objc_blocks2_x86_64` with `objc` off
    and on.

  - **A dyld shared cache image**
    (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/objccache.rs (CacheReader)`,
    `crates/unlace-analysis/src/loader/dyldcache.rs (objc_selector_base)`,
    unlace, no option: it rides `objc`): an image rebuilt out of a cache keeps
    its own sections, but the cache builder moved the rest of its metadata. A
    small method list holds its selectors as offsets from the cache's *selector
    base* (`entsizeAndFlags & 0x40000000`) and, under `0x20000000`, its type
    strings too. The strings and the `__objc_selrefs` targets live in libobjc's
    `__OBJC_RO` region, outside the image. `class_ro_t.baseMethods` with its low
    bit set names a relative list of lists (`entsize 8`; each entry's `>> 16` is
    the list's offset from the entry, its low 16 bits an image index), the shape
    of preattached categories. When the image under analysis was loaded from a
    cache (`AnalysisCtx::image_path` opens it), `MachoImage::with_cache` reads
    every address outside the image's own sections through the cache, one slid
    page at a time with pointers unslid, each page read once and each read
    charged to the walk budget. `methods.rs (read_small_direct)` resolves the
    two flags from the base and `classt.rs (method_lists)` walks the list of
    lists. The base comes from the `ObjCOptimizationHeader` the cache header
    names (`objcOptsOffset`; `relativeMethodSelectorBaseAddressOffset` at
    +0x30, an offset from the cache base), else from libobjc's `objc_opt_t`
    (`__objc_opt_ro`, version 16 on, the same field at +0x28 as a signed offset
    from the record) on an older cache. A method whose IMP lies outside the image, a
    category of another image preattached to this image's class, is named at
    that address as an import (`AnalysisOutput::import_slot_names`) and makes
    no function. Class, super and protocol reference slots hold plain pointers
    into other images, so the same reads name them; the cache's hash tables are
    not consulted.
    Two readings apply to every Mach-O, and a cache is where they show. The
    entry size of a method list is `entsizeAndFlags & 0xfffc`: the two low bits
    are the uniqued and sorted flags, which the cache builder sets on disk, and
    reading them as size walks 15-byte records. And the linker merges the
    categories of a class into one, so the metadata names only the merged
    category while the symbol keeps the original (`-[NSObject(NSKeyValueCoding)
    valueForKeyPath:]` against a metadata `NSObject(Foundation)`); a symbol at
    the IMP that spells the same class and selector is the label
    (`sections.rs (MachoImage::method_symbol)`), which is also what lets the
    prototype reach a function the symbol table already named.
    Foundation out of an iOS 16.4 arm64e cache: 3,979 `objc_msgSend$<sel>` stubs
    named (none before), every selector, class, super and protocol reference
    slot named (6,050, 566, 481 and 33), `self` and `_cmd` typed on its methods.
    `tests/stages/dyldcacheobjc.toml` runs the two synthetic caches of
    `dyld_cache_objc.py`, one with the header and one with only the
    `objc_opt_t`.
  - **SDK C prototypes** (`objcsdk`, unlace, the C half of the same directory,
    `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/protos/sdkprotos.rs (SdkProtoPass)`):
    the same headers declare the C functions an image imports — CoreFoundation,
    libdispatch, Security, CoreGraphics, `os_log`, and in a kernel SDK the
    functions a kext calls — and an import of one had no prototype, so a call
    whose arguments were set up before an earlier call lost them
    (`v2 = CFStringGetLength();`) and a tail call printed bare
    (`dispatch_async_f(); // tail-call`). The pass runs on any Mach-O when the
    directory is named, needs no `objc`, and is registered after the libc
    tables, which it defers to (`has_builtin_prototype`); the `objc_msgSend`
    family is left to the selector path. For this half an SDK root also
    contributes `usr/include` (without its C++ tree), and a kext
    (`MH_KEXT_BUNDLE`) gets `Kernel.framework/Headers` alone so user and kernel
    declarations of one name do not meet
    (`sdkprotos.rs (header_paths)`).
    Each header is first cut down to the target: preprocessor conditionals over
    the pointer width, the architecture, the platform the image's build version
    names (`TARGET_OS_IPHONE`, `TARGET_OS_OSX`, …), `__cplusplus` and the
    compiler (`sdkprotos.rs (predefined)`) keep only the branch that
    applies, and an include guard is no condition. A condition that turns on
    anything else keeps every branch and marks their text as undecided: a
    function declared there is still read (both branches must then agree), but a
    record defined only there, or with such a condition inside its body, has no
    layout, and an enum defined there has no names — the 32-bit-inode
    `struct stat` beside the real one is the case. A `#pragma pack` or
    `#pragma options align` caps the alignment of the members it covers
    (`pack(push, 4)` around the Mach message structs); a form the reader does
    not follow leaves the rest of that file's records without a layout
    (`sdkprotos.rs (select_branches)`). Objective-C bodies are dropped, their
    class names kept. The rest is split into statements — a linkage block
    (`extern "C" { }`) is transparent, an inline function is dropped with its
    body — and each statement is indexed by what it defines without resolving
    anything: `typedef` names, `struct` / `union` / `enum` bodies by tag, the
    enum macros (`typedef CF_ENUM(Base, Name) { … }` and its `NS_` / `CF_OPTIONS`
    forms, `OS_ENUM(name, Base, …)` / `DISPATCH_ENUM`, which define `name_t`),
    the object macros (`DISPATCH_DECL(dispatch_queue)`, `OS_OBJECT_DECL(…)`:
    `name_t` is a pointer to the opaque `name_s`), and the statements holding
    `name(` for an imported `name` (`sdkprotos.rs (Index)`).
    Only those are then parsed: the return type is what precedes the name once
    attribute macros are skipped (an all-capitals name or a `__` name that is no
    type, each with its argument list: `CF_EXPORT`, `API_AVAILABLE(…)`,
    `__attribute__((…))`), each parameter is specifiers plus a declarator
    (pointers, an optional name, arrays, a function pointer or block), `...`
    makes it variadic, and `()` declares nothing. Types resolve on demand
    through the index; a `typedef` or record the headers define two ways is
    unresolved, except that two pointer definitions are still a pointer, an enum
    agrees with its underlying integer, and a transparent union is its first
    member. A function gets a prototype only when every declaration of it
    resolves and they agree (`sdkprotos.rs (signature)`).
    A `struct` or `union` whose members all resolve — no bitfield, no packing
    attribute, every array bound a constant — is interned with its 64-bit
    layout, so a pointer parameter to it has fields
    (`CFRange v2; … v2.length + v2.location`,
    `GadgetGetInfo(a0,&v2); … v2.count`); any other record is a declared one
    behind its pointer (`__CFString *`). An enum whose enumerators evaluate
    becomes a named enum of its underlying width, so constants print by name
    (`kCFCompareNumerically|kCFCompareCaseInsensitive`,
    `== kCFCompareEqualTo`). A by-value struct argument is spread into one
    parameter per member only where the convention passes it as those members
    would travel alone — a homogeneous aggregate of up to four floating-point
    members or two words on AArch64, two doubles or two words on x86-64, and
    only while the registers last — an AArch64 struct over sixteen bytes is the
    pointer the caller passes, and every other by-value aggregate, argument or
    return, leaves the function without a prototype
    (`sdkprotos.rs (passing)`). The prototype is parked on each import
    address and by name, as the libc tables are. On the arm64e `trustd` of iOS
    16.4 against the iOS 16.5 SDK, 252 of the 255 imported functions the SDK
    declares get a prototype (the other three take `sqlite3_int64`, whose type
    is a build-time macro); reading the linked frameworks' headers and
    `usr/include` adds about 0.15 s to that load in a development build. With
    no directory named the pass returns before reading anything.
  Decoding every method's encoding asks the type factory for `objc_object *`
  once per argument, and the factory finds a type by name with a linear scan of
  every type it holds; with thousands of class structs interned that scan is no
  longer cheap, so the decoder caches the named opaque pointer types it hands out
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/objc/encoding.rs (TypeCtx)`).
  record layouts in `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/swift/descriptors.rs`):
  a stripped Swift binary keeps its reflection sections, and they name much of
  its code. The pass reads `__swift5_types` / `swift5_type_metadata` (the nominal
  type context descriptors: kind, parent chain, name, metadata accessor, field
  descriptor, for a class the trailing vtable and override table, and for an
  enum its case count: the payload cases in the low 24 bits of the word at
  +20 plus the empty cases at +24, which `AnalysisOutput::swift_enum_cases`
  hands to the engine keyed by the enum's metadata accessor, so that chapter
  2's `switchextent` bounds the enum's `switch` tables),
  `__swift5_protos` (protocol descriptors with their requirement rows),
  `__swift5_proto` (conformance descriptors: protocol, conforming type, witness
  table pattern, resilient witnesses) and `__swift5_fieldmd` (field descriptors),
  per the ABI's `Metadata.h`. Everything there is a 32-bit self-relative pointer,
  so no fixup resolution is needed (an ELF's unallocated sections — the symbol
  and string tables, debug info — sit at address 0 and are left out of the
  address map the reader resolves through, so a binary that kept its symbols
  reads as its stripped twin does); an *indirectable* pointer (low bit set)
  names a pointer-sized slot, which is a rebase (resolved through the
  chained-fixup overlay, §1.2) or a bind to another image — and the overlay now
  records each bind slot's import name (`ChainedFixups::bind_name`), which is
  how a conformance to `Swift.Hashable` or an override of a UIKit initializer
  learns the other image's descriptor name. Names follow the demangler's
  name-only conventions so they read like symbol-table names and agree with the
  real symbol where one survives (the fixture's unstripped build is the oracle):
  `Module.Type.type_metadata_accessor`; `Module.Class.vtable#3.getter` for a
  vtable slot's implementation by position and kind (a slot carries no selector;
  the optimizer leaves a removed method's slot null, which is skipped);
  `Module.Sub.init(coder:rootView:)` for an override whose overridden method
  descriptor is an import (`…Tq`), the real member name; `Module.Sub.vtable#3.init`
  for an override of a local base; `<Module.Type:Swift.Hashable>.hash(into:)`
  for a resilient witness whose requirement descriptor is an import,
  `<T:P>.requirement#2` for a local protocol's witness (the witness-table words,
  read through the chained-fixup overlay on a Mach-O and the `R_*_RELATIVE`
  addends on an ELF), `Module.P.requirement#2.default` for a default
  implementation; and the records: `….nominal_type_descriptor`,
  `….protocol_descriptor`, `….module_descriptor`,
  `<T:P>.protocol_conformance_descriptor`, `<T:P>.protocol_witness_table`,
  `….reflection_field_descriptor`. A type path follows the parent chain
  (`Module.Outer.Inner`; an anonymous context is transparent, an extension
  context demangles its extended type, a parent in another image is named
  through its module-descriptor import). Only a code address where a function
  can start is ever named as a function: not data (a base-protocol or
  associated-type witness row points at data), not a misaligned arm64 address,
  and not a point strictly inside a body the image states — a sized function
  symbol or a single-function `.eh_frame` FDE
  (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/entry/mod.rs (stated_function_bodies)`),
  since a name there would become a function splitting that body. A stated
  start is not required: swiftc emits no FDE for a function that keeps no
  frame, so the stripped `swift_metadata_elf`'s `.eh_frame` states 13 starts,
  fewer than the functions its records name. Function names use the FID-precedent placeholder gate. Every record's claim
  on a function is collected before any name is given, because the linker
  folds functions with identical bodies (identical code folding) and one
  address is then the target of records of unrelated types — on the Toyota
  app 2,350 of the 57,147 claimed functions, 2,037 of them claimed by more
  than one type. A claimant is a type by its descriptor (a local one by
  address, so two private types that print the same path are two claimants;
  an imported one by symbol), and a type whose path cannot be named still
  claims the functions it points at, it just offers no name. Such a function
  is never named after one of its claimants: when all claims come from one
  type it is named after the first member (in order, a number compared as a
  number, so `requirement#2` comes before `requirement#10`) with the count of
  members it serves
  (`<T:P>.requirement#0.merged#2`); when they are witnesses of one protocol
  member from different types it is named after the member alone
  (`<*:Swift.RawRepresentable>.init(rawValue:)`); any other mix (different
  types' vtable slots, different members) keeps the engine placeholder. A
  name already given to another function (the same member's second folded
  body; a static and an instance requirement spelled alike; two Clang types
  of one name) gets `.2`, `.3`, … in address order, so every name resolves
  to one function. On the Toyota iOS app
  (314,038 functions, 304,309 of them `sub_<addr>`) the pass names 57,147
  stripped functions — 14,615 metadata accessors, 15,204 vtable slots, 27,322
  witnesses, 6 overrides — every one at an address function discovery already
  found, in about 0.3 s and 135 MB over the baseline decompile. The work is
  bounded by the image: a conformance descriptor several section entries name
  is read once, every record row (a descriptor, a vtable, override,
  requirement or witness row, a witness-table word) is charged against one row
  per four bytes of the image, which a real image never exceeds since each row
  occupies at least that much of it, and the names built (type paths included)
  stop at 16 MiB plus the image's length, so repeated or overlapping records
  in a crafted file cannot multiply into millions of names. The pass is
  registered only for `Compiler::Swift` (§1.3's detector) in Mach-O or ELF, so
  every other image's pass set is unchanged; the stage test
  `tests/stages/swiftmetadata.toml` runs the fully stripped swiftc-built
  `swift_metadata_elf` off and on.
- **Swift type layouts** (`swifttypes`, the type-layout arm of the pass above,
  default-on and inert unless `swiftmetadata` is on;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/swift/swifttypes.rs`): a
  non-generic type whose metadata needs no runtime initialization (the
  descriptor's `MetadataInitialization` is none: no foreign or singleton
  initialization; and a class whose descriptor sets `HasResilientSuperclass`,
  bit 13 of the kind-specific flags, is skipped whatever that says, since its
  field offsets wait for the runtime to size the superclass) has that
  metadata laid out statically,
  and its accessor is the one-line function that returns the address — `adrp
  x0, …; add x0, x0, …; mov x1, #0; ret` on arm64 (or the `adr x0, …; nop` a
  linker relaxes the pair to), `lea rax, [rip + …]; xor
  edx, edx; ret` on x86-64, a class with Objective-C heritage tail-calling the
  runtime with the same address; one that is the last instruction of its
  section is read only as far as the section goes — which the pass decodes and checks: the
  metadata's descriptor word must point back at the descriptor (through the
  chained-fixup overlay on a Mach-O; through the `R_*_RELATIVE` addends on an
  ELF, which the pass now also feeds the reader, so an ELF's local witness
  tables are named too). From a struct's metadata: its size and alignment (the
  value witness table before the address point, or the builtin table an import
  names — `$sBi64_WV` is 8 bytes, `$sytWV` empty) and its field offset vector
  (32-bit entries at the descriptor's offset); from a class's: the instance
  size and alignment and the pointer-sized field offset vector (an
  Objective-C-heritage class's static offsets are the compile-time layout, the
  same values its `__objc_ivar` offset variables hold). From the reflection
  field descriptor, which the first arm already parsed: each stored property's
  name and mangled type, whose symbolic references (`\x01` a direct, `\x02` an
  indirect context descriptor reference, with a 4-byte payload) the demangler
  resolves through a hook (`demangle_swift_type`, §1.3) that the pass answers
both
  is one unlace struct per type under its dotted name — `metafix.Point { long x;
  long y; }`, a class as its object layout with a local superclass embedded as
  `super` at 0 and otherwise the `isa` word (and a Swift-native root's
  reference counts) — with field types mapped from the Swift type: the sized
  integers, `Double`/`Float`/`Bool`, `Swift.String` as its two words, a class
  reference as a pointer to that class's struct (a shell for one without a
  static layout, so the name is still right), a nested struct inline, a
  collection as its storage word under the instantiation's name, a closure as
  its two words; an optional keeps its payload's type when nil is the zero
  word (a reference, a string, a collection, a closure). A payload-less enum
  with a static layout is a C enum of its cases in declaration order (the
  values the runtime gives them, 0, 1, …) at the width its value witness
  table states, so a field or a return of that type prints its case by name;
  an optional of an integer, a float or a struct (a payload with no spare
  bit) is a two-field struct named after the instantiation, the payload then
  a one-byte `is_nil` tag; a Clang-imported type (`__C.CGSize`, `__C.NSString`)
  is the C type of that name when the image has one (DWARF, the Objective-C
  pass), inline for a struct and through a pointer for a class; in an image
  that kept its symbols, a global variable's storage symbol (`$s…vp`) types
  its data object with the variable's demangled type under the dotted name
  (`callfix.ctr.step = 2;`). Any other type
  — an enum with payloads, an imported value type (`Foundation.Date`), a
  generic instantiation without a known layout, a tuple, an existential — is
  `undefined<n>` over the bytes up to the next field, so the layout is always
  right and the names are always real; only the field's own type is withheld. A layout is refused
  whole when the field count disagrees with the descriptor, an offset
  overlaps, a type exceeds its slot, or the type's dotted path is one two
  descriptors share (private types of the same name), so nothing is ever
  read through the wrong name. What then binds: the metadata records as typed
  data (`….type_metadata` as `swift.type_metadata`, `….class_metadata`,
  `….value_witness_table`); the accessor prototypes
  (`swift.MetadataResponse Module.Type.type_metadata_accessor(void)`, so
  `return &Module.Type.type_metadata;`; the call sites pass no argument). A
  located accessor computes its address into the return register and returns
  (or tail-calls the runtime with it) without reading the request, so it takes
  none. A generic or cache accessor reads the request and gets no prototype
  here. The `self` of every class vtable getter and of every local protocol's
  witness getter (the `IsInstance` flag read, so a static property's metatype `self` is left alone; a getter whose
  body the linker folded with another type's, or with a member that is not a
  getter, gets no `self` at all — `Namer::ambiguous_self`). Swift passes
  `self` in the `swiftself` register (x20 on arm64, r13 on x86-64), which a
  locked prototype cannot name without also fixing the arity; a getter's
  arity is known, so the pass pins
  the parameter on the function — the analysis-tier form of the console's
  `map param` (`AnalysisOutput::swift_types.param_locks` →
  `Architecture::loader_param_locks` → the decompile drive's `mapped_params`),
  the rest of the signature recovered as usual — and a witness getter also
  names its two leading arguments, the `Self` metadata and the witness table
  (its `self` is the address of the value: `T *` for a struct, `Class **` for
  a class). Every other member's `self` is the `swiftcall` arm's, below.
  On the Toyota iOS app the pass locates 12,809 static metadata records (4,790
  structs, 4,811 enums, 3,208 classes; the 859 classes and 351 structs whose
  accessors look up a runtime cache are skipped), lays out 4,585 structs and
  3,205 classes with 30,997 fields (22,794 typed), and pins the `self` of 5,739
  vtable getters and 2,821 witness getters, for about 0.1 s and 3 MB over the
  naming arm. The stage test `tests/stages/swifttypes.toml` runs the
  stripped swiftc-built `swift_types_elf` with the arm off and on.
  The arm also types the result of every call to an accessor that no
  prototype covers (a local generic or runtime-initialized type's, an
  imported `…Ma` stub's) and of every call to an instantiation helper the
  helper arm below names: an accessor returns the metadata first whatever
  arguments it takes, and a generic type's accessor takes its generic
  arguments after the request, which an import's name does not tell, so
  only the result is locked, at the call site, through the per-site output
  type lock (`unlace-decomp/src/p5_types/swiftmetaresult.rs`, a
  `sitetypelock` client, 05), and the arguments stay recovered. A result
  that is a register pair or that joins another value through a phi is
  left untyped. A read outside the 16-byte record (the value witness table
  word below it, the field offset vector and generic arguments past it)
  would print as an element of an array of records; `valuewitness` keeps
  such offsets byte offsets, so these results are typed only while that
  option is on.
- **Swift helpers** (`swifthelpers`, the helper arm of the pass above,
  default-on and inert unless `swiftmetadata` is on; arm64 only;
  `crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/swift/swifthelpers.rs`):
  swiftc emits two kinds of function into every image that uses generic
  types, and a stripped image leaves them `sub_`. The arm reads every `bl`
  target in the text once and recognises them by their bodies.
  `__swift_instantiateConcreteTypeFromMangledName` (and its `Abstract`
  twin) tests a cache word and otherwise makes its one call, to
  `swift_getTypeByMangledNameInContext2` (`…InMetadataState2`), with a
  mangled name found through a 32-bit relative offset (`add xD, xB, wN,
  sxtw`). The register `xB` is based on says where the name record is: the
  cache word itself (the one-argument form, which holds the offset and the
  negated length until it is filled) or the second argument (the
  two-argument form Apple's toolchain emits). Runtime calls are recognised
  by the import a stub or PLT entry jumps to, a stripped stub decoded to
  its slot. The helper is named, given the prototype `void *f(void *cache[,
  void *name])`, and at every call whose arguments are `adrp`/`add` or
  `adr` constants the mangled name is demangled, its symbolic references
  resolved through the descriptor table as for field types above, and the
  cache word named after the type as the image's own `…MD` symbol would be
  (`hf.Box<hf.Unit>.type_metadata_demangling_cache`, typed as a metadata
  pointer). A lazy protocol witness table accessor opens with `adrp; ldr
  x0, [cache]; cbz x0; ret`, then makes a call for the concrete type's
  metadata, moves its result to x1 and calls `swift_getWitnessTable` with a
  conformance descriptor in x0 (local, or loaded from a `__got` slot). The
  type comes from that call (an instantiation helper call read as above, a
  local non-generic type's accessor, an imported `…Ma`), the protocol from
  the descriptor, and the function is named
  `<T:P>.lazy_protocol_witness_table_accessor` with the prototype `void
  *f(void)`, its cache `<T:P>.lazy_protocol_witness_table_cache`, the
  conformance's type replaced by the concrete one so two instantiations of
  one generic conformance keep apart names. The names follow the
  metadata pass's label-gated rename; a body that does not decode to these
  shapes and a call whose arguments are not constants are left alone. Both
  shapes are the shrink-wrapped ones, the cache test before any frame setup:
  a helper that saves its frame first and branches back to the epilogue
  after the runtime call, or an accessor that opens with `stp x29, x30`
