own address as SLEIGH spells the PC (`inst_start`, Thumb's `+ 4`, A32's `+ 8`) to
be PC-relative where an add or subtract reads it (RISC-V `auipc`), and keeps a
value PC-relative through an add or subtract of something that is not; the
difference of two (a switch's `sub eax,r13d` after two RIP-relative `lea`s) is a
distance, and a mask, a shift or a truncation below 32 bits of one (`movzx
ecx,al`, Thumb `uxtb`) is a number. PIC base folding exempts what it composes
through the proven base for the same reason (an ld.lld i386 PIE's `lea
eax,[ebx-0x3088]` into its first page). The recogniser is built only for an image
that maps something below the floor. Every PIE and shared object does (its
`.dynsym`, a PIE's `.interp`), so only a fixed-address executable's walk is
untouched. Nor does a folded `adr` change which constants may *start* a carry in
an `ET_DYN` image (only a visible PC does), which keeps the internal address
register of SLEIGH's `ldm` out of an ARM shared object's rows.

Measured over 375 images (the 127 above, 220 zero-based ELF images from the angr
test corpus and the vendored fixtures, 30 decbench x86-64 PIEs, and zlib linked
for seven targets by ld.lld and two by GNU ld): no row is lost, and 700 rows are
added in 67 images, each a PC-relative formation — 236 x86-64 `lea [rip]`, 179
A32 and Thumb `adr` and the 170 PLT slot reads they start, 39 AArch64 `adrp`
pairs and `adr`, and 76 RISC-V `auipc` pairs and the loads through them. 682
match an independent capstone evaluation of the instruction and its straight-line
predecessors; the other 18 match GNU objdump's `auipc` pair annotation or were
checked by hand. A PIE whose first page holds only metadata (every decbench x86-64
image) gains nothing. The walk costs no measurable time: an in-process interleaved
A/B over x86-64, AArch64, ARM and RISC-V C libraries and bash stays within ±1.5%,
the same spread an A/A run shows. Recomputing the forms costs 6 to 24 ns per
decoded instruction, 0.1–0.4% of the walk over the x86-64, AArch64 and ARM C
libraries and bash. Emitted C is unchanged.

(unlace) **PLT stubs** (always on). A GNU ld A32 PLT entry builds its GOT slot's address in
`ip` and jumps through it: `add ip,pc,#0,12` (SLEIGH renders it `adr r12,...`),
`add ip,ip,#N,20` (one more add with `--long-plt`), then `ldr pc,[ip,#M]!`. The
constant scan reads each step on its own, so it filed the PC value as a `Data`
row, and also `N<<12` once the GOT lies far enough from the stub for that
immediate to land in a mapped section: two rows per stub, neither an address the
stub uses. The walk now follows the chain in its own order
(`crates/unlace-analysis/src/listing/pltstub.rs`): each step is the
instruction the walk decoded, in the mode it chose, and an open chain waits for
the walk to decode its fall-through; it never decodes ahead. It runs on ARM images
only, and only on instructions inside the linker's stub sections (the list
`fdeinterior` uses; on ARM, `.plt` and the `.iplt` that holds a static image's
IFUNC stubs in the same template), where the linker puts its stubs: a hand-written `adr; add; ldr pc` veneer elsewhere
keeps its rows, and an image without section headers follows no chain, since
nothing there says where the stubs are. Any such instruction that sets one
register to a constant starts a chain,
whether or not that first value lands in a mapped section (a stub far from its
GOT can have its `pc + N<<20` in a gap between segments). A chain is one register set
to a constant, one or two further instructions that only add constants to it
(each write of the register is an `INT_ADD` or `INT_SUB` of exactly one value
computed from the register itself and one constant, or a `COPY` of such a sum, so
`mov ip,#K`, `movw ip,#K`, `mov ip,ip` and `add ip,ip,ip` each break the chain), then a load through it plus a constant whose value is the target of a
`BRANCHIND` (a value computed from the loaded word, such as `ldr pc` clearing the
Thumb bit, stands for it, so `ldm ip,{r0,pc}` names `pc`'s word), from a slot in
a mapped section; a chain whose slot is unmapped is not a stub. Only `COPY`, `INT_ADD` and `INT_SUB` of constants are evaluated, and
a middle step must neither touch memory nor branch. The constant rows of an open
chain are held back; the chain's instructions file no constant `Data` row once it
completes, and the load files the slot as a `Read`, which is what
IDA reports for the stub and what an x86 stub's `jmp [slot]` already gives
(register pair carrying files the same row on its own, and the two give one); the
slot's file word (the PLT's resolver) is not followed. The calls into the stub,
and its import name, are unchanged. A run that leaves the shape at any step keeps
the rows the constant scan gives it, so an `adr` whose register is then used any
other way is still a reference. GCC 14 for armhf emits the A32 stub for Thumb code
too; the Thumb-only PLT (`--thumb-plt`, M-profile) is not recognised.
The call graph reads the reference rows, so `decompile-all`
can visit functions in a different callee-first order; synthesized structures
are named as a serial run names them whatever the order, and on musl `libc.so`
(and its stripped copy) and `libstdc++.so` for ARM the output is byte-identical
with and without the chain.

(unlace) **Condition skips** (always on). SLEIGH lifts a predicated instruction (`ldrne`,
`moveq`, `popeq {..,pc}`, `bxne r3`, an instruction in a Thumb `it` block) to a
`CBRANCH` to the next instruction ahead of its own ops: the path where the
condition fails. The reference walk filed that `CBRANCH` as a `Jump` to the next
instruction, one row for every predicated instruction in the program, which no
other tool reports. Ghidra keeps a `goto inst_next` out of an instruction's
flows (`SleighInstructionPrototype` gives it `BRANCH_TO_END`, not `JUMPOUT`).
The resolved p-code no longer says `inst_next`, so the reference walk reads the
shape from the instruction's ops instead: a `CBRANCH` to the instruction's own
fall-through that other ops follow (`Classified::condition_skip`). Such a skip
stays one of the instruction's flows, so every
walk still takes it and PIC pool composition, no-return propagation, AIF and the
Listing walk see the same shape as before; only the reference walk files no row
for it, unless the skip runs into the entry of another function from an
instruction with no fall-through of its own (`bxne lr`, `ldrne pc`, `popne
{..,pc}`, the `addls pc` of a table dispatch) right before that function. Then
the skip is the one way into the other function, which the call graph counts
among its callers and tail jumps (`callbacktype`, `calleevote`), so it keeps its
`Jump`. A predicated instruction that falls through (`ldrne`, `moveq`, `strne`,
a pool word decoded as `andeq`) reaches the same entry by its fall-through,
which files no row either, so its skip files nothing. The walk holds each such
skip, with the mode it decoded the instruction in, until it ends, and decides
against the final entry set (seeds, prologue roots, entries found from calls,
focus and gap-walk entries), so the order in which it finds an entry cannot
change the answer; only a kept skip's instruction is rendered, in that mode. A conditional branch whose label is the next instruction (`bne` to the
next line) is a `CBRANCH` and nothing after it, so it keeps its `Jump`, as in
Ghidra, where its target is an operand, not `inst_next`. A predicated branch
whose label is the next instruction (`it eq; beq.w` to the next line) lifts to
the skip and then the branch, both to the next instruction; only the first is
the skip, and the branch keeps its `Jump`. A predicated
instruction with no ops of its own after the skip would keep its row too. The
rule applies to ARM images only (A32 and Thumb). The same `goto inst_next` comes
ahead of the ops of x86 `cmovcc` and `rep` string instructions, AArch64 `ccmp`,
`ccmn`, `fcmp` and `fcsel`, PowerPC conditional returns (`beqlr`), MIPS `bc1t`
and the SPARC `call`, and on those architectures each still files a `Jump` to its
own fall-through. As with the PLT stubs, the call graph reads these
rows. Where literal-pool words decoded as a predicated instruction run into the
next function's entry, the skip's row made that function look like a callee of
the one before it; without it `decompile-all` visits the functions in their real
callee-first order, which can change the types it infers (`status_caller` in the
`et_rel_status_arm.o` fixture takes `int`, the parameter type of its callee
`guarded_status`, instead of `unsigned int`; 2 of 3676 functions of an armhf
glibc `libc.so.6` change the same way). On musl
`libc.so` and its stripped copy the `decompile-all` output is byte-identical
with the option on and off.

(unlace) Every rule above widens what the walk reads out of an instruction it
reached; the complementary defect is the instructions it never reaches at all.
The descent's successors are `classify`'s static targets plus fall-through, and a
`BRANCHIND` has neither by construction — it is where the design defers to
jump-table recovery, which runs over a *decompiled* function and so is not
available to this tier. So the walk stops dead at every switch dispatch. On the
filing image, an MSVC i386 window procedure, `--from` its entry filed 61
references whose source addresses run up to the dispatch `JMP dword ptr [EAX*0x4
+ 0x4017c4]` and then resume in the epilogue: the whole 758-byte case-body region
between them was undecoded, and `unlace strings` reported the message the handler
plainly pushes with `xrefs_count: 0` and no owning function.

**Jump-table following**
(`crates/unlace-analysis/src/listing/switchtable.rs`) closes that
with one table read, of content that cannot change, bounded by the image's own
partition. The table base is the address the dispatching instruction itself
materialises — the `Data` reference the constant scan already files for it, which
is what makes the rule format-independent rather than a pattern match on `JMP
dword ptr [reg*n + imm]`. A base in a *data-space varnode* is deliberately not a
candidate: `jmp qword ptr [__imp_X]` and an ELF PLT entry encode their slot that
way, the constant scan files it as a `Jump`, and a veneer must not be read as a
one-entry table of whatever its unrelocated slot happens to hold. From the base
the entries are read in order through the same read-only dereference literal-pool
following uses, and each one is admitted only while it is pointer-sized,
pointer-aligned, drawn from allocated non-writable memory with file content, and
an address inside the **same executable section** as the dispatch — a case body
is code, and it is the dispatcher's own code. The first word that is not all of
those ends the table, which is what stops the scan at the `int3` padding after
the last case on the filing image; a run shorter than two entries is not a table
at all, because one plausible word after a constant is a coincidence and a
compiler does not lower a one-case switch through a table.

What the accepted entries become is the other half of the rule. They are queued
as successors of the **dispatching function**, not as function entries of their
own, so the case bodies are walked under the name of the switch that reaches them
and every reference they form is attributed there. That is what the query was
asked for: an agent looking for the handler that prints a message wants the
handler, not `sub_<the case body's address>`. Measured over a 33-image crackme
sweep, two images changed and neither lost a reference: the filing image gained
10 string references and 7 owned strings, and a second gained 8 and 7 — on that
one the walk also *re-attributed* three strings out of `zlib`'s `inflate`, which
had been claimed by an address inside `inflate`'s own extent because the real
entry's descent could not get past the `state->mode` switch, onto the containing
function.

(unlace) That rule reads the one table shape whose base is an operand of the jump.
Neither of its two premises holds on an x86-64 image: the base is materialized by
an instruction of its own — `lea jt(%rip),%rdx` on gcc, `LEA RDX,[__ImageBase]` on
MSVC — so the dispatch files no data reference at all, and the entries are signed
32-bit **displacements** rather than pointers, measured from the table on the gcc
form and from the image base on the MSVC one. So the whole of a `switch`'s direct
callees was missing from `unlace decompile-graph`: on the filing PE the reporter's
function listed 9 callees where Ghidra listed 33, and the missing ones were exactly
the `CALL`s inside case bodies.

**Delta-table following** closes that by asking what the branch register holds
instead of searching for a constant that might be a table. From the dispatch the
walk takes a **backward slice** over instructions it has already decoded: an
instruction joins the slice only where it defines something the chain still wants,
and the walk stops the moment the chain wants nothing. That is what keeps the cost
where the value is — a computed jump is usually not a switch at all, and `jmp *%rdx`
fed by `mov 0x8(%rax),%rdx` is settled one instruction back, because a value that
reaches the branch through an operation the fold does not model (a multiply, a mask,
a call's return) is unknown and asks for nothing further. The slice is then folded
forward through four values: a constant, a constant plus an unknown index, a word
read out of the array at that address, and that word composed with a constant. A
table is read only where the `BRANCHIND`'s own input is the last of those, so a jump
through a plain pointer, a virtual dispatch and a returned function pointer all
decline before any memory is read. A branch on a *data-space* varnode declines
first of all, which is the forwarding veneer the shipped rule already refused.

How far the table runs is the other half, and it cannot come from the entries. Two
delta tables laid back to back — which is what `-O2` gnulib's
`quotearg_buffer_restyled` has, an eleven-case table immediately followed by a
127-case one — continue each other seamlessly: read past the end of the first and
the second one's entries are real code addresses in the right section, merely
measured from the wrong base, and the walk decodes the middle of unrelated
functions. The bound therefore comes from the switch's own range check, which a
compiler always emits ahead of a table dispatch: `cmp $0xa,%r11d; ja default` lifts
to `INT_LESS(sel, 0xa)` feeding a `CBRANCH`, and eleven is the case count. The
search for it stops one instruction past that branch, so an unrelated comparison
further up the block cannot widen the bound, and a dispatch with no readable range
check is declined outright rather than read unbounded. Measured over a 16-image
sweep of the fixture corpus: no call-graph edge lost anywhere, and gained where the
image has a delta switch — `mcount_x86_64` 495 to 508 functions reachable from the
entry, the gnulib image 89 to 100, the MSVC fixture 2 to 6. `unlace strings` over the
896 KB `mcount_x86_64`, which holds 470 computed jumps, 676 ms to 704 ms.

(unlace) gcc's own dispatches kept most of a switch's callees out of that read all
the same — 3,913 of the 186,139 direct call sites in 51 x86-64 decbench binaries,
2,609 of them at `-O0`, where every computed jump of a PIE fails. Five things
were in the way, and each is now read. **Switch reach** (always on) is how far
the read follows a dispatch — the unscaled index, the long slice across calls,
the sixteen-instruction search for the range check, the masked index and the
re-read below; the slice and the search used to stop at eight instructions and
at the first call. ssh `-O2`'s dispatch at `0x42a26` in `main` read 9 of its 13
cases on the old walk and reads all 13 now.

*The `-O0` chain.* gcc spends seven instructions between its `ja` and the jump:
`mov %eax,%eax; lea 0(,%rax,4),%rdx; lea jt(%rip),%rax; mov (%rdx,%rax,1),%eax;
cltq; lea jt(%rip),%rdx; add %rdx,%rax`. The table base sits in the *unscaled*
index slot, which x86 SLEIGH spells as a multiply by one, so the slice follows a
multiply by one as a copy (a multiply by anything else still prunes the
selector's chain). The 32-bit load writes `rax = zext(eax)`, which retires the
tracked `eax` before `cltq` reads it back, so a register with no value of its
own reads as the low part of the wider register holding one, in the processor's
byte order: a constant truncated, a table entry as it is. The range check is
then ten instructions up, and it has a window of its own (sixteen instructions)
rather than the slice's.

*The range check.* The guard is the nearest conditional branch above the
dispatch that leaves its own instruction — a `cmov` or a `rep` prefix branches
only to the end of the instruction it is in, and clang's Duff's device in bash's
`internal_malloc` has a `cmovae` between its mask and its jump — and the bound
is a comparison that feeds that branch's condition —
in the branch itself, or in the nearest instruction above it that writes what
the condition reads. Instructions that leave the condition alone may sit in
between (gcc `-O2` puts a `movb $0x3f,0x34(%rsp)` between `cmpb $0x56,0x9c(%rbx)`
and its `ja`); a comparison anywhere else is not a bound, which drops the carry
a `sub $0x18,%rsp` in the dispatch chain used to contribute and the carry of a
`cmp` ahead of a `je`. Which side of the comparison the dispatch is on comes
from evaluating the condition twice, with the comparison as it comes out for a
selector above the constant `c` and for one below it and every other flag the
comparison sets clear. A branch taken for the large selector leaves the
dispatch `c + 1` cases. A branch taken for the small one leaves it the selectors
from `c` up, which bounds an unsigned `w`-byte selector at `2^(8w) - c` when that
is within `jumptablemax` and is no bound otherwise: bash's `cmp
$0xfffffffb,%r12d; jb default` guards a five-case table indexed by `sel + 5`, and
reading it as `0xfffffffb + 1` cases ran on into the table after it. The
comparison may have its constant on either side and in a temporary of the same
instruction, which is how AArch64 SLEIGH spells `cmp x8, #6` (`tmp = 6; tmpCY =
tmp <= x8`). Nothing checks that the comparison is on the selector: the nearest
one may test another value entirely. An index masked by `and $m`, followed back
over the code that falls into the dispatch through scaling, copies and zero
extensions, states at most `m + 1` cases whatever the range check says — clang
guards `switch (x & 3)` under `if (y <= 200) *p = y;` with the `cmp $0xc8`, which
read as 201 cases ran twenty entries into the next functions' tables, and the
Duff's device checks the byte count against 32 above its `and $0x7` — and where
no range check bounds the selector the mask is read only when all `m + 1`
entries are cases.

*A base far above the jump.* gcc `-O2` hoists the base out of a loop into a
callee-saved register, as far as the prologue: diff's `main` loads its option
table with `lea jt(%rip),%r15` right after the pushes and dispatches some sixty
instructions and nine calls later. The slice reaches 96 instructions back; a
call no longer ends it when everything it still wants is a register the default
prototype model lists as unaffected, and the fold keeps only those values
across the call. Stepping back over an instruction that does not fall through
(a `jmp`, a `ret`) leaves the block, so the slice stops there.

*Order.* The walk is breadth-first, and a `.cold` fragment that sorts ahead of
its parent jumps back into the parent's loop, so a dispatch can be decoded
before the code that falls into it. A read that stopped because no decoded
instruction ends where the slice needed one records that address. When any body
later decodes an instruction that falls through to it, that body reads the
table again once its own queue drains and walks the cases as its own: it reaches
the dispatch by falling into it, and it is the function the cold fragment
belongs to.

With all five, the 51 binaries miss 156 direct call sites instead of 3,913 —
none at `-O0` outside tar and e2fsck — and the call graph gains 1,868 edges and
loses three, two of which were jumps from a table read past its end. What is
left is a selector the code never range-checks because its type cannot exceed
the table (tar's `parse_expression` switches on a token type held in a byte,
whose table is followed directly by another one, so there is no safe place to
stop), and AArch64's byte and halfword tables scaled by four (`ldrb w11,
[x9,x8]; add x10,x10,x11,lsl #2; br x10`), whose entries the fold does not
compose, and a range check on another value than the selector with no mask to
overrule it.

*Predecessor edges.* (unlace; `crates/unlace-analysis/src/listing/switchflow.rs
(register_targets)`) The slice steps back by address and stops at the first
instruction that does not fall through, so a base hoisted above a `jmp` never
reaches it, and the sixteen-instruction search for the range check has the
same wall. Three shapes every x86-64 compiler emits lost whole switches to that
— every call their case bodies make, with `coverage.unwalked` and `notes`
empty: a base hoisted out of a loop above an `if/else` whose first arm ends in
`jmp` (clang `-O2`, MSVC `/O2`; the slice stops at the `jmp` seven
instructions short of the `lea`), two switches sharing one hoisted `LEA
RBP,[__ImageBase]` where the first switch's case bodies end in `jmp` or `ret`
before the second dispatch (MSVC: the second switch read 0 of 8), and a range
check more than sixteen instructions above the jump. Once a body's queue has
drained, every dispatch in it that the linear read declined is read again over
the body's own **predecessor edges** — each decoded instruction's fall-through
and branch targets, and the case edges of the switches it has read, the edges
the walk already follows forward. The value a register holds on entry to an
instruction is what each decoded predecessor leaves in it, met: asked on
demand from the `BRANCHIND`'s input back through the ops that define what it
still wants, folded through the slice's own four values, with a call killing
what the calling convention does not preserve. Predecessors that agree keep
the value, ones that disagree make it unknown, and a predecessor the walk has
not decoded — the back edge of a loop whose latch only the case bodies reach
— contributes nothing, as the linear slice never saw it either. The range
check is found on **every path** of predecessors up from the dispatch: on
each, the nearest conditional branch, whether the path leaves it by its
fall-through or by its taken side, read by the same rule as before. clang
`-O3` copies a switch's check into both arms of an `if/else` above the
dispatch's block, `cmp $7,%r15d; jbe disp` in one and `cmp $7,%r15d; ja
default` falling into it in the other; a join takes the largest count of its
paths. A check that sends its constant itself away from the dispatch (`cmp
$5,%edi; jb disp` by its taken side, MSVC's `cmp ecx,5; jae default` by its
fall-through, where `jbe`/`ja` would keep 5) states one case fewer than the
count rule reads: cases 0 to 4. Each
check must compare the **selector**: the addend of the sum that addresses
the table itself (the sum the table's load reads from, or one whose constant
is the table), which the fold could not value, followed up the path through
copies, extensions and arithmetic with a constant (the steps the masked index
is followed by), must reach the comparison still naming a register it reads, or a
copy of one made in the straight-line code just above the comparison (MSVC
copies the selector before its check and indexes the table by the copy:
`mov r10d,ecx; cmp ecx,8; jae default; ...; mov ecx,[rdx+r10*4+rvas]`, with
no write to `ecx` between the copy and the comparison), or be loaded from the address the comparison loads from (gcc's `cmpb
$0x78,(%rax,%rcx); ja; movzbl (%rax,%rcx),%edi`) with no store, call or write
to that address's registers in between; a register the calling convention
does not preserve is a different value past a call. Any other constant plus
unknown on the way is no index: a field's address (`mov 8(%rdi),%eax`) is
one, and its base register is what a comparison of another field (`cmpl
$0x800,4(%rdi)`) reads. The function's entry, a path that comes back to
itself, more than 256 predecessors visited, a conditional branch that is no
range check and a comparison of another value all bound nothing. Without that
test the far reach read
comparisons the slice never could as table sizes: Rust's `write_char` matches
an enum discriminant loaded from memory with no range check, seventeen
instructions under `cmp $0x800,%esi; jae` on the code point, and that read
as 2,049 cases ran through the next tables into the middle of other
functions, whose own dispatches it then decoded and read wrongly in turn
(cargo: 34 such reads among 139, 219 references lost). An index masked by
`and $m` caps the count at `m + 1` here as in the slice. Only a range-checked
table is read this way (the unchecked call-table read stays with the slice),
and only by the walk of the function whose extent holds the dispatch: a
body that reaches another function's dispatch through an edge into its
middle leaves it to that function's walk, which reads it linearly once the
code falling into it is decoded. A function with no declined dispatch pays
nothing; one read decodes at most 512 instructions, each once,
and a jump that is no switch — a tail call through a pointer, a virtual
dispatch — declines at the first definition the fold does not model, as the
slice does. On the issue's repro (Clang 21/22 `-O2 -fPIE -pie`, MSVC 19.50
`/O2`) all four functions read 8 of 8 case helpers where three read 0 of 8 or 8
of 16; on gcc 15 `-O2` the hoisted-loop shape stays unread, because gcc keeps
the base in a caller-saved `%r8` across calls whose bodies it has seen
(`-fipa-ra`), which no model of the default calling convention admits. On bash
`unlace strings` owns 29 more literals (1,031 to 1,060) at the same 0.43 s;
`unlace xrefs` on a 14.5 MB libavcodec goes from 5.49 s to 5.61 s.

*What is left is said.* (unlace; `crates/unlace-cli/src/xrefs.rs
(unresolved_jumps_note)`) Every decoded computed jump on a register or a
loaded temporary that neither read resolved to a switch or a call table is
recorded (`XrefIndex::unresolved_computed_jumps`; a jump through a pointer
slot — `jmp *slot(%rip)`, a PLT entry, or crt's `mov slot(%rip),%rax; jmp
*%rax`, which the fold reads as a slot and never a table — and a trap's
`BRANCHIND` on what its own `CALLOTHER` yields are not ones), and `unlace
xrefs` puts them in `coverage.notes`: for `--from` a function, the ones inside
it; for a `--to` that found nothing, every one in the image, since the
reference asked about may sit in a case body the walk never decoded. A miss
is no longer silent.

A complete call graph is not a better one for every consumer. Case bodies are
where an interpreter recurses, so the new edges merge recursive functions into
larger strongly connected components of `decompile-all`'s callee-first plan, and
`protoorder` (`cycles`) gives no member of a cycle the prototypes of its callees:
bash `-O0`'s `execute_*` recursion grows from 206 to 367 functions and 33 of its
signatures change, mostly to plainer integer types (`extract_arithmetic_subst`
from `char *(char *,int *)` to `unsigned long(unsigned long,unsigned long)`,
`execute_command`'s `struct_69 *` to `unsigned long`), as do dash's
`subevalvar` and `evaltreenr` and coreutils `numfmt`'s `main`. With `protoorder
off` those functions come out the same with the option on and off.

(unlace) Both reads stop at the engine's own jump-table ceiling,
`Architecture::max_jumptable_size` — 1024 unless `option jumptablemax <n>` raises
it — so one value decides how far a switch is followed in both tiers. A range
check that states more cases than the ceiling is not a reason to decline: the
first `jumptablemax` entries are still read and walked, and the walk records the
switch as **truncated** (`SwitchTable`, with the case count the range check
states and the number read, which is zero when the ceiling is below the two
entries a table needs). A table with no range check that reads up to the
ceiling is recorded the same way, with no stated count.

(unlace, GH-299) Neither read covers the dispatch Cortex-M firmware uses for
almost every switch, and the function-discovery walk (`walk.rs`) had no table
read at all: a computed jump there has no successor, so the case region behind
every `tbb`/`tbh` stayed undecoded, and the AIF gap walk planted entries in it —
a case body that opens with a common prologue and ends in its own return is a
valid subroutine with a known fingerprint. **Thumb offset tables**
(`crates/unlace-analysis/src/listing/thumbswitch.rs`, always on)
read them in both walks. `tbb [pc,rN]` and `tbh [pc,rN,lsl #1]` jump to
`inst_next + 2 * table[rN]`, where the byte or halfword table starts at
`inst_next`; the dispatch's own p-code is folded through the same lattice as the
delta-table read, extended with a narrow table word and its doubling, and only
this PC-relative form — table and base both the instruction's own `inst_next` —
is an answer. The table states no length either, so the count again comes from
the range check: the `cmp rN,#n` the dispatch sits behind lifts to
`INT_LESSEQUAL(n, rN)`, and when a conditional branch follows it within three
instructions with nothing in between writing `rN` or overwriting the comparison
flags, the table has `n + 1` entries if `bhi` sends indices above `n` away from
the dispatch, and `n` if `bcs` sends indices at or above `n` away. The condition's
p-code must establish that upper bound; reading the same flags with the opposite
polarity (`bls` or `bcc`) is insufficient. A branch to the dispatch itself,
intervening control flow, or a signed condition establishes no such bound, so
neither it nor a dispatch with no check is read. Over the jump-table ceiling the first `jumptablemax` entries are
read, and the xrefs walk records the switch as truncated like any other table. Because the offsets are
unsigned and the cases are laid out after the table, an entry that lands inside
the table, or outside the dispatcher's executable section, refuses the whole
read rather than truncating it. The cases become same-function successors of the
dispatch, as a branch target is, plus a code reference from it. Scored against
the symbol tables of the 93 non-u-boot 32-bit ARM ELFs in the decbench corpus,
default mode: mid-body entries 6,946 to 4,375 net (2,606 gone; 35 new, all
gap-walk entries in other holes of the functions whose cases are now decoded)
and true function starts 41,822 to 42,180 (the functions only a case
body calls), with none lost; on the Keil-built `CMSIS_DAP.axf`, whose tables
sit behind `bcs`, 18 to 16 and 300 to 301; the A32 u-boot images and the i386
PE corpus are unchanged. A function a case body calls is now walked too, and
its own tail `b` takes the target in as any branch the walk follows does: on an
armhf `libc.so.6` a case body calls `0x73248`, whose tail `b` pulls in
`0x73078`, a true start nothing else reaches, so it is no longer listed;
`tailcallentry` (on by default with `listing`) recovers it. The walk decodes the
case bodies, and what they call, on every Listing build, so discovery alone
takes longer where tables are read (`unlace functions` about 8% on betaflight and
that libc), while a whole-binary run gets faster because no case body is
decompiled as a function of its own. It is ARM-only and needs a walk, so it is inert without `--option listing on`.

**A32 tables in the reference walk.** The two A32 forms the Listing walk follows
under `armframes` (above, `a32switch.rs`) are read by the xrefs walk too,
with the same reader and the same option. A guarded `addls pc,pc,rN,lsl #2`
walks each `b caseN` after `b default`; a guarded `ldrls pc,[pc,rN,lsl #2]`
walks each word after it. The A32 read comes before the table-base read: the
dispatch's PC-relative operand names the dispatch itself, which is not a table.
The cases are the dispatcher's own code, walked as its successors with the state
the dispatch holds, so a GOT base made before the dispatch reaches every case
(the `picpool` rule above). The dispatch files one `Jump` to each case, as
Ghidra's `ArmAnalyzer` adds a computed-jump reference per case. The words of an
`ldr` table are data the dispatch reads: they are not decoded and file no
pointer row, which matches Ghidra, whose ARM switch recovery labels and
disassembles the targets but adds no reference from the words. A predicated
dispatch lifts as a skip to `b default` ahead of its jump. `classify` keeps that
skip as one of the jump's flows with no fall-through, on every architecture and
under every option, so PIC pool composition, no-return propagation and every
other consumer of the instruction see one shape: a pool word loaded before
`bxne r3` still reaches the `add rN,pc,rM` after it along the skip, and a
function that leaves through `bxne r0` or `bl abort` is proved no-return
exactly as before. Where A32 tables are read, both walks only recognise the
skip (`Classified::predicated_skip` in
`crates/unlace-analysis/src/listing/classify.rs`): a computed jump
whose only flow is its skip is read as a table. Under `armframes off`, and on
every other architecture, no A32 table is read. On ARM the skip files no `Jump`
row under every option (the condition-skip rule above). The switch record states the guard's case count, so a table longer than
`jumptablemax` is marked truncated. A dispatch whose table gives no case (a run
shorter than two entries, or `b caseN` slots past the section end) states no
count, and the other table readers run on it only when it is unpredicated: a predicated computed jump
that is no A32 table gets no table at all. A literal-pool word after a call that the walk falls into is one
such jump, since a GOT offset like `0x000ff4a8` decodes as `andeq pc,pc,...`, and the pool words after it
must not become its cases. The reader takes a dispatch only when its index is scaled by four (`lsl #2`),
so 8-byte slots and an unscaled `add pc,pc,rN` are not read as tables, and an `ldr` table ends before its
first word with bit 0 set, an interworking target rather than an A32 case. A dispatch the walk reaches before the
guard that falls into it (a branch into the dispatch, or breadth-first order)
waits at the address the guard read stopped at and is read again, A32 reader
first, once that code is decoded.
Without this, the walk stopped at the dispatch and followed only `b default`.
GCC 14 no longer emits either form from C in ARM state (it compresses the table
to bytes, `ldrb rN,[rT,rN]; add pc,pc,rN,lsl #2`); that form is not read. Thumb
`ldr pc` tables are not read either: their PC is 4 bytes ahead, not 8.

**AArch64 compact tables** (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/listing/a64switch.rs`,
always on) are read in both walks by the register-chain fold above. clang and
gcc lower an AArch64 `switch` to a table of byte, halfword or word offsets in
`__const`/`.rodata`, each scaled to instructions and added to an `adr` base
(`adrp`/`add` table; `adr` base; `ldrh w13,[x11,x10,lsl #1]`; `add
x12,x12,x13,lsl #2`; `br x12`; gcc's `add x0,x1,w0,sxtb #2` reads a byte back
signed). The fold's narrow table word, shifted left by one to three (`lsl #2`,
or a multiply by two or four) and added to a constant, is the case address
(`switchtable.rs (Val::Relative)`), and the dispatch slice follows a
constant left shift so the entry's `lsl #2` reaches the load. The count comes
from the range check, read the way the delta-table read reads one, with one
more shape: when the instruction before the dispatch's block does not fall
through, the check may be the branch *into* the block (`cmp w9,#0xb; b.ls
dispatch`, clang's second table of a `switch` over two value ranges), found
among the decoded instructions above the block head and read with the taken
arm as the in-range one (`switchtable.rs (entering_guard)`). In the
Listing walk every aligned word of the executable ranges counts as decoded
for that search: AArch64 instructions are four bytes, so the code above a
dispatch reads the same whether the walk reached it yet or not. A table with
no range check at all is read when `switchextent` (default on) bounds it: a
function's jump tables are emitted back to back in one read-only section, so
the table runs to the lowest table of the same function above it, found by
decoding the function's extent (its entry to the next known entry, or a MiB)
linearly and naming the table of each computed jump the fold proves reads
one (`crates/unlace-analysis/src/listing/switchextent.rs`);
what an instruction writes after a branch inside its own p-code (an AArch64
`csel`/`csinc`) is unknown to the fold, as in chapter 2's extent decode.
A function's last table has no such bound and is not read: an object the
function merely reads may sit anywhere in the section, and a bound taken
from one could run the table on into another function's, whose entries are
plausible code addresses measured from the wrong base. The cases are the
dispatcher's own successors, so no gap entry is planted on them: cmark-gfm's
re2c scanner `_scan_html_block_start` listed as 104 bytes plus five `sub_`
functions is one function of 4,484 bytes, and the framework's 442 functions
are 407, the 35 case bodies gone; the Swift `AssetItem` copy helper of a
13 KB iOS app function keeps its 27-case enum dispatch. The `compacttable_aarch64`
fixture pins clang's byte table (`ldrb; adr; add x10,x10,x11,lsl #2; br x10`):
every case callee has `dispatch` as caller in `unlace xrefs`
(`crates/unlace-cli/tests/xrefs_switch_case_calls.rs`).

(unlace, GH-299) **Bounded i386 switch coverage** (`x86listingswitch`, default-off;
`crates/unlace-analysis/src/listing/x86listingswitch.rs`) extends
the discovery Listing for linked little-endian i386 ELF and PE images. It
recognizes a computed jump whose own p-code loads a four-byte destination from
`table + index * 4`, or from `table + byte * 4` where the byte is read from
`index_table + index` (MSVC's two-level form, `movzx edx, byte [ecx+idx];
jmp [edx*4+table]`). The index bytes are read for exactly the proved range,
and the pointer table for every entry up to the largest byte read. A word
loaded from a frame slot (`[ebp-0x8b4]`) is an index of its own, the same at
every load of that slot. Unoptimized MSVC code compares the slot and reloads
it for the jump (`cmp dword ptr [ebp-0x8b4],0x64; ja; mov ecx,[ebp-0x8b4]`),
so the guard bounds the reloaded value too. Once such a slot is read, a store
anywhere later in the path refuses the proof. An unsigned guard on that exact whole 32-bit index must
constrain the dispatch along one local predecessor chain, with at most sixteen
instructions and 256 p-code operations. The proof tracks machine-width values,
flag arithmetic, and supported normalization; it refuses unrelated comparisons,
signed bounds, unknown upper bits, partial-register clobbers, unproved address
wrap, calls, and alternate incoming edges that bypass the guard. Incoming edges
come from decoded instruction flow and previously admitted table edges, so
dropping captured references in a partition-only Listing does not weaken the
proof. The nearest preceding function entry supplies no ownership evidence.

The reader takes exactly the proved number of aligned words, capped by the
live `jumptablemax`; fewer than two entries is not a switch. Every byte read
must belong to allocated, read-only, file-backed data, and every destination
must be in the dispatch's executable section. No destination may lie inside
an instruction that starts in the fifteen bytes below it, even where another
instruction also starts at it: two words of one table a byte apart decode
both, and the overlapping decode can reach code nothing else does, so the
re-check against the completed candidate refuses it. An invalid in-bound word refuses
the whole table. No missing proof falls back to an unbounded pointer scan. A
callback word immediately after a four-case table therefore stays outside its
successors. `PoolImage::contains_bytes` enforces the complete read contract;
the existing object loader already clips PE data to its virtual/raw section
bounds. This does not change the separate xrefs walk's pointer-scan policy.

After the ordinary serial or parallel walk finishes, shared reconciliation
keeps that ordinary model as the fallback and builds an isolated candidate.
Proved targets are instruction roots, not function entries; ordinary calls from
newly reached code retain the existing function-claim rules. Reconciliation
collects dispatches in address order, extends their decoded successors, and
repeats for at most sixteen rounds. Before publication it proves every admitted
dispatch again against the completed candidate, including newly exposed direct
and computed incoming edges and new function claims. An invalidated proof, a
newly conflicting entry, a required seventeenth round, or exhausted memory
budget discards the whole candidate, including earlier independent expansions.
No provisional instructions, references, or callees escape into the fallback.
Resume rebuilds ordinary coverage before applying this feature, including when
the option is disabled after an earlier expansion, so extended coverage cannot
be mistaken for ordinary fallback provenance.

The budget is at most 1 GiB and one quarter of available host memory, or
128 MiB when availability is unknown. It accounts for the ordinary model,
added instructions, pending targets/references, and retained dispatch edges;
incoming-edge collection and table rows also consume a checked aggregate
record allowance before allocation. Resident growth is checked when available,
but its absence does not remove the record allowance. Refusal preserves the
ordinary model rather than retaining an incomplete expansion.

Coverage records exact decoded instruction members. Cases may surround an
independent function and an undefined gap: neither the intervening bytes nor
an entry inside the first/last case span becomes owned by the dispatcher.
Existing seeds and direct-call claims remain authoritative; an established
case-entry conflict refuses the proof. Separate entry heuristics, including
`fast_funcdisc` and tail-call entry recovery, retain their own policies. The
feature remains opt-in because additional ordinary successor coverage can
change which otherwise unreferenced functions the gap walk discovers. The
measured corpus loses seven real tail-callee entries. Newly discovered entries
can also make existing `funcboundflow` truncate emitted branches: crypt32's
`0x6e8ee740` loses `memcpy` paths when `0x6e8eea21` becomes an entry, and
`0x6e904a20` loses part of case five. Local table admission is not proof of
improved whole-function C. Kernelbase's `GetComputerNameExW` also changes a
520-byte array into a scalar used as a large output buffer. The preserved
`abace009d9` audit reviewed 726 changed comparisons and 1,482 code or
semantic-metadata hunks. A fresh `e265bf23` capture strictly verifies
726 comparisons and 1,480 hunks, preserving every semantic API field,
399 removed addresses and all seven true-start losses. Exact prior content
permits annotation reuse; eighteen changed contexts and their 27 hunks were
manually read again. The same seventeen addresses still fail in both arms,
with no success-to-error transition or error repair. Fresh raw results
retain eleven `new-error` labels from changed stopping diagnostics and six
identical errors; natural queries omit
the budget flag and all actual failures report 120 seconds, while forced
supplements set it explicitly. Forced interior requests are not newly valid
entries. Completed review is not a claim of correct whole-image C.

On latest tested base `dd4f9fde`, all 141 entry inventories and 744 arm models
remain exact, as do complete-record panels on 20 controls and 13 known unsafe
anchors. Native serial/parallel/stream fixture exports pass. The full 21-image
C capture remains explicitly labeled with its `e265bf23` predecessor; these
bounded current-base checks do not imply a new full-corpus C capture.
Contention-logged current-base timing records enabled Wine discovery at
+7.17% wall and +7.17% child CPU. All samples/ranges are retained;
`quiet=false` does not certify a tight global overhead bound. The feature stays
off in every mode and adds no new function-boundary or tail-call policy. It is a
partial improvement for GH-299; its original private PE and crackme
acceptance cannot be established without those artifacts.

(unlace) The walk's decode set is global, so it cannot say how long one function
is: code two entries share is decoded under whichever entry reached it first. A
gcc `.cold` fragment sits below its parent and jumps back into the parent's body,
so the fragment's walk claims the parent's tail and the parent's own walk stops
where that tail begins (on python3.10, `PyType_Ready`'s 12 KB body claimed 200
instructions and its 1.9 KB fragment 2,782). `build_measured` therefore keeps the
successor graph the walk decoded, one `(vma, len, falls through)` row per
instruction plus one row per branch or switch-case edge, and
`function_instruction_counts` re-runs each requested entry's own descent over it,
stopping at every other seeded entry and at a caller-given cap. Shared code then
counts for every entry that reaches it, whatever order the walk claimed it in.
The plain `build` keeps no graph, so `unlace xrefs`, `strings`, `crypto` and the
plain `unlace functions --json` listing pay nothing for it. `unlace functions
--summary` (and `--reachable-from`, which already walk the image) count up to
`maxinstruction + 1` to flag, before any decompile, the functions whose body
exceeds `maxinstruction`, and list each truncated switch under the function whose
extent contains its dispatch. On the MSVC state machine that motivated it (a
16.6 MB function dispatching through a 90,781-entry image-base-relative table),
the default walk reads 1024 entries and reports the switch; with `jumptablemax
100000` it reads the whole table, and the body the cases reach is over the
100000-instruction budget.


(unlace) The same pool word is a second defect one surface over, in the **listing**
rather than the reference walk. A function's extent contains its pool, so a
straight-line disassembly of `main` walks off the end of the code and decodes the
constant: `1337ARM`'s `main` ended `ldmia sp,{r4,r11,sp,pc}` and then
`0x8458 39050000 andeq r0,r0,r9, lsr r5` — four bytes nothing executes, listed as
an instruction, in place of the success constant `0x539` the program is about.
**Pool-word folding** (`crates/unlace-console/src/litpool.rs`, fed by
`ConsoleProgram::add_fixed_refs_at`) lists such a word as the constant it holds
(`.word 0x00000539`) instead. The evidence is the listing's own and nothing
wider: as each row is decoded, the fixed addresses it names are harvested from
its p-code — the constant locations it READS, in the two shapes SLEIGH spells one
in (a `LOAD` off a constant address, and a direct memory varnode), and the
constant addresses its flow ops name. A word read by some instruction in the
range, and branched to by none of them, is data.

That the evidence has to be *in the range* is what makes the rule predictable and
steerable rather than a global guess: listing the pool word on its own contains
no such load, so it decodes exactly as before, and that is the escape hatch. Four
further refusals bound it — a writable section (a GOT slot is read by address
too, and a writable `.text` is a packer), an address a function symbol sits on
(code by declaration), an unaligned or non-scalar width, and a width that does
not tile a whole number of decoded rows. As in the reference walk, the width has
to come from the ACCESS rather than from the address varnode, which a `LOAD`
makes pointer-sized whatever it reads; and an instruction's own fall-through is
not counted as a branch target, because every predicated ARM instruction lowers
to a `CBRANCH` over its body and a literal pool is a run of words that decode as
predicated instructions — counting it would veto every pool word but the first. The last one is what keeps the listing
stable: a fold only ever merges whole rows over the same bytes, so no address
after it can shift and a wrong fold costs one mis-rendered row rather than a
re-aligned listing. The residual false positive is a literal that lands on real
code — `cortexm_poolentry_le32` carries one deliberately, where a pool reference
resolves onto an undiscovered function's first word — and it costs exactly that
one row, with the bytes beside it and the raw decode one command away.

(unlace) The tiling refusal has a prerequisite the walk itself has to supply: a
pool word is only foldable if it **starts a decoded row**, so anything that puts
the listing off the instruction grid vetoes every word after it. A byte the
translator refuses is listed as a `.byte` row rather than ending the listing, and
where the walk resumes from one is architecture-dependent
(`crates/unlace-console/src/disasm.rs (resume_grid, recovery_span)`).
Advancing one byte is right where any address can start an instruction and wrong
where they must be aligned: on ARM a refused pool word cost one byte, and the
four rows after it started at `main+0xd5`, `+0xd9`, `+0xdd` and `+0xe1` —
addresses no ARM instruction can begin at, so the four remaining pool words the
function's own `ldr`s named were not row starts and none of them folded. One
refused byte therefore took the whole pool with it. The recovery row instead runs
**to the next grid boundary**, in one row rather than a run of one-byte rows,
which is what puts the following row back on the grid. The grid is the alignment
every row decoded so far shares — the OR of their addresses and sizes — so an ARM
listing of 4-byte rows resumes on 4 and a Thumb listing that has decoded a 2-byte
row resumes on 2; an architecture that declares no instruction alignment
(SLEIGH `define alignment=1`), or a listing with nothing decoded yet to infer a
grid from, keeps the byte-at-a-time recovery unchanged.

(unlace) The walk also has to carry its own **end of mapped memory**, because the
load image will not stop it. `LoadImage::load_fill` answers a read that STARTS on
a mapped address for its whole length, zero-filling every byte past the last
segment it crosses — the upstream BFD contract
(`crates/unlace-analysis/src/loadimage_object.rs`), and what makes a
`.bss` tail read back as zeroes rather than as a hole. Only the start address is
therefore ever checked, and a windowed listing that runs off the end of the code
decodes the fill: on a crackme whose executable `PT_LOAD` stops at `0x080d1904`
with the next segment a page and a half above it, `unlace disassemble 0x80d18b0
--count 30` walked to `0x80d191b` and reported eight `ADD byte ptr [EAX],AL` rows
out of bytes that are not in the file — while `unlace disassemble 0x80d190b`, an
address inside the same hole, correctly refused. The listing clips its own length
to the **contiguous mapped run** holding the start
(`crates/unlace-console/src/disasm.rs (mapped_run)`, over
`LoadImage::get_segments`): adjacent and overlapping segments are one run, since
a listing crossing from one `PT_LOAD` into the next at the byte the first ends
has crossed no hole, and a loader that publishes no segments at all (the XML
`<binaryimage>` corpus, a relocatable object) is silence rather than a bound. A
decode that would STRADDLE the bound is refused the same way the translator's own
refusal is, so the mapped bytes under it list as `.byte` rather than as an
instruction the file only half contains; and the stop is stated in the listing's
`notes`, with the next mapped address, because a short answer is otherwise
indistinguishable from one the caller's own `--count` ended.

## 1.7 The no-return family

Whether a call falls through decides the CFG of every caller, so no-return facts
are program-prep facts, computed before any function is decompiled. Five analyzers
cooperate, each subsuming the last's blind spot; all of them emit the same
`NoReturnFact` through the same commit arm (address-resolved
`set_function_no_return`, §1.1), and the flow consequence — an artificial halt at
the call site, dead fall-through never decoded — is inherited from the engine's
flow layer (`crates/unlace-lift/src/p2_lift/flow.rs`), never
re-implemented per pass.

**Known names** (`noreturn_known`,
`crates/unlace-analysis/src/loader/noreturn.rs (NoReturnKnownPass)`, the
`NoReturnFunctionAnalyzer` port) flags every function symbol whose name — leading
underscores stripped in a loop, so `__stack_chk_fail` matches `stack_chk_fail` —
appears on a shipped list, under upstream's namespace guard (global names and
exactly `std::`, never a class method like `Menu::_exit`). Which list applies is
format- and language-selected, the `noReturnFunctionConstraints.xml` model: the
vendored ELF list (`crates/unlace-analysis/data/ElfFunctionsThatDoNotReturn`
— `exit`, `abort`, `__assert_fail`, `pthread_exit`, `__cxa_throw` and the C++
terminate family, and two unlace divergence blocks appended in place, each fenced by
its own `# (unlace divergence, DIV-nn)` comment: (DIV-21) the genuinely-unconditional
libc additions upstream omits — the BSD `err`/`errx`/`verr`/`verrx`/`errc`/`verrc`
family, `quick_exit`, `__assert_perror_fail`, `__chk_fail`, `__libc_fatal`, `__fortify_fail_abort`;
`warn`/`warnx` return and stay out — and (DIV-78) the libstdc++ `std::__throw_*`
family, below — plus a GNU Fortran block: the four libgfortran fatal diagnostics
`_gfortran_runtime_error`, `_gfortran_runtime_error_at`, `_gfortran_os_error` and
`_gfortran_os_error_at`, which libgfortran declares no-return; the warning
`_gfortran_runtime_warning_at` and the recoverable I/O error
`_gfortran_generate_error` return and stay out, and the block lists exact names, not
a `_gfortran_` prefix), widened by a Rust wildcard list (`core::panicking::panic*`,
`handle_alloc_error`, `rust_begin_unwind`) or a Go exact list (`runtime.gopanic`,
`runtime.throw`, `runtime.goexit`, …) when source-language detection fires (§1.4),
or replaced by the PE/Mach-O list (`__fastfail`, `_invoke_watson`, the same GNU
Fortran block, plus the shared C names) off-ELF. (unlace) Each list also carries a
block of names a public declaration marks no-return and the vendored list lacked,
its source named in the comment above it: on ELF, glibc's `_Exit`, `thrd_exit`
and `__pthread_unwind_next`, libstdc++'s and libc++abi's `__cxa_rethrow`,
`__cxa_bad_typeid`, `__cxa_pure_virtual`, `__cxa_deleted_virtual` and
`__cxa_throw_bad_array_new_length`, `std::unexpected`, `std::rethrow_exception`,
`std::nested_exception::rethrow_nested`, `std::throw_with_nested` and the
`<optional>`/`<variant>`/`<format>` throw helpers, and libc++'s `std::__1`
throw helpers in their mangled spelling; off-ELF the same C++ runtime names and
the Darwin ones (`_Exit`, `longjmp`, `siglongjmp`, `pthread_exit`, the `err`
family, `__assert_rtn`, `dispatch_main`, `objc_exception_throw`,
`objc_exception_rethrow`, `objc_terminate`); on Go, the calls the Go compiler
ends a block at or lowers bounds and SIMD panics to (`runtime.block`,
`runtime.panicrangestate`, `runtime.panicBounds`, `runtime.panicExtend`,
`runtime.panicSimdImm` and the `panicBounds64`/`32`/`32X` helpers) and `os.Exit`.
A second such block per list (#28) names, each with its declaration in the
comment above it: on ELF, the remaining C++ runtime exits (`__cxa_call_terminate`,
`__cxxabiv1::__unexpected`, `_Unwind_SjLj_Resume`, libstdc++'s
`std::__throw_bad_weak_ptr`, `std::__throw_bad_any_cast` and
`std::__glibcxx_assert_fail`), newlib's `__assert_func`, Android's
`__android_log_assert`, OpenBSD's `__stack_smash_handler`, libiberty's `xexit` and
`xmalloc_failed`, CPython's `Py_FatalError`, `_Py_FatalErrorFunc`, `Py_Exit` and
`Py_ExitStatusException`, the two unrecoverable UBSan handlers, and the Linux
kernel's `__noreturn` functions from objtool's `noreturns.h` whose names a user
program is unlikely to reuse (`make_task_dead`, `kthread_exit`, `usercopy_abort`,
`start_kernel`, …; `do_exit` and `rest_init` stay out); off-ELF,
`_Unwind_Resume`, `_Unwind_SjLj_Resume`, `__cxa_call_unexpected`,
`__cxa_call_terminate`, `__stack_chk_fail`, Darwin's `abort_with_reason` and
`abort_with_payload`, and the CPython exits; on PE only (the Win32 list), the MSVC
CRT /GS reporters (`__report_gsfailure`, `__report_securityfailure(Ex)`),
`_amsg_exit`, the Microsoft STL `std::_X*` throwers in both decorations and
demangled, `std::unexpected`, nine MFC `AfxThrow*Exception` functions,
`_com_raise_error`, and ntdll's `RtlExitUserProcess`, `RtlExitUserThread` and
`RtlRestoreContext`; for Rust, `__rust_alloc_error_handler`,
`__rdl_alloc_error_handler` and `core::panicking::assert_failed_inner`; for Go,
`runtime.goexit`, `runtime.morestackc` and `runtime.dieFromException`. Names whose
declaration lets them return stay out: `_Unwind_Resume_or_Rethrow` returns when no
handler is found, and `_com_issue_error` calls a replaceable handler.
glibc's `__assert` is left out: stripped of its underscores it would name a
program's own returning `assert`. The Rust list's mangled prefixes only match
legacy symbols (`_ZN4core9panicking5panic17h...`), and current rustc emits v0
symbols (`_RNvNtCs..._4core9panicking5panic`) whose crate hash sits mid-name, so
it also carries Rust paths — `core::panicking::panic_fmt`,
`core::option::unwrap_failed`, `core::slice::index::slice_index_fail`, the
`panic_const::panic_const_*` family and the rest of the `-> !` functions of
core, alloc and std. For a Rust ELF each symbol is demangled without its hash
(`{:#}`), a trailing generic argument list is dropped
(`core::panicking::assert_failed::<i64, i64>` names
`core::panicking::assert_failed`), and the path is compared against those
entries; an item nested inside a listed function (`<begin_panic::Payload as
PanicPayload>::as_str`) never matches. The scan mirrors the exact symbol
streams the loader installs and emits the *install* address — for a UND import, the
PLT-stub address, since the `.dynsym` entry is address 0 and demangling means a
raw-name lookup would miss. One name is matched only as an import and only as
spelled: `__stack_chk_fail_local`, which glibc `debug/stack_chk_fail_local.c`
declares `noreturn`, at each import resolver address and each relocatable
object's undefined code extern, so its call prints `// no-return` and nothing
after it. Neither `_stack_chk_fail_local`, `stack_chk_fail_local` nor a helper
the image defines matches: a linked image's own helper is no-return only when
its body shows it.
Name-based: free, exact, and useless on stripped custom wrappers.

`crates/unlace-analysis/src/loader/rustnoreturn.rs` additionally
recognizes the complete legacy-mangled `std::process::exit` path in a Rust ELF.
The suffix must contain exactly sixteen lowercase hexadecimal hash digits and
the final mangling terminator; malformed and extended spellings refuse. The
vendored list is unchanged. This supplies the same address-keyed
no-return fact as the existing panic entries. This preserves the exit-code argument
and preceding effects while preventing flow into the compiler's dead trap padding;
existing structuring can then duplicate the closed exit tail without introducing
a Rust panic for a reachable branch. Other namespaces, longer names such as
`std::process::exit_status`, and non-Rust compiler selections do not gain this fact.
The rule does not infer no-return from a leaf named `exit`, recover stripped
wrappers, or add a Rust-v0 signature.

**Pclntab names** (the `gonoreturn` pass,
`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/pclntab/gonoreturn.rs
(GoNoReturnPass)`, unlace, gated by `noreturn_known`, Go-detected binaries only;
formerly its own option): the known-names
pass above reads the object's symbol tables, and a production Go binary is
stripped — both tables gone, zero facts emitted, so the whole vendored Go list
(`runtime.gopanic`, `runtime.panicshift`, `runtime.panicunsafestringlen`, …)
went unused on exactly the binaries it was vendored for, and every
`runtime.panic*` call site kept a bogus fall-through edge (rendered as flow
into the INT3 padding after the function, and it breaks the `gomorestack`
fold's shape wherever the stack-growth arm follows such a call). The names
survive stripping in the pclntab, so this pass walks the same table the
`gopclntab` pass recovers names from — same `recover_go_table` parse, same
executable-range admission — and matches each recovered `(addr, name)` against
the same vendored list with the same reader (`name_matches`), emitting
ordinary address-keyed `NoReturnFact`s through the same commit arm. Pass order
installs the pclntab names before the no-return arm resolves addresses, so the
facts land whether or not a `.symtab` exists; unstripped, they are idempotent
duplicates of `noreturn_known`'s. Registered only for `Compiler::Go` (beside
`gopclntab`, preserving that pass's appended-last contract), so every non-Go
pass set is byte-identical; `option noreturn_known off` disables it together
with the symbol-table pass.
The Go name list leaves `runtime.panicCheck1` returnable so callers retain
the path from the conditional check to `runtime.gopanic`.

**Discovered, ≥3 evidence** (`noreturn_disc`,
`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/noreturn_disc/mod.rs`, the
`FindNoReturnFunctionsAnalyzer` evidence tally; Listing-gated, default-on per
DIV-22 as in Ghidra): a callee is concluded no-return when at least **3** of its
call sites (`EVIDENCE_THRESHOLD`) show no valid fall-through, plus a bounded
fixpoint promotion for a caller whose body contains a terminal call to an
already-concluded callee and no returning path anywhere: no RETURN, no jump out of
the function to a callee not known no-return, no computed jump and no
fall-through-less call to such a callee (a tail call returns when its target does;
trustd's `_GetAssetFileURL` returns through `b _objc_autoreleaseReturnValue`, and
only its landing pad ends in `bl _Unwind_Resume`, which made every call to it
print `// no-return`). The threshold buys robustness to
disassembly noise at the price of blindness to rarely-called functions; and the
predicate has a structural blind spot: a no-return call followed by alignment **NOP
padding** reads as a valid fall-through and contributes no evidence at all.

What counts as "no valid fall-through" is the positive-evidence predicate of
`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/noreturn_disc/discstrict.rs`
(DIV-92; formerly the `noreturn_discstrict` option, now simply how
`noreturn_disc` reads a call site). A call with no fall-through address at all —
a tail jump lowered to a call — is evidence: that is a property of the call
instruction. A call whose p-code ends in a RETURN behind a CBRANCH to the next
instruction has a fall-through there (`listing/classify.rs`; unlace#756): SPARC
lifts `call` as `didrestore = 0; CALL f; if (didrestore == 0) goto next; RETURN`,
the RETURN only for a callee that ran `restore` in its delay slot, and reading
the last op alone made every SPARC call a terminal one, so any function with
three callers in a linked image was concluded no-return. For its *successor* only **positive** evidence counts: the successor
is data (outside every executable range, so the compiler emitted nothing there to
fall into), the successor is an x86 `int3` (MSVC, and clang and rustc targeting
Windows, plant the trap after a call that does not return: `call
__CxxThrowException@8; int3`), or the successor is another function's entry (the
compiler left the caller no tail at all). The promotion rule skips an `int3` in
the caller's body rather than reading its lifted RETURN as a returning path, and
`noreturn_propagate` skips a trailing `int3` as padding when it locates the last
real instruction, so a static-CRT `_Xlen` (`call __CxxThrowException@8; int3`)
is concluded no-return once its callee is. On SLABHIDDevice.dll (i386 MSVC, no
symbols, default `auto` mode, so the Listing is built) this names
`__CxxThrowException@8` and the helpers that only throw. The legacy tally had a third arm ahead of those two — the
successor is not a decoded instruction start.

That third arm is a statement about unlace, not about the program. The Listing walk
(§1.7) pushes **every** call's fall-through onto its per-function instruction
worklist unconditionally, and that worklist drains before the function is left, so
a call's successor is always attempted; it fails to become an instruction start in
exactly three ways — `decode_one` returned an error, the decode was zero-length, or
the address is outside every executable range. The Listing records no decode
outcome (a failed decode and an unvisited byte are the same `Undefined` code unit),
so the arm is precisely a decode-failure detector: three bytes unlace cannot decode
are enough to conclude that a function whose body is `mov $7,%eax ; ret` never
returns, after which the flow layer deletes the live tail of every one of its
callers (GH-312). Dropping the arm is also what makes the data arm reachable for
the first time — `is_data` implies `!is_instruction_start`, so under the legacy
order the arm above consumed every site it would have caught. Measured over the 660
stripped x86-64 binaries and 110 stripped non-x86-64 binaries of the decbench
corpus on which the Listing is built, the two tallies conclude the *same* 581
callees no-return: the arm's entire marginal output there is decode-failure votes
that never reach the threshold on their own.

**Propagation fixpoint** (angr; `noreturn_propagate`,
`crates/unlace-analysis/src/analyzers/noreturn_propagate/mod.rs
(propagate_noreturn)`, the CFGFast returning-analysis idea): seed the terminal set
from the Known-flagged functions, then sweep the call graph to a fixpoint with
**no evidence threshold**. The base rule is a strict tail-call rule
(`function_is_no_return`), conservative by construction: a function is concluded
no-return only when its last *real* instruction — trailing NOP padding skipped,
closing exactly the blind spot above — is a CALL or tail JMP to a terminal-set
member, AND no RETURN exists in the body, AND no computed jump exists, AND every
static branch target stays inside the reachable body or is itself terminal. Each
conclusion joins the terminal set and re-enqueues callers, so a wrapper-of-a-wrapper
converges (sweeps bounded by candidate count + 2). This catches the canonical miss:
a cold wrapper like coreutils' `xalloc_die` — single-digit call sites, under the ≥3
threshold; `call abort` followed by padding, invisible to the evidence predicate —
which unconditionally cannot return. Without it, every caller grows a spurious
fall-through edge into the cold path that structures into an invalid
`while(true)`+`goto`.

A call through an import slot counts as a no-return call when the load-time
passes flagged the slot, and on x86 also when the slot is `TerminateProcess` and
the process handle is the current one (`terminates_current`): reading the
contiguous instructions before the call backward (at most four), the `-1`
pseudo-handle stored as the first argument (`push -1`, `mov dword [esp],-1`,
`or rcx,-1`, `mov rcx,-1`), or eax/rax stored as it (`push eax`, `mov
[esp],eax`, `mov rcx,rax`) after a `call [GetCurrentProcess]` with only constant
argument stores in between. The CRT's `__invoke_watson` and
`__report_gsfailure` end that way and keep a cookie check and a `ret` behind the
call, so the reachability rule concludes them
(`tests/stages/terminatecurrent.toml`).

On Go AMD64 ELF, `pclntab/gomcall.rs` independently identifies the
unique `runtime.mcall` name and entry address in pclntab and verifies that
the entry lies within the Listing's executable ranges. The saved goroutine
context can resume its caller. The propagation sweep skips that address
because its scheduler body reaches terminal handlers without a reachable
machine return. Existing terminal seeds, scheduler callback analysis, and
explicit callee and call-site overrides still apply.

An import stub is never a candidate (`import_stubs`, read from the same
`resolve_imports` stream the Known pass and the `error` recognizer use, keeping
only `ImportSymKind::Import` entries). A stub's body is the dynamic linker's
trampoline, not the import, so whether it returns belongs to the import: the
Known pass decides that by name at the stub address, and propagation draws
nothing from the body. MIPS is where the body misleads. A `.MIPS.stubs` lazy
stub is `lw $t9,-0x7ff0($gp); move $t7,$ra; jalr $t9; li $t8,<dynsym index>`;
the resolver jumps to the import, which returns to the caller through `$t7`, so
control never reaches the word after the stub. Before the stub tail-call rule
ended the walk at the resolver (see *MIPS lazy-binding imports*), the Listing modelled the
`jalr` as a returning call whose fall-through is the next stub's entry, and the
reachability rule below therefore concluded every stub laid out in front of a
Known no-return stub (`exit`, `abort`, `__stack_chk_fail`) no-return, then the
stub in front of that one, and so on. Ordinary imports such as `memcpy`,
`fopen64` and `pthread_once` then truncated every caller at the call.

The deferred analysis commit also seeds the Listing from function symbols already
marked no-return, including `option noreturn <name>` applied before `read symbols`.
These explicit facts must reach propagation before caller flow is constructed;
they do not depend on the known-name analyzer being enabled. A wrapper that calls
a marked leaf and then has unreachable INT3 bytes is handled by the reachability
rule below. Marking the leaf does not conclude a wrapper with a reachable return,
an unresolved jump, or an unmodelled escaping path. Without a known or explicit
no-return fact, a call followed by INT3 alone does not establish that its callee
cannot return. The existing `listing`, `noreturn_propagate`, and `noreturn_reach`
gates still control this inference.

A seed need not be a function: an import a `-fno-plt` build reaches only through
its `.got` slot is flagged at the slot's address (§1.3), and the call through it
names no target the Listing can see. `terminal_slot_calls` therefore decodes each
x86 `call [rip+disp32]` (x86-64) or `call [abs32]` (i386), `notrack` allowed, and
each AArch64 `blr xN` whose register an `adrp`/`ldr` pair at most four instructions
earlier loaded from the slot, whose static target is unknown, and a call whose slot
is a no-return seed ends its
path in both rules exactly as a call to a terminal function does, so a `die()`
ending in `exit()` through the GOT is concluded no-return as its PLT twin is.

Two rules fold into the same fixpoint, both Ghidra-derived:

- **The `error(nonzero,…)` value rule** (DIV-16, under `noreturn_known`): glibc `error()`
  and `error_at_line()` exit when `status != 0` but return for `status == 0`, so
  `error` can never be a Known name. The recognizer resolves the `error` entry
  addresses, then per call site backward-scans the straight-line predecessors for
  the defining write of the first integer-argument register (x86-64 SysV
  `EDI`/`RDI`): only a literal `MOV` of a nonzero constant accepts; `XOR EDI,EDI`,
  any non-constant definition, an intervening call or branch all reject — a false
  positive would delete live caller code. A qualifying *tail* call concludes the
  wrapper no-return (GNU `pfatal_with_name`), and independently *every* qualifying
  call site is emitted as a `no_fallthru_calls` fact that the drivers apply as a
  per-site CALL_RETURN flow override
  (`crates/unlace-cli/src/decompile_all.rs`) — the fall-through prune that
  stops the flow-follower from absorbing the next function.

  These scans read through a borrowed view of the existing Listing, bounded to
  `[function entry, next function entry)`, instead of copying each function's
  instructions into temporary collections. The strict call-site scan keeps its
  address-order predecessor rule: a gap between decoded instructions does not by
  itself stop the scan, but instructions from the preceding function are out of
  bounds. The reachability scan keeps the stricter straight-line rule from its
  former predecessor window: every step must have an explicit fall-through to
  the next instruction, so a gap breaks the argument proof. Both reject an
  intervening call, branch, or terminal instruction before accepting a constant.
- **CFG reachability** (`noreturn_reach`, DIV-19; the
  `targetOnlyCallsNoReturn` rule of Ghidra's discovered analyzer,
  `function_reaches_only_noreturn`): the tail rule is a subset — it cannot conclude
  a wrapper whose no-return call is mid-body with a dead tail after it (openssh
  `sshpkt_fatal`), whose RETURN is present but unreachable, or that routes through
  a switch whose every arm is no-return (`sshpkt_vfatal`). The generalization walks
  the instruction-level reachable graph from entry, treating a transfer to a
  terminal callee as ending its path, and concludes no-return iff no RETURN is
  reachable and at least one path ends at such a transfer. Every uncertainty — a
  reachable RETURN, an unresolved indirect jump, an escape to a possibly-returning
  neighbour, a call with no modelled fall-through — answers "returns". (ida) The
  one recorded over-conclusion and its fix: a GCC `-O2` hot/cold-split check
  (`jcc <.cold>` where the cold fragment is `call abort`) was short-circuited like
  an unconditional transfer, skipping the returning fall-through arm and marking
  the whole `quotearg_*` family no-return; a conditional jump now walks both arms,
  the returning shape IDA Pro and Ghidra both produce.
- **(unlace) DOS exits** (#1288; `propagate_exits`): on a real-mode raw or MZ
  image the fixpoint runs over the raw discovery's Listing seeded from the DOS
  exit interrupts (§1.6, *A DOS program exit ends the flow*) rather than the
  Known list; an exit site is a terminal call site to both rules, the way a
  qualifying `error(nonzero,…)` call is.

Finally, (angr) **flow-time extern matching** closes the case no address-keyed fact
can reach: in an ET_REL `.o`, a libc no-return is a UND symbol with no address and
no PLT, so nothing above ever marks it, and flow runs off the function's end into
alignment padding decoded as garbage `add [rax],al` statements. Under
`noreturn_known`,
`crates/unlace-lift/src/p2_lift/noreturn_externmatch.rs` applies
the same vendored name list and namespace guard *at the flow query seam*
(`crates/unlace-decomp/src/infra/decompile_drive.rs
(query_call_no_return)`); its sibling
`crates/unlace-lift/src/p2_lift/noreturnextern.rs` applies an
equivalent name match in the same query, differing in name-resolution path and
name set — it carries a frozen hard-coded copy of upstream's 21 names rather than
reading the shipped list, so neither unlace divergence block reaches it; it is
queried only after the vendored-list match has already declined. On a
normally-linked ELF the proto flag is already set, so both are no-ops there. These
two run inside the engine, not the analysis tier — chapter 02 owns the halt
mechanics they feed.

**The libstdc++ throw family (unlace, DIV-78).** Every `std::__throw_*` helper in
`<bits/functexcept.h>` (and `__throw_regex_error` in `<bits/regex_error.h>`) is
declared `__attribute__((__noreturn__))` and every body ends in
`_GLIBCXX_THROW_OR_ABORT` — a `throw`, or `abort()` when the library is built
`-fno-exceptions` — so none of them can return. Upstream Ghidra's list names
`__cxa_throw` and the terminate entry points but omits this whole family, and the
attribute is a compile-time fact that survives into no binary artifact: at the
decompiler's boundary `std::__throw_length_error` is an ordinary undefined
`.dynsym` import reached through a PLT stub. Nothing but the shipped list can prove
the call cannot return, so without the entries the fall-through is followed and the
code after every such call — most often clang's `call __stack_chk_fail`
unreachable-trap, or the next function's entry — is emitted as if it ran. The
family is on the list twice over, because the two matchers see two different
spellings of the same symbol: the analysis-tier scan matches the **mangled**
`.dynsym` name *before* demangling, written as a trailing-`*` wildcard over the
Itanium `ZSt<len>__throw_<name>` prefix so a signature change (`__throw_ios_failure`
gained a `const char*, int` overload in GCC 7) cannot age the entry out; the
flow-time matcher sees the **demangled** display name, which the `std`-only
namespace guard admits and the leading-underscore strip reduces to
`throw_length_error`. A same-named method on a user class stays out by the
namespace guard, and the mangled prefixes are exact ABI encodings of
`std::__throw_*`, so neither spelling can reach an unrelated symbol.

## 1.8 In-engine image binding

Inside the engine, P1 is the architecture/loader binding —
`crates/unlace-lift/src/p1_partition` — three front-ends over one base,
the C++ inheritance chain modeled by composition:

- `crates/unlace-lift/src/p1_partition/sleigh_arch.rs
  (SleighArchitecture)` is the base every path shares: resolve a language id
  against the `.ldefs` records scanned from the spec roots (the C++ file-level
  statics become an explicit `LanguageDatabase` value the bootstrap owns), find the
  `.pspec`/`.cspec`/`.sla` files, build the SLEIGH translator, and run the
  `Architecture::init` tail (type factory, prototype models, print language). The
  upstream translator-reuse cache is deliberately not ported — it affects build
  speed only — and is the recorded loss here. (unlace) A spec root is a
  directory or a tree held in memory
  (`crates/unlace-lift/src/p1_partition/memoryspecs.rs
  (MemorySpecs)`): a table of `/`-separated relative paths and their contents.
  The table need not follow Ghidra's layout; one language's `.ldefs`, `.sla`,
  `.pspec` and `.cspec`, flat, form a complete root. The database mounts each
  table under an internal `unlace-memory://<n>` root and answers every listing,
  lookup and read under it from the table alone, never from the filesystem.
  (unlace) A bootstrap over spec roots reads only the `.ldefs` its language
  needs (`LanguageDatabase::load_language`): it lists the `.ldefs` under the
  roots, reads the files named for the id's processor field first
  (`x86.ldefs` for `x86:LE:64:default`), then the rest in spec-path order,
  and stops at the first that defines the id; the C++ parses every `.ldefs`
  on each load. `crates/unlace-console/src/engine.rs (language_database)`
  scans a list of roots once, reading every `.ldefs`. A bootstrap over the
  result skips the `.ldefs` scan and reads only its own language's `.sla`,
  `.pspec` and `.cspec` (`LanguageDatabase::read_spec`), so threads may share
  one database.
- `crates/unlace-lift/src/p1_partition/xml_arch.rs (XmlArchitecture)`
  binds the decompiler's XML `<binaryimage>` container — the datatest corpus's
  entire load path, and the reason the analysis tier can be default-on without
  touching parity: this front-end never sees an `ObjectLoadImage`.
- `crates/unlace-lift/src/p1_partition/raw_arch.rs
  (RawBinaryArchitecture)` is the catch-all leaf for a raw byte image: its file
  match always succeeds (so capability sorting pushes it last), the language must
  be supplied by the target, and the loader is a plain offset-mapped
  `RawLoadImage`. The live CLI reaches it only through `--raw-image`, with an
  explicit target, base, and one or more numeric entry seeds. It resolves and
  initializes the language first, attaches the default code space, and only then
  applies the VMA. This order gives nonzero bases defined word-addressed behavior.
  Base and entry values arrive in code-space address units and are checked before
